404	All of these give the keyboard back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away. <kbd>Tab</kbd> ends your typing. It doesn't move to the next field unless Full Keyboard Access is on. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).
405	
406	- A number past the field's range is held to the end of the range.
407	- Text that isn't a number changes nothing, and the field goes back to the value it had. Decimals take a full stop, whatever your Mac's region.
408	- An unchanged value isn't an edit, so clicking into a field and leaving makes no undo step.
409	
410	Three other kinds of field work a little differently:
411	
412	| Field | How it behaves |
413	| --- | --- |
414	| One-line text, such as a clip's name | Takes the whole width of its row, and long text scrolls inside it. <kbd>↩</kbd>, <kbd>Tab</kbd> or a click elsewhere applies it. |
415	| Timecode, such as **In** and **Out** in the Clip tab's [Timing section](/editing/timing-section/) | Takes a time such as `1:23`, `83.5` or `1:23:04`. A time Frame Job can't read beeps and the field goes back. Unlike a number field, it has no range of its own. The clip's rules decide what it can take, and a time they [won't allow](/getting-started/refused-edits/) beeps. |
416	| Multi-line text, such as the Text tab's **Content** | <kbd>↩</kbd> applies and <kbd>⇧↩</kbd> starts a new line. See [Multi-line fields](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/#multi-line-fields). |
417	
418	A greyed control is dimmed and takes no clicks. It usually depends on something else in its section, such as a shadow's **Blur** waiting for **Drop shadow** to be on.
419	
420	## Use a quick pick
421	
422	A field with common values has a chevron at its right. Click the chevron for a menu of those values, each spelled as the field shows it at rest, with a checkmark on the current one. The Shadow section's **Opacity**, for example, offers `0%`, `25%`, `50%`, `75%` and `100%`.
423	
424	Anything you were typing in the field is applied before the menu opens. A value past the field's range is held to the end of the range, as a typed one is. Picking the value the field already holds changes nothing and makes no undo step.
425	
426	## Drag a slider
427	
428	Click a slider to jump to that value, or drag to follow the pointer. The preview follows as you go, and the whole press, from mouse-down to mouse-up, is one undo step. A press that never changes the value makes no step.
429	
430	A slider and its field show the same value, but the field can reach further. **Volume**'s slider stops at 400%, for example, while its field goes higher. A value past the slider's end pins the knob at the end of the rail.
431	
432	On a row the selected action changes, a slider also shows where the value starts. A tick marks the value at the playhead when it isn't where the knob is. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
433	
434	## Choose a colour
435	
436	Click a colour swatch to open the macOS colour panel. The panel has an opacity control, and the value follows it live, so a drag in the panel changes the picture as you go. A colour you can see through shows a checkerboard in its swatch.
437	
438	The panel edits the swatch you clicked last. Click another swatch to move it there.
439	
440	## Edit several clips at once
441	
442	With several clips selected, the inspector shows the first clip's values. A row whose clips disagree adds a small **mixed** badge beside its control, and resting the pointer on it reads "The selected clips have different values".
443	
444	The control stays live. An edit gives every selected clip the same value, as one undo step, and the badge goes.
445	
446	A row writes only to the clips it applies to. With a video clip and a text clip selected, a text setting changes the text clip and leaves the video clip alone.
447	
448	The [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) works the same way.
449	
450	## Reset a section
451	
452	A **Reset** button appears on a section's header only while that section differs from its default. Click it to put the whole section back, as one undo step. Clicking the button doesn't fold the section, though a click anywhere else on the header does.
453	
454	Not every section has one. While you're editing an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/), a section the action can animate hides Reset, and the same place shows **Clear** while the action changes something in that section. A section no action can animate keeps its Reset.
455	
456	## Right-click a row
457	
458	Right-click a row's label, slider or checkbox, or the space beside them, for the items that apply to that row. A number field or a pop-up keeps its own right-click and doesn't open this menu.
459	
460	| Item | When it shows | What it does |
461	| --- | --- | --- |
462	| **Remove from action N** | The selected action changes this row | Takes the row out of that action |
463	| **Go to action M** | Another action changes this row | Selects that action |
464	| **Reset to default** | The row has a default | Puts the row back to its default |
465	| **Set end value to default** | Takes the place of **Reset to default** while an action is selected, on a row that animates | Sets the row's value at the action's end to the default |
466	
467	The last two are greyed while the row already holds its default. A row with nothing to offer has no menu.
468	
469	What the marks in a row's left gutter mean is on [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/). An agent sets an action's end values with `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
470	
471	## Related

478	---
479	title: "The inspector"
480	description: "Find your way around the inspector's five tabs, the Clip tab's sub-tabs and its folding sections."
481	---
482	
483	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
484	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
485	
486	The inspector is the panel at the right of the editor window. It's where you read and change the numbers behind what you see: the selected clips, the project's media, the project itself, its words and the Assistant. This page covers how it's laid out. [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/) covers how its controls behave.
487	
488	<AtAGlance
489	  menu={['View ▸ Hide Inspector', 'View ▸ Transcript', 'View ▸ Assistant']}
490	  keys={['⌥⌘I', '⌃⌘T', '⌃⌘A']}
491	  where="The editor window, middle right"
492	  tools="set_clip"
493	/>
494	
495	<Shot
496	  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
497	  alt="The inspector on the Clip tab with a video clip selected. At the top is the clip's name, speech.mov, over the line video · 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 fps. Under it are the action lane, reading no actions, and the sub-tabs Picture, Color, Sound and Clip, with Picture active. Below them the Transform section is open, showing Scale, Position, Rotation, Opacity and Blend."
498	/>
499	
500	## The five tabs
501	
502	| Tab | What it's for |
503	| --- | --- |
504	| **Clip** | The selected clips. With nothing selected it reads "Select a clip to edit its properties." |
505	| **Media** | Every file in the project. See [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). |
506	| **Document** | The project as a whole. See [The Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). |
507	| **Transcript** | The timeline's words. **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>) goes straight there. See [The Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/). |
508	| **Assistant** | A conversation that edits this project. **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) goes straight there. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/). |
509	
510	## The Clip tab's pinned block
511	
512	With a clip selected, three things stay pinned at the top of the Clip tab while its sections scroll underneath: the selection header, the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and the sub-tabs.
513	
514	The selection header shows:
515	
516	- **A chip** coloured by the clip's kind. It's neutral when the selected kinds have different colours.
517	- **The name.** With one clip selected this is a field. Type to give the clip its own name, which is one undo step, "Rename Clip". Empty the field to go back to what the clip shows by default. This is the only control that clears a clip's name.
518	- **A line of facts.** The kind, the duration in the project's timecode, the source's pixel size and the source's own frame rate, for example `video · 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 fps`. A clip with no source shows only the facts it has.
519	- **A colour dot** at the end of the name line, for a clip's [colour label](/timeline/names-and-labels/). With several clips selected it shows only when they all share the label.
520	
521	With several clips selected, the header reads "3 clips selected" and gives their total duration. Renaming here needs a single clip.
522	
523	## Sub-tabs
524	
525	The strip under the action lane splits the Clip tab into **Text**, **Shape**, **Graphic**, **Picture**, **Color**, **Sound** and **Clip**. It shows only what the selection can use, and sections that don't apply are absent, not greyed out.
526	
527	| Selected | Sub-tabs |
528	| --- | --- |
529	| A movie | Picture, Color, Sound, Clip |
530	| A picture | Picture, Color, Clip |
531	| A text clip | Text, Picture, Clip |
532	| A shape | Shape, Picture, Clip |
533	| A graphic | Graphic, Picture, Clip |
534	| A nest | Picture, Clip, with Sound before Clip when something inside can make a sound |
535	| An audio-only clip | Sound, Clip |
536	| An adjustment clip | Color, Clip |
537	
538	With a mixed selection, the rules are these:
539	
540	- **Text**, **Shape** and **Graphic** appear only when every selected clip is that kind.
541	- **Picture** appears when a selected clip draws, unless an adjustment clip is in the selection.
542	- **Color** appears when a selected clip draws and none of them is text, a shape, a graphic or a nest. An audio-only clip on its own doesn't get it.
543	- **Sound** appears when a selected clip has sound.
544	- **Clip** is always there, last.
545	
546	A sub-tab you pick stays active while the selection doesn't change. A new selection starts on the first tab it has, so a text clip starts on **Text** and a shape on **Shape**.
547	
548	While an action is selected, a sub-tab it changes shows a mark such as `◆2` after its label, counting what the action sets there. See [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/).
549	
550	## Selection follows to the Clip tab
551	
552	Clicking a clip on the timeline or the canvas moves the inspector to the **Clip** tab, even if the clip was already selected. A selection that changes any other way, such as a paste, <kbd>⌘A</kbd> or an agent, moves it only from **Media** or **Document**.
553	
554	Two tabs hold their ground:
555	
556	- **Transcript** stays when you click a clip, and scrolls to that clip's first word.
557	- **Assistant** isn't pulled away when the selection changes without a click, so the Assistant's own edits don't take you off the conversation.
558	
559	Clearing the selection moves no tab.
560	
561	## Fold a section
562	
563	Click a section's header to fold it. A folded header keeps a one-line summary of what's inside, such as `100%` for Transform or `2 filters` for Filters, so you can read a value without opening it. The fold is remembered per section, in every window and between launches.
564	
565	The summary's colour tells you about the section:
566	
567	| Summary colour | What it means |
568	| --- | --- |
569	| The action colour | The selected action sets something in this section |
570	| Body text | The section differs from its default |
571	| Faint | The section is at its default |
572	
573	On the Clip tab, a section you've never clicked starts closed, except Transform, a text clip's Content, a shape's Shape and a graphic's Properties. Every Media and Document section starts open.
574	
575	If every section on a Clip sub-tab would be shut, the first one you haven't folded yourself opens by default. A section you closed yourself stays closed.
576	
577	Inside an action, a section the action sets shows `◆1` or a higher count in its header and opens by itself, without changing what's remembered. A faint ⊘ marks a section actions don't animate. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
578	
579	Folding animates, unless **Reduce Motion** is on in macOS.
580	
581	## Hide or show the inspector
582	
583	Choose **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (<kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd>) and the preview takes its space. The item then reads **View ▸ Show Inspector**. The inspector is shown by default, and your choice is remembered between launches.
584	
585	This menu item is the only way to hide it. Dragging the divider to the edge stops at the inspector's smallest width.
586	
587	**View ▸ Transcript** and **View ▸ Assistant** bring it back if it's hidden.
588

595	=================== getting-started/keys-and-typing.mdx
596	---
597	title: Keys and typing
598	description: How Frame Job's single-letter keys share the keyboard with text fields, what gives the keys back to the editor, and what Esc leaves.
599	---
600	
601	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
602	
603	Frame Job plays on <kbd>Space</kbd> and trims on <kbd>W</kbd>, so a letter means one thing on the timeline and another in a text field. The rule is short: the keys belong to the editor unless you're typing or a sheet is open.
604	
605	<AtAGlance
606	  keys={['Space', '↩', 'Tab', '⎋']}
607	  where={['The editor window', 'The Preview Window']}
608	/>
609	
610	This page explains how the keys are shared. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) has the full list.
611	
612	## Single-letter keys
613	
614	These keys need no modifier and act on the editor window. They also work in the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).
615	
616	| Key | What it does |
617	| --- | --- |
618	| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play or pause |
619	| <kbd>J</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> <kbd>L</kbd> | Play in reverse, pause, play forward |
620	| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Back or forward one frame, ten with <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
621	| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Previous or next edit point |
622	| <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | Start or end of the project |
623	| <kbd>,</kbd> <kbd>.</kbd> | Nudge the selected clips one frame earlier or later, ten with <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
624	| <kbd>I</kbd> <kbd>O</kbd> | Set In, Set Out |
625	| <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>E</kbd> | Trim the start or end to the playhead |
626	| <kbd>M</kbd> | Add Marker |
627	| <kbd>T</kbd> | Add a text clip at the playhead |
628	| <kbd>C</kbd> | Crop mode on or off |
629	| <kbd>Z</kbd> | Region mode for [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) |
630	| <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> | Fit Timeline |
631	| <kbd>N</kbd> | Snapping on or off |
632	| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Deselect the selected action |
633	
634	<kbd>⇧</kbd> and Caps Lock still count as no modifier, so Caps Lock doesn't stop these keys. <kbd>⌘</kbd>, <kbd>⌥</kbd> and <kbd>⌃</kbd> always make it a different key.
635	
636	The single-letter keys never fire while you're typing. While a sheet is open none of them works, in either window, so the project can't change underneath the sheet. In the Preview Window they also do nothing while a field in the editor window is still being typed in.
637	
638	Some menu items have a single-letter key the menu doesn't show. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) gives those too.
639	
640	### When the focus changes a key
641	
642	A few places claim keys for themselves while they hold the focus:
643	
644	| Where the focus is | What changes |
645	| --- | --- |
646	| The preview canvas | Hold <kbd>Space</kbd> and drag to pan a zoomed canvas. A tap of <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays and pauses. |
647	| The Transcript tab's text | The arrow keys select words. See [Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/). |
648	| A selected point on a [curve](/color/curves/) | The arrow keys move the point, <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes it and <kbd>⎋</kbd> deselects it. |
649	| A button, with macOS Full Keyboard Access on | <kbd>Space</kbd> presses the button. |
650	
651	Everywhere else in the window, <kbd>Space</kbd> plays and pauses.
652	
653	## Menu shortcuts
654	
655	Every shortcut with <kbd>⌘</kbd> belongs to a menu item, so it does exactly what the item does. While the item is greyed out, the shortcut does nothing. That includes every editor command while a sheet is open.
656	
657	## Start and finish typing
658	
659	A field takes the keys only when you click in it, or choose a command that opens one for typing, such as **Clip ▸ Rename…** or **View ▸ Assistant**. Nothing else moves the keyboard into a field, so you won't type into one by accident.
660	
661	Any of these applies what you typed and gives the keys back, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away:
662	
663	| Do this | Where it works |
664	| --- | --- |
665	| Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | A one-line field. Multi-line fields have [their own rule](#multi-line-fields). |
666	| Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>⇧Tab</kbd> | Any text, including the Assistant's message field |
667	| Click outside the field | Anywhere in the window. The click still does what it would have done, after the field lets go. |
668	
669	<kbd>Tab</kbd> doesn't step through fields. With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, it does, and walks to the next control instead.
670	
671	A click on the title bar doesn't end your typing. Neither does a click on the field's own margins or on a text view's scroller, because they count as part of the field. A click on a field's [quick-pick chevron](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#use-a-quick-pick) applies what you typed, then opens its menu.
672	
673	While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> and <kbd>Tab</kbd> belong to it.
674	
675	## Delete keys while you type
676	
677	These four keys act on the timeline when you're not typing. In a text field their menu items switch off, so the keys keep their usual text meaning and a slip of the finger can't delete a clip.
678	
679	| Key | On the timeline |
680	| --- | --- |
681	| <kbd>⌫</kbd> | **Delete** |
682	| <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | **Ripple Delete** |
683	| <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> | **Open Nest** |
684	| <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> | **Close Nest** |
685	
686	## Multi-line fields
687	
688	Four places take more than one line: the Text tab's **Content**, a graphic's multi-line text setting, the Assistant's message field and text you're [editing on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).
689	
690	| Key | What it does |
691	| --- | --- |
692	| <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | Applies the text. In the Assistant's message field it sends the message, and beeps if the Assistant is busy. |
693	| <kbd>↩</kbd> with any of <kbd>⇧</kbd>, <kbd>⌘</kbd>, <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌃</kbd> | Starts a new line |
694	
695	On the canvas, <kbd>⎋</kbd> stops editing. If the text changed, Frame Job asks whether to **Apply**, **Revert** or **Cancel**.
696	
697	While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> belongs to it.
698	
699	## Keys in a sheet
700	
701	In a sheet, <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the main button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> presses **Cancel**. The [single-letter keys](#single-letter-keys) stay off until the sheet closes.
702	
703	## What Esc leaves
704	
705	<kbd>⎋</kbd> backs out of whatever is under way.
706	
707	| What's under way | What <kbd>⎋</kbd> does |
708	| --- | --- |
709	| A canvas drag: move, scale, rotate, crop, a line's endpoint or an obscure region | Puts everything back as it was before you pressed, with no undo step |
710	| Crop mode | Leaves it, as <kbd>↩</kbd> does, while the preview canvas holds the focus. <kbd>C</kbd> leaves it from anywhere. |
711	| Region mode, from <kbd>Z</kbd> or the Obscure section's **Place on Canvas** | Leaves it |
712	| The key-colour or qualifier eyedropper | Cancels it |
713	| A selected curve point in the Color tab | Deselects it |
714	| A selected action | Deselects it, so the Clip tab shows the clip's own values again |
715	| Typing in a number field | Throws the typing away |
716	| A rename field on the timeline | Closes it and keeps the old name |
717	| A selection in the Transcript tab | Clears it |
718	
719	Region mode also ends by itself when the selection stops being the clip it started for, or the playhead leaves that clip.
720	
721	A canvas tool that waits for your click or drag shows a crosshair and a hint on the canvas, and only one can wait at a time. The hint says what to do:
722	
723	- "Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel"
724	- "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel"
725	- "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel"
726	- "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel"
727	
728	## Related
729	
730	- [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/)
731	- [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/)
732	- [Gestures with no menu item](/reference/gestures/)
733	=================== getting-started/refused-edits.mdx
734	---
735	title: When an edit is refused
736	description: How Frame Job tells you it won't make an edit, from the Refused strip in the inspector to a beep with no message, and why nothing changes.
737	---
738	
739	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
740	
741	Frame Job has rules that keep a project sound, such as how far two clips may overlap. When an edit would break one, nothing changes and Frame Job says so. How it says so tells you what happened.
742	
743	<AtAGlance
744	  where={['The foot of the inspector', 'The timeline, for a drop']}
745	/>
746	
747	| What you see | What happened |
748	| --- | --- |
749	| A beep and a **Refused:** line at the foot of the inspector | A rule wouldn't allow the edit |
750	| A clip animates back to the last place it was allowed | The rules wouldn't allow the drop |
751	| A beep and no message | The edit would have changed nothing |
752	| An error alert | Frame Job couldn't use the request at all |
753	
754	Only a drop can still move the clip, to the last allowed place on its way. None of the others changes the project or makes an undo step.
755	
756	## The refusal strip
757	
758	When a rule won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps and shows the rule's own sentence at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused: ":
759	
760	> Refused: track 3 is locked, so the gap on it cannot be closed
761	
762	The strip shows up to three lines. Rest the pointer on it to read the whole sentence.
763	
764	It stays until you click it or the project changes, which means an edit, an undo or redo, or going into or out of a nest. Moving the playhead or changing the selection doesn't clear it, so you can look around while you work out what to do.
765	
766	The sentence is exact rather than friendly. It can name clips and tracks by Frame Job's own numbers, which aren't their positions on the timeline, and give lengths in the timeline's smallest units rather than in seconds.
767	
768	Each feature's page lists what can stop it, and [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/) gathers them in one place.
769	
770	A typed Start, Length or end value on an action shows the strip too. Dragging an action's band never does. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
771	
772	## A drop that springs back
773	
774	While you drag, positions the rules don't allow are skipped and the clip waits at the last allowed one. A clip dropped on one of those positions animates back to that place and stays there, as one undo step. If the drag never reached an allowed place, it animates back to where it started and nothing changes. See [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/).
775	
776	## A beep with no message
777	
778	An edit that would change nothing beeps but shows no message, because no rule was broken. A slip does this when the clip is already at the end of its footage, and **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** does it on clips that already have the copied look.
779	
780	## An error alert
781	
782	Now and then Frame Job can't use a request at all, such as a value outside its allowed range. It shows an error alert naming the offending value. You'll rarely meet one, because the inspector's number fields already [hold what you type to their range](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#type-a-value).
783	
784	## With an agent
785	
786	An agent is told the same things in words. An edit a rule won't allow fails with the rule's sentence, and an edit that changes nothing fails saying so. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
787

794	---
795	title: "Requirements and install"
796	description: "What your Mac needs to run Frame Job, where to download it, and what happens the first time you open it."
797	---
798	
799	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
800	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
801	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
802	
803	Frame Job runs on an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 26 or later. There's no account to make, and you can start cutting as soon as it's in your Applications folder.
804	
805	<AtAGlance
806	  needs={['An Apple Silicon Mac', 'macOS 26 or later']}
807	/>
808	
809	## What Frame Job needs
810	
811	| You need | Details |
812	| --- | --- |
813	| An Apple Silicon Mac | Frame Job is built for Apple Silicon alone, so an Intel Mac can't run it. |
814	| macOS 26 or later | 26.0 is the oldest system it opens on. |
815	| An account | None. There's nothing to sign up for. |
816	| An API key | None to edit. Only the Assistant and cloud transcription need one, and each runs on [your own key](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/). Everything else works without a key. |
817	
818	:::note
819	M1 and M2 Macs have no AV1 decoder. They can export [AV1](/export/av1-and-vp9/), but Frame Job won't import an AV1 file on them. The rest of the editor isn't affected.
820	:::
821	
822	## Download and install
823	
824	<Steps>
825	
826	1. Download the newest build: [FrameJob.dmg](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/releases/latest/download/FrameJob.dmg). This link always gives you the latest release.
827	
828	2. Open the DMG.
829	
830	3. Drag Frame Job to Applications.
831	
832	</Steps>
833	
834	The download is signed and notarized, and it can [update itself](/getting-started/updates/).
835	
836	A copy you build yourself has no updater. To build one, see [Developing Frame Job](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/blob/main/docs/developing.md).
837	
838	## First launch
839	
840	Frame Job asks you for nothing the first time it opens: no account, no key and no system permission. As with any app downloaded from the internet, macOS may ask you to confirm that you want to open it.
841	
842	With nothing to open, it shows the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/), with **Open Video…**, **New Project**, **New Recording…** and your recent projects.
843	
844	<Shot
845	  name="01-welcome.window"
846	  alt="The Welcome window: the Frame Job mark and name, the line Open a file. Start cutting., the buttons Open Video…, New Project and New Recording…, and a line of the file types it opens."
847	/>
848	
849	Three things come later, and only when you get to them:
850	
851	- **System permissions.** Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera and Input Monitoring come up only when you press **Record** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), and only for what that recording uses. Frame Job never asks at launch. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
852	- **Automatic updates.** The second time you open the downloaded copy, it asks whether to check for updates automatically. See [Updates](/getting-started/updates/).
853	- **API keys.** They're optional, and you set them in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>), which works with no project open. See [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).
854

861	=================== getting-started/undo-and-saving.mdx
862	---
863	title: Undo and saving
864	description: What one undo step is, how the Edit menu names it, what makes no step, and how Autosave keeps your work.
865	---
866	
867	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
868	
869	Every change to a project is a step you can take back. Once a project has been saved, Frame Job also writes your work to disk as you go, so you can try things without worrying about losing it.
870	
871	<AtAGlance
872	  menu={['Edit ▸ Undo', 'Edit ▸ Redo']}
873	  keys={['⌘Z', '⇧⌘Z']}
874	  tools={['undo', 'redo']}
875	/>
876	
877	## Undo and redo
878	
879	**Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) and **Edit ▸ Redo** (<kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>) walk back and forward one step at a time.
880	
881	A new edit clears the redo history, so anything you undid and didn't redo is gone. Each project keeps its last 32 steps.
882	
883	## What counts as one step
884	
885	One step is one thing you did, however many clips it touched.
886	
887	| What you did | How much it counts for |
888	| --- | --- |
889	| A menu command or key | One step, even when it changes many clips. Ripple Delete over a range, Un-nest of several nests, Detach Audio on a selection and a Remove Silences pass are each one. |
890	| A gesture | One step from mouse-down to mouse-up, however long the drag lasts: a move, trim, rate stretch, slip, roll or duplicate-drag. |
891	| An inspector edit | One step for a typed value or a slider press, even with several clips selected. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/). |
892	| A flip of a track's switch, a track rename or a track reorder | Each one is its own step. |
893	
894	## How steps are named
895	
896	The Edit menu names the step it will take back, such as **Undo Move Clips**, and Redo is named the same way. Check the name before you press if you're not sure what you're about to undo.
897	
898	| For | The names you'll see include |
899	| --- | --- |
900	| Clips | Move Clips, Rename Clip, Label Clip |
901	| Tracks | Hide Track, Mute Track, Lock Track, Solo Track, Track Matte, Track Volume, Track Pan, Reset Track Mix, Rename Track, Reorder Track, New Track, Remove Track, Remove Empty Tracks |
902	| Markers | Add Marker, Move Marker, Rename Marker, Chapter Marker, Remove Marker |
903	
904	## What makes no step
905	
906	Anything that doesn't change the project makes no step, so <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> walks straight past it:
907	
908	- Selecting, including a click on a clip that doesn't move it.
909	- Moving the playhead.
910	- Setting the in/out range.
911	- Going into or out of a nest.
912	- An edit Frame Job [wouldn't make](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
913	- An edit that would leave everything as it was.
914	
915	<kbd>⌘Z</kbd> in the Assistant's message field undoes your typing there and never touches the project's steps. Sending the message drops that typing history.
916	
917	## How Autosave keeps your work
918	
919	Once a project has been saved, it autosaves in place as you work, the macOS way. An untitled project has no place of its own on disk until its first Save, so save early. See [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/) for saving, reverting and browsing earlier versions.
920	
921	The word "edited" in the title bar means changes haven't reached the disk yet. It clears after every silent autosave, and the window's close button never shows a dot.
922	
923	Each save writes the new project beside the old one and swaps it in, so a crash part-way through can't leave you with half a project. See [Crash-safe writes](/projects/save-and-revert/#crash-safe-writes).
924	
925	## With an agent
926	
927	Each agent tool call that edits the project is exactly one step, so one `undo` takes back one call. `undo` and `redo` take no arguments. `undo` reports the name of the step it took back, and it's an error when there's nothing to undo. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).
928	
929	## Related
930	
931	- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
932	- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
933	- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)
934	=================== getting-started/updates.mdx
935	---
936	title: Updates
937	description: Check for a newer Frame Job, choose whether it checks by itself, and see which copies update themselves.
938	---
939	
940	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
941	
942	The copy of Frame Job you download keeps itself up to date. It tells you when a new version is ready and installs it when you say so.
943	
944	<AtAGlance
945	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…"
946	  needs="The copy downloaded from the project's GitHub Releases page."
947	/>
948	
949	## Which copy updates itself
950	
951	The copy you download from the project's GitHub Releases page updates itself, with [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org). A copy built from source has no updater: it has no menu item and it never checks.
952	
953	An update is always the whole app. Release notes are on the release's page on GitHub.
954	
955	## Check for updates
956	
957	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…**, directly under **About Frame Job**. It has no shortcut.
958	
959	If a newer Frame Job has been published, a window shows its version. Choose **Install Update** to download it, then **Install and Relaunch** to replace the app and relaunch it. If there's nothing newer, it says you're up to date, and its **Version History** button opens the release's page.
960	
961	The item is greyed while a check is already running. No agent tool checks for updates or installs them.
962	
963	## Automatic checks
964	
965	The second time you open Frame Job, it asks whether to check for updates automatically. If you agree, it checks about once a day while it's open and tells you when an update is ready. It installs one only when you say so, unless you tick **Automatically download and install updates** in that prompt, or the matching box in the update window.
966	
967	Frame Job [remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/) your answer and when it last checked.
968	
969	## Turn automatic checks off
970	
971	There's no Settings control for this. With Frame Job closed, run this in Terminal:
972	
973	```sh
974	defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob SUEnableAutomaticChecks -bool NO
975	```
976	
977	**Check for Updates…** still works afterwards.
978	
979	## Signed updates
980	
981	Every update carries an EdDSA signature, and Frame Job won't install one whose signature doesn't match the key built into the app. Only a release published from the project itself can be installed.
982	
983	## Related

2	---
3	title: "Canvas background and timecode"
4	description: "Set the colour behind every layer, make the canvas transparent, choose how times are shown, and decide how new clips are sized."
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The **Appearance** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) sets three things for the whole project: the colour behind your clips, how times are written, and how big a new clip starts.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Appearance" tools={['set_canvas', 'add_clip']} />
12	
13	| Control | What it does | Default |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| **Background** | The colour behind every layer. | Black, opaque |
16	| **Timecode** | How the project shows a time. | Frames |
17	| **Fit new clips to canvas** | Scales down a new clip that's bigger than the canvas. | On |
18	
19	A change to **Timecode** or **Fit new clips to canvas** is one undo step.
20	
21	## Set the background colour
22	
23	Click the **Background** swatch and pick a colour in the Colors panel. The colour sits behind every layer, so it shows wherever no clip covers the canvas.
24	
25	To put a colour on the timeline as a clip instead, see [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
26	
27	## Make the background transparent
28	
29	Lower the opacity in the Colors panel. The swatch shows a checkerboard behind the colour, and the **Background** row of the [Document summary](/projects/document-tab/#the-document-summary) reads `Transparent`, or the colour with its opacity.
30	
31	Most export formats can't carry transparency, so while the background isn't fully opaque, the section adds a note about the formats that can.
32	
33	| The note says | When |
34	| --- | --- |
35	| "Transparent — kept by 4 export formats." | Three or more formats keep it, so the note counts them. They're HEVC with Alpha (MOV), VP9 with Alpha (WebM), ProRes 4444 (MOV) and Animated PNG. |
36	| "Transparent — needs an alpha format." | Frame Job can't name the formats yet, which can happen on a project with nothing on the timeline. |
37	
38	See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).
39	
40	## Choose a timecode format
41	
42	**Timecode** sets how times are written everywhere the project shows one, including the toolbar, the ruler, the inspector, markers and the transcript.
43	
44	| Choice | Looks like |
45	| --- | --- |
46	| **Frames** | `HH:MM:SS:FF` |
47	| **Milliseconds** | `HH:MM:SS.mmm` |
48	
49	**Frames** doesn't drop frames, so at 29.97 fps the count runs slightly behind the clock over a long timeline.
50	
51	## Fit new clips to canvas
52	
53	This decides how big a new clip starts. It's on by default.
54	
55	| Setting | A clip bigger than the canvas | Any other clip |
56	| --- | --- | --- |
57	| On | Starts at Fit scale: scaled down until all of it shows. | Starts at 100 %, its native size. |
58	| Off | Starts at 100 %, so it runs past the edges of the canvas. | Starts at 100 %. |
59	
60	A clip counts as bigger when either its width or its height is larger than the canvas. Fit never scales a clip up, and changing the setting leaves clips already on the timeline as they are. To fit or fill one clip, see [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/).
61	
62	## Reset the section
63	
64	**Reset** on the **Appearance** header puts all three back to their defaults: opaque black, **Frames** and on. It's offered only while one of them differs, and it's one undo step.
65	
66	## With an agent
67	
68	`set_canvas` sets all three, and anything it doesn't name keeps its value.
69	
70	| Argument | What it takes |
71	| --- | --- |
72	| `background` | Four numbers from 0 to 1, `[r, g, b, a]`. Three numbers, or one outside the range, fails and nothing changes. |
73	| `timecode_frames` | `true` for **Frames**, `false` for **Milliseconds**. |
74	| `fit_new_clips` | `true` or `false`, as the checkbox. |
75	
76	`add_clip` follows **Fit new clips to canvas** as the app does. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
77

85	=================== projects/canvas-size.mdx
86	---
87	title: "Canvas size"
88	description: "Set the project's frame from a preset, a source file or typed numbers, and choose whether your clips scale along with it."
89	---
90	
91	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
92	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
93	
94	The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is composited into, and every export starts from its size. Change it when the whole video should be a different shape.
95	
96	<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Canvas" tools="set_canvas" />
97	
98	A new project starts at 1920 × 1080. A project opened from a movie or a picture takes that file's size, and one opened from a sound file starts at 1920 × 1080.
99	
100	## Pick a preset
101	
102	<Steps>
103	
104	1. Open the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).
105	
106	2. Tick **Resize clips proportionally** if you want your layout to [follow the new size](#resize-your-clips-with-the-canvas).
107	
108	3. In the **Canvas** section, choose a size from **Preset**.
109	
110	</Steps>
111	
112	The list runs in this order:
113	
114	- **1080p · 1920 × 1080**
115	- **4K · 3840 × 2160**
116	- **720p · 1280 × 720**
117	- **Vertical · 1080 × 1920**
118	- **Square · 1080 × 1080**
119	- **1440p · 2560 × 1440**
120	- **Source Size**, which [matches a file](#match-a-source-file)
121	- **Custom**, which the popup shows when the size matches none of these. Choosing it beeps and changes nothing, so [type the size](#type-a-size) instead.
122	
123	Each change is one undo step.
124	
125	## Match a source file
126	
127	Choose **Source Size** in **Preset** to set the canvas to the size of the first media file that has a picture size. It beeps when no file in the project has one, as in a project of sound files only.
128	
129	A file with an odd width or height can't be used. Choosing it puts up the same alert as [typing an odd number](#type-a-size), and the size stays as it was.
130	
131	## Type a size
132	
133	Type into **Width** and **Height**, in pixels. **Preset** then reads **Custom**, unless the size happens to match a preset or the first media file that has a picture size.
134	
135	- Both numbers must be even. An odd number puts up an alert such as "canvas width must be even (h.264 encodes in macroblocks), not 1081", and the size stays as it was.
136	- The range is 16 to 16,384. A number outside it is pulled to the nearest limit.
137	- A number with a fraction is rounded to a whole pixel.
138	
139	A project opened from an odd-sized movie keeps that size. Once you change either field, though, both sides are checked. If one side is odd, fix that side first. If both are, choose a preset, because a field can only change one side at a time.
140	
141	## Resize your clips with the canvas
142	
143	**Resize clips proportionally** decides what happens to your clips at the next size change. It's off by default.
144	
145	| Setting | What a size change does |
146	| --- | --- |
147	| Off | Clips keep their scale and their distance in pixels from the centre of the canvas. |
148	| On | Every clip's position and scale change by the same ratio as the canvas, so the layout looks the same at the new size. |
149	
150	When the shape of the canvas changes too, a clip's horizontal position follows the width and its vertical position follows the height. Its scale follows the smaller of the two ratios, so a clip that fitted the old canvas still fits the new one.
151	
152	The checkbox is a preference on this Mac. It's remembered across launches and it isn't saved in the project, so ticking it is not an undo step. The size change it scales is.
153	
154	## Good to know
155	
156	- A resize scales each clip's own placement. An [action](/motion/actions/) that moves a clip keeps its old target, so check any animated moves afterwards.
157	- Clips inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) aren't touched. A nest keeps the size it was made at.
158	- To turn a landscape timeline into a tall or square one, with each clip reframed, use [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/).
159	- Captions can follow a new canvas too. See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/).
160	
161	## With an agent
162	
163	`set_canvas` takes the size and, on each call, whether to scale the clips, with `rescale_clips`. It doesn't read the checkbox, so leaving `rescale_clips` out means the clips aren't scaled. A size outside the range isn't pulled to the limit as a typed one is: the call fails and nothing changes. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
164	
165	## Related
166	
167	- [The Document tab](/projects/document-tab/)
168	- [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/)
169	- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
170	- [Export size](/export/size/)
171	=================== projects/consolidate-media.mdx
172	---
173	title: "Consolidate Media"
174	description: "Copy every file a project uses into its package, so you can hand it over, move it or archive it without the originals."
175	---
176	
177	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
178	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
179	
180	A project normally points at your files where they are. Consolidate Media copies them all into the `.framejob` package and points the project at the copies, so the package becomes the whole edit. You can then hand it to someone, move it, or archive it and delete the originals.
181	
182	<AtAGlance
183	  menu="File ▸ Consolidate Media…"
184	  where="Media tab footer ▸ Consolidate…"
185	  tools="consolidate_media"
186	  needs="A saved project, and room on the disk for a second copy of the footage."
187	/>
188	
189	## Consolidate a project
190	
191	<Steps>
192	
193	1. Choose **File ▸ Consolidate Media…**, or **Consolidate…** at the foot of the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). Both are off when the project has no media. If the project has never been saved, you'll [save it first](#save-the-project-first).
194	
195	2. Watch the **Consolidating Media** sheet as the files copy.
196	
197	3. Read what the sheet reports, then choose **Close**, or **Show in Finder** to see the copies.
198	
199	</Steps>
200	
201	Every file in the media list is copied into a `media` folder inside the package, whether a clip uses it or not. To keep the package smaller, [remove](/projects/remove-media/) what you don't need first. [Unused only](/projects/media-tab/#unused-only) shows you what that is.
202	
203	## Save the project first
204	
205	An untitled project has no package to copy into. On one, the command asks "Save this project first?" and offers **Save…** and **Cancel**. After the save it carries on where it left off. Cancelling the Save panel stops the command.
206	
207	## While it copies
208	
209	The sheet shows a bar, a line such as "Copying 4 files (2.1 GB) into the package…", and the name of the file being copied. When every file is already inside and only the project's links need correcting, the line reads "Relinking 2…".
210	
211	**Cancel** stops between files, so the sheet shows "Stopping…" until the file in progress is done. What was copied stays copied and the project points at it, and the rest keep pointing at the originals. The project always opens. Run the command again to copy the rest.
212	
213	## When it finishes
214	
215	The sheet says what happened and offers **Show in Finder** and **Close**. **Show in Finder** shows the package's `media` folder and closes the sheet. The changes to the project are one undo step called **Consolidate Media**.
216	
217	| The sheet says | What it means |
218	| --- | --- |
219	| "Copied 4 files (2.1 GB) into the package." | How many files it copied, cursor files included. |
220	| "No files needed copying." | Nothing was copied. It also appears beside the lines below when no copy succeeded. |
221	| "Stopped before the rest." | You chose **Cancel**. |
222	| "2 files could not be copied." | Those files keep pointing at their originals, so every clip still plays. The first file's reason shows underneath. |
223	| "1 missing file was left alone — relink intro.mov." | See [Missing files](#missing-files). It names up to three. |
224	| "1 cursor file was missing and left alone." | See [Cursor files](#cursor-files). |
225	
226	## What gets copied
227	
228	### Names and duplicates
229	
230	- Two different files with the same name are kept apart, as `intro.mov` and `intro-2.mov`. Names are compared without regard to case, and a name already in the `media` folder counts as taken.
231	- Two rows in the media list that point at the same file share a single copy.
232	- Files already in the package's `media` folder aren't copied again.
233	
234	### Missing files
235	
236	A missing file can't be copied, so it's left alone and the sheet names it. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/) and consolidate again.
237	
238	With nothing to do, Frame Job doesn't open the sheet. It shows an alert reading "Nothing to consolidate." and why:
239	
240	- "Every file this project uses is already inside the package."
241	- "Every file this project can find is already inside the package. 2 missing files need relinking first."
242	
243	### LUTs
244	
245	[LUTs](/color/luts/) are in the media list, so they're copied like footage, used or not. The looks and Camera Logs that use one then read the copy in the package.
246	
247	### Cursor files
248	
249	A screen recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) is copied too, next to its movie and named after it: `Recording.mov` and `Recording.fjcursor`. It counts as one of the files copied in the final report.
250	
251	- It's copied only once its movie is, and the project points at the copy only once it's there.
252	- One that can't be copied is listed with the other failures, and the recording keeps its original cursor file.
253	- One that's missing is left alone: "1 cursor file was missing and left alone."
254	
255	### WebM, MKV and converted files
256	
257	For a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/), or a file [converted with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), Frame Job copies the movie it plays from, not the file you imported. The row's [tooltip](/projects/media-tab/#the-tooltip) then says it was copied into this project's package.
258	
259	## Move a consolidated package
260	
261	Move or rename a consolidated package and it finds its own copies when it opens. Any missing file with a file of the same name in the package's `media` folder is pointed back at it, and a screen recording's cursor file is found again the same way.
262	
263	This happens with no sheet, adds no undo step, and doesn't mark the project as changed. A file Frame Job can still find is never touched, even if a file of the same name sits in `media`. Anything still missing after this brings up the [Missing media sheet](/projects/relink-media/#relink-from-the-missing-media-sheet).
264	
265	## Good to know
266	
267	- Nothing checks for free space first. A copy that runs out of room is reported with the files that couldn't be copied, and those files keep pointing at their originals.
268	- Undo points the project back at the originals but leaves the copies in the package. Consolidating again then makes second copies, such as `intro-2.mov`.
269	- When two rows share a copy and that copy fails, both keep pointing at the original.
270	
271	## With an agent
272	
273	`consolidate_media` does the same work with no sheet and no **Cancel**, and Frame Job's own window doesn't respond until the copy is done, which can take a while. On a project that has never been saved it stops and says to save first. The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you before it runs it. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).
274	
275	## Related
276	
277	- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)

283	---
284	title: "The Document tab"
285	description: "See what your project is at a glance, and find the settings that apply to the whole project: canvas, frame rate, appearance and markers."
286	---
287	
288	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
289	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
290	
291	The Document tab holds what belongs to the project as a whole rather than to one clip: its size, its frame rate, its background and its markers. The canvas you set here is the fixed frame every clip is composited into, and every export starts from its size.
292	
293	<AtAGlance where="Inspector ▸ Document" tools={['set_canvas', 'get_project']} />
294	
295	<Shot
296	  name="11-document-inspector.inspector"
297	  alt="The inspector's Document tab. The Document section reads Resolution 960 × 540, Frame rate 30 fps, Duration 00:00:05:07, Tracks 5, Background Black and Colour SDR — Rec. 709. Below it are the Canvas section with its Preset, Width, Height, Resize clips proportionally, Dynamic Range and Blending rows, and the Frame Rate section with Rate and Duration."
298	/>
299	
300	## Open the tab
301	
302	Click **Document** at the top of the inspector. Selecting a clip on the timeline moves the inspector to the **Clip** tab, so come back here when you've finished with the clip.
303	
304	## What's in the tab
305	
306	The tab has five sections, from top to bottom.
307	
308	| Section | What it's for |
309	| --- | --- |
310	| **Document** | A read-out of the project. See [below](#the-document-summary). |
311	| **Canvas** | [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/), then the project's [dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/) and [blending](/hdr/blending/). |
312	| **Frame Rate** | The [project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) and the timeline's length. |
313	| **Appearance** | The [background colour, timecode format and Fit new clips to canvas](/projects/background-and-timecode/). |
314	| **Markers** | Every [marker](/timeline/markers/) in the project, in time order. |
315	
316	## The Document summary
317	
318	The first section tells you what the project is before you change anything. Its rows are read-only and update as you work.
319	
320	| Row | What it shows |
321	| --- | --- |
322	| **Resolution** | The canvas size in pixels, such as `1920 × 1080`. |
323	| **Frame rate** | The project's real rate, such as `29.97 fps`, even when the **Rate** popup [can't list it](/projects/frame-rate/#rates-the-popup-doesnt-list). |
324	| **Duration** | The timeline's length, in the project's [timecode format](/projects/background-and-timecode/#choose-a-timecode-format). |
325	| **Tracks** | How many tracks the project has. |
326	| **Background** | `Black`, `White`, a `#RRGGBB` value or `Transparent`. A colour that's only partly opaque also shows its opacity as a percentage, such as `#336699 · 50%`. |
327	| **Colour** | `SDR — Rec. 709` or `HDR — Rec. 2100 HLG`. |
328	
329	## How changes behave
330	
331	You can undo any change you make here to the project. The exception is **Resize clips proportionally**, which is a preference on this Mac rather than part of the project, so undo doesn't touch it.
332	
333	The tab always shows the whole project. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open it keeps working, and it changes the project rather than the nest. A nest keeps the size it was made at, whatever you do to the canvas.
334	
335	## With an agent
336	
337	`set_canvas` changes the size, rate, background, timecode format, Fit new clips to canvas, dynamic range and blending in one call. It must name at least one of them, and anything it doesn't name keeps its value. It works on the whole project, so a call addressed to a nest fails, while a call made with a nest open through `set_scope` changes the project, as the tab does. `get_project` reads the settings back. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
338

344	=================== projects/ffmpeg-conversion.mdx
345	---
346	title: "Convert files with ffmpeg"
347	description: "Use your own ffmpeg to bring in a file macOS can't open: what Frame Job asks, what it copies or re-encodes, and how to change your answer."
348	---
349	
350	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
351	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
352	
353	When macOS can't open a file and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can use it to repackage or convert the file on import. Frame Job doesn't include ffmpeg, and without your own copy this step never appears.
354	
355	<AtAGlance
356	  where={['The alert that appears on import ▸ Repackage or Convert']}
357	  tools={['import_media', 'relink_media']}
358	  needs="Your own ffmpeg and ffprobe, both installed on this Mac."
359	/>
360	
361	## Repackage or convert a file
362	
363	<Steps>
364	
365	1. Add, open or relink the file as usual. If macOS can't open it, an alert appears: "Frame Job cannot open “*file*”."
366	
367	2. Read what it would cost. The alert names the codecs and gives the size and the time.
368	
369	3. Choose **Repackage** or **Convert** to go ahead, or **Cancel** to leave the file out.
370	
371	</Steps>
372	
373	The first button reads **Repackage** or **Convert** depending on the work to be done:
374	
375	| The button | What the alert tells you |
376	| --- | --- |
377	| **Repackage** | Every stream can be copied as it is. No re-encoding, no loss of quality, and a few seconds' work. |
378	| **Convert** | The video can be copied, but the sound has to be re-encoded to AAC. That also takes a few seconds. |
379	| **Convert** | This Mac can't decode the video, so the whole file has to be re-encoded to H.264. The alert gives its picture size and length, and says it takes at least as long as the clip runs, usually longer. |
380	
381	If you choose **Cancel**, Frame Job then shows the reason it couldn't read the file.
382	
383	A conversion shows no progress window. The file appears when it's finished. If you add several files that need this step, Frame Job asks about them one at a time.
384	
385	## What's copied and what's re-encoded
386	
387	Each stream is copied when it can be, and re-encoded when it can't.
388	
389	| Stream | Copied unchanged | Otherwise |
390	| --- | --- | --- |
391	| Video | H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4, QuickTime Animation and DV | Re-encoded to H.264 |
392	| Sound | AAC, ALAC and the usual 16-, 24- and 32-bit PCM | Re-encoded to 256 kbps AAC |
393	
394	The H.264 encode uses x264 at CRF 18 when your ffmpeg has it. Without x264 it uses Apple's VideoToolbox encoder, at a bitrate worked out from the picture size and frame rate, from 2 to 60 Mbps. Either way the result is 8-bit 4:2:0, so a 10-bit source comes in as 8-bit.
395	
396	VP9 Profile 0 or 2 with a known frame rate is copied too, with AAC or ALAC sound beside it, and any other sound is re-encoded to AAC. Frame Job then checks that every frame of the copy sits exactly on the frame rate. If the copy fails that check, or won't open, it's re-encoded to H.264 once. Unless you've told Frame Job to do this automatically, it asks you again first.
397	
398	Only the first video stream and the first audio stream are carried over. Subtitles and data streams are dropped.
399	
400	## Where the converted file goes
401	
402	The converted file goes into `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, the same folder as [WebM and MKV copies](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#the-rewrapped-folder). It keeps its own name in the Media tab, and your original is untouched.
403	
404	Importing the same file again uses the finished conversion with no question, even if you've since removed ffmpeg or chosen never to convert. If the original's path, size or modification date has changed, it counts as a new file.
405	
406	## Remember your answer
407	
408	Tick **Do this automatically from now on** in the alert to keep the answer you give:
409	
410	- Ticked with **Repackage** or **Convert**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
411	- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails with its usual message.
412	
413	There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:
414	
415	```sh
416	defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
417	```
418	
419	That setting holds `ask`, `always` or `never`, and `ask` is the default.
420	
421	## Finding ffmpeg
422	
423	Frame Job needs both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. With only one of them, this step doesn't appear.
424	
425	It looks on your `PATH` first, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `/bin`. It looks once per launch, so quit and reopen Frame Job after installing ffmpeg.
426	
427	To use one particular build, name it in Terminal:
428	
429	```sh
430	defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg
431	```
432	
433	`ffprobe` is then taken from beside it, or else found by the same search. If nothing runnable is at that path, Frame Job doesn't look anywhere else for `ffmpeg`, and this step doesn't appear.
434	
435	## When a conversion fails
436	
437	| The alert says | What it means |
438	| --- | --- |
439	| "Could not convert *file* with ffmpeg: *reason*" | ffmpeg stopped with an error. The reason is its own last line, and without one the sentence ends at "ffmpeg." |
440	| "ffmpeg gave up converting *file*." | It ran out of time. |
441	
442	A **Repackage** gets five minutes or twice the file's length, whichever is longer. A **Convert** gets 30 minutes or 30 times the file's length, whichever is longer. Neither gets more than 4 hours.
443	
444	No partial file is left behind. If a conversion finishes but macOS still can't open the result, Frame Job throws it away and shows the original error, so the next import starts afresh.
445	
446	## A lost conversion stays missing
447	
448	Unlike a [WebM copy](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#if-a-copy-goes-missing), a conversion that's deleted isn't made again when the project opens. The media stays missing until you [relink it](/projects/relink-media/). Relinking to the original file goes through this step again.
449	
450	A conversion you've only moved is treated like any other file: its [bookmark](/projects/import-media/#referenced-not-copied) often finds it again. One moved to the Trash goes on playing from the Trash.
451	
452	## Files ffmpeg isn't offered for
453	
454	Frame Job doesn't offer ffmpeg for:
455	
456	- A picture or a `.cube` file it can't read.
457	- A file that timed out, because ffmpeg would stall on the same volume.
458	- A codec this Mac can't decode inside a file macOS can open, or inside a WebM or MKV file. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
459	- A WebM or MKV file stopped by the [free-space check](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#free-space).
460	- A file in which ffprobe finds no video or audio.
461	
462	## With an agent
463	
464	An agent's import never shows this question. Unless you've chosen to convert automatically, the offer counts as declined, and the import fails and gives the reason. While the answer is still `ask` and ffmpeg is installed, the error also says how to get past it: import the file from the app's window, or set the answer to `always`.
465	
466	To set it, tick [**Do this automatically from now on**](#remember-your-answer) with **Repackage** or **Convert**, or run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:
467	
468	```sh
469	defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport always
470	```
471	
472	With `always` set, `import_media` and `relink_media` convert without asking, and the import can take as long as the conversion does. `import_media` then gives the converted file as `path` and the file you named as `original`, as it does for a WebM copy. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
473	
474	## Related

480	=================== projects/frame-rate.mdx
481	---
482	title: "Project frame rate"
483	description: "Choose the rate your project runs at, match it to your footage, and see what a rate change does to the timeline."
484	---
485	
486	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
487	
488	The project's frame rate sets the grid that every edit lands on. A new project runs at 30 fps, and a project opened from a movie takes the movie's rate. A rate chosen for one export is separate: see [Export frame rate](/export/frame-rate/).
489	
490	<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Frame Rate" tools="set_canvas" />
491	
492	## Choose a rate
493	
494	In the **Frame Rate** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/), choose a rate from **Rate**: **24**, **23.976**, **25**, **30**, **29.97**, **50**, **60** or **Match First Clip**.
495	
496	The change is one undo step. See [what it does to the timeline](#what-a-rate-change-does).
497	
498	## Match the first clip
499	
500	**Match First Clip** takes the rate of the earliest clip on the timeline whose file has video. It beeps if there isn't one.
501	
502	It sets the rate once, and later changes to the timeline don't move it. The popup then shows that rate, if it [lists it](#rates-the-popup-doesnt-list). A picture counts as having video here, and it reads as 30 fps.
503	
504	## Rates the popup doesn't list
505	
506	A project can run at a rate the popup doesn't have, because a file's rate is kept as it is when you open it.
507	
508	- A file at 24, 23.976, 25, 30, 29.97, 48, 50, 60 or 59.94 fps keeps that exact rate.
509	- Any other rate is kept to three decimals, so a 47.3 fps recording stays at 47.3 and doesn't become 48. Screen recordings often have odd rates.
510	
511	:::caution
512	At a rate it doesn't list, **Rate** shows **24**. The **Frame rate** row at the top of the Document tab shows the real rate, so trust that one.
513	:::
514	
515	Choosing a popup item changes the rate. **Match First Clip** brings the file's own rate back.
516	
517	## What a rate change does
518	
519	Changing the rate moves every clip start, clip length, action and marker onto the new frame grid, inside nests as well.
520	
521	- A clip's length is held to the media it has left, so a coarser grid can't push a clip past the end of its file.
522	- A clip always keeps at least one frame.
523	- An action stays inside its clip. A speed ramp's action is only snapped to the new grid.
524	- Where a clip starts reading its source doesn't change, and sound fades keep their lengths.
525	
526	If two markers land on the same frame at the new rate, only one stays: the one added first.
527	
528	Frame Job doesn't check the new positions for overlaps, and it won't stop a rate change because of one. Each edge moves by less than a frame, so an overlap can grow by a frame at most.
529	
530	## Read the timeline's length
531	
532	**Duration**, under **Rate**, is a read-only row showing the timeline's length in the project's [timecode format](/projects/background-and-timecode/#choose-a-timecode-format).
533	
534	## With an agent
535	
536	`set_canvas` takes `fps` as `[numerator, denominator]`: `[30, 1]`, `[30000, 1001]` for 29.97 or `[24000, 1001]` for 23.976. Any fraction works, so an agent can set a rate the popup doesn't list, such as 48 or 59.94 fps. A 0 in either place fails and the rate stays as it was. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
537	
538	## Related

543	=================== projects/import-media.mdx
544	---
545	title: "Import media"
546	description: "Bring movies, sound, pictures and LUTs into a project with Add Media… or a Finder drop, and find out why a file won't come in."
547	---
548	
549	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
550	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
551	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
552	
553	Importing puts a file in the project's Media tab, ready to place on the timeline. Frame Job reads the file from where it already is, so nothing is copied and the project stays small.
554	
555	<AtAGlance
556	  menu="File ▸ Add Media…"
557	  keys="⇧⌘I"
558	  where={['Media tab ▸ Add Media…', 'Drag from the Finder onto the Media tab']}
559	  tools={['import_media', 'add_media']}
560	/>
561	
562	<Shot
563	  name="10b-media-tab.inspector"
564	  alt="The Media tab of the inspector, with the Add Media… button and its ⇧⌘I shortcut at the top of the list, and a count of the project's items beside them."
565	/>
566	
567	## Add media
568	
569	<Steps>
570	
571	1. Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>), or **Add Media…** at the top of the Media tab.
572	
573	2. Pick one or more files, and choose **Open**.
574	
575	</Steps>
576	
577	Frame Job checks every file, then adds the ones it can read to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) together, as one undo step. The step is called **Add Media**, or **Add 3 Media Files** for three.
578	
579	The files are in the Media tab, not on the timeline. [Place them](/editing/add-clips/) from there. Thumbnails and waveforms are built in the background, so they fill in a moment later.
580	
581	Adding a file that's already in the list changes nothing. A file Frame Job can't read shows an alert naming it, and the rest are still added.
582	
583	## Drop on the Media tab
584	
585	Drag files from the Finder onto the Media tab to add them to this project. It works like **Add Media…**, with one difference: a drop has no list of allowed types, so Frame Job tries every file you drop. That's how a format the panels don't list gets in.
586	
587	A Finder drop anywhere else on the window, such as the canvas or the timeline, doesn't add to this project. It opens the file as a new project of its own, as a drop on the Dock icon does. See [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).
588	
589	## What each way takes
590	
591	The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels only let you pick the types they list. To bring in anything else, drop it on the Media tab.
592	
593	| Files | **Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…**, or a drop on the window or the Dock | A drop on the Media tab |
594	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
595	| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
596	| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
597	| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
598	| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
599	| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
600	| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |
601	
602	A `.cube` is imported, never opened. It sits in the Media tab and you apply it to clips as a [look](/color/luts/), or to a file as its [camera log](/hdr/log-luts/). It never goes on the timeline.
603	
604	Caption files aren't media. Bring an `.srt` in with [Import Captions](/captions/import-captions/). Every format and codec Frame Job reads is listed in [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).
605	
606	## Referenced, not copied
607	
608	A project remembers each file's path and a Finder bookmark, and reads the file from there. The package stays small, but it depends on your footage staying put. If you move a file, the bookmark often finds it again.
609	
610	When you want a package that holds everything it needs, use [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).
611	
612	WebM and Matroska files, and anything converted with ffmpeg, are the exception: Frame Job reads those from a copy it keeps in its own folder. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) and [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
613	
614	## A project always opens
615	
616	A project opens even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place on the timeline and show a slate, and their rows in the Media tab wear the **missing** badge.
617	
618	Those clips still export, showing the slate and with no sound. To bring them back, see [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
619	
620	## Codecs this Mac can't decode
621	
622	Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame. If nothing on this Mac can decode it, the file is left out and an alert names the codec.
623	
624	| The alert says | What it means |
625	| --- | --- |
626	| "*file* is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode." | VP8 doesn't import. |
627	| "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." | AV1 needs a hardware decoder, which this Mac doesn't have. |
628	| "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." | VP9 Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. Profiles 0 and 2 do. |
629	
630	Any other codec gets the same sentence with its four-character code in place of a name. There's no way past these, and [ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) isn't offered.
631	
632	A file in a codec this Mac does decode still imports when some of its data is damaged.
633	
634	## Import errors
635	
636	| The alert says | What it means |
637	| --- | --- |
638	| "Could not read *file*." | The file is damaged, or it isn't a format Frame Job reads. |
639	| "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." | The file holds neither. |
640	| "Timed out reading *file*." | The check took more than 30 seconds, usually because the file is on a stalled network volume. |
641	| "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." | The `.cube` can't be read. The alert names the line and the problem. |
642	
643	If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job may offer to convert a file before it shows the first two of these. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
644	
645	## Good to know
646	
647	- A project holds at most 1,024 media files.
648	- Undoing an import takes the files out of the project and leaves them on disk.
649	
650	## With an agent
651	
652	`import_media` does what **Add Media…** does, one file at a time, and it never stops to ask a question. It takes the file's path, absolute or starting with `~`, and gives back the new media id with what it found in the file: its kind, length, size, frame rate, and whether it has video, sound or transparency. Place the file with `add_clip`.
653	
654	`add_media` is different: it adds an entry from a description you supply and doesn't look at the file. Only the path is needed, and a path already in the list changes nothing. Use it only to replay a project's own JSON. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).
655	
656	## Related
