664	---
665	title: "On-device media analysis"
666	description: "What Frame Job works out about your files on this Mac, when it runs, how to stop it, and where the results are kept."
667	---
668	
669	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
670	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
671	
672	Frame Job studies your files so its commands know where the cuts fall, who's in frame and when someone is talking. All of it happens on this Mac, with no upload, no network request and no key.
673	
674	<AtAGlance
675	  menu={['Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes', 'Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Background', 'Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
676	  where={['The Analyzing sheet', 'Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Background']}
677	  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'analyze_cutout', 'split_at_shots', 'reframe_clip', 'detect_silence', 'set_media_speech', 'set_video', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version']}
678	  needs="Nothing. Every analysis runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
679	/>
680	
681	This page explains the analysis itself. How to use a result is on the page of the feature that uses it.
682	
683	## What Frame Job works out
684	
685	| Result | When it's made | What uses it |
686	| --- | --- | --- |
687	| [Filmstrips, waveforms and loudness](#whats-built-when-a-file-arrives) | When a file arrives | The timeline and the audio tools |
688	| [Voice detection](#voice-detection) | When a file arrives | Remove Silences, Enhance Voice, Duck by Speech and others |
689	| [Shots](#shots) | When something asks | Split at Shot Changes, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version |
690	| [Faces](#faces) | When something asks | Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Switch by Speaker, Show Subjects |
691	| [People and salient regions](#people-and-salient-regions) | When something asks | Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Show Subjects |
692	| [Person masks](#person-masks) | When a clip needs them | Remove Background, Text Behind Subject |
693	| [Foreground masks](#foreground-masks-on-pictures) | When a picture needs one | Remove Background, Text Behind Subject |
694	| [Sound events](#sound-events) | When an agent asks | Agents only |
695	
696	## Analysis happens on demand
697	
698	Importing a file doesn't analyse its picture. Frame Job does that when something asks for it: Split at Shot Changes, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version, Switch by Speaker, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject or an agent.
699	
700	Only the part that's needed is read:
701	
702	- Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and an agent reframing a clip ask for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side.
703	- Split at Shot Changes reads the parts its clips play, and skips any stretch of the file between them that no clip uses.
704	- A part that's already been analysed isn't read again, so a second request over the same footage starts at once.
705	
706	If two analyses of one file run at different times, what they find is added together. Neither replaces the other.
707	
708	## The Analyzing sheet
709	
710	When a menu command needs an analysis that isn't in the project yet, the **Analyzing** sheet comes up while it's made. When everything is already there, the sheet doesn't appear and the command goes straight ahead.
711	
712	<Shot
713	  name="15f-analyzing-sheet.sheet"
714	  alt="The Analyzing sheet for Split at Shot Changes. A sentence explains that nothing changes until the analysis is found and that Stop leaves everything as it is. Below it, the file speech.mov has an empty progress bar and the word Waiting, and a Stop button sits at the bottom right."
715	/>
716	
717	The sheet has one row for each file that needs work, with its name, a bar and a status:
718	
719	| Status | What it means |
720	| --- | --- |
721	| Waiting | Frame Job hasn't read the file's first frame yet. |
722	| A percentage | The share of the work done so far. |
723	| Done | This file has finished. |
724	
725	For [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), a file can have a row for each thing being found, such as "speech.mov — Faces", "speech.mov — Shot changes" and "speech.mov — People and salient regions".
726	
727	These commands use the sheet:
728	
729	- **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**
730	- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**, after you press **Follow** in its own sheet
731	- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**, after you press **Make** in its own sheet
732	- **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**, before its own sheet, when it needs to find faces because it's working from one microphone
733	
734	When every row is done, the sheet closes by itself and the command carries on. Every editor action is off while the sheet is up.
735	
736	If the project changes while the sheet is up, which an agent can do, the command makes no edit. The inspector says so and asks you to choose the command again.
737	
738	[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) doesn't use this sheet. It makes its masks while you go on working, and shows its progress in **Status** in the Clip tab's **Background** section.
739	
740	### Stop an analysis
741	
742	Choose **Stop**, or press <kbd>Esc</kbd>. The sheet closes, the command is cancelled and no edit is made. What was already saved stays in the project, so choosing the command again carries on from there.
743	
744	Minimising the window also stops the work. When you bring the window back, the sheet starts again on whatever hadn't finished.
745	
746	### When an analysis fails
747	
748	If an analysis can't finish, the command stops instead of editing with half an answer. Frame Job beeps, and the foot of the inspector names the file and the reason, for example: "The shots analysis of “interview.mov” failed: …"
749	
750	If a file is missing or can't be read, Split at Shot Changes and Switch by Speaker stop before the sheet opens, and Follow Subject says so in its own sheet. Make Vertical Version keeps a clip whose file is missing as it's placed and goes on with the rest. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
751	
752	## Analysis runs in the background
753	
754	You can keep working while an analysis runs, except while the Analyzing sheet is up.
755	
756	- Picture analysis runs at low priority, one job at a time across all your open projects.
757	- Sound analysis has its own queue, so one sound job can run beside one picture job.
758	- Frame Job saves what it has found every 30 seconds, and at the end of each stretch of the file it reads. If a job stops part-way, everything saved so far is kept and the next request continues from there.
759	- A job that nothing wants any more is dropped if it hasn't started, and cancelled if it has. Closing a project does this to its jobs.
760	
761	## What each analysis finds
762	
763	### Shots
764	
765	Frame Job finds the hard cuts in a video by comparing each frame's colours with the frames before it. This is plain arithmetic, with no machine learning.
766	
767	- A gradual dissolve isn't reported as a cut.
768	- A single flash frame isn't a cut.
769	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can show as one cut.
770	
771	[Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/) cuts your clips at these moments.
772	
773	### Faces
774	
775	Frame Job looks for faces ten times a second of the file's own time, using Apple's Vision framework. For each face it keeps its box, how far it's turned and tilted, and how open the mouth is.
776	
777	Faces are listed from left to right. They carry no identity, so Frame Job doesn't know that a face in one sample is the same person in the next, and it never puts names to faces.
778	
779	### People and salient regions
780	
781	At the same ten samples a second, Frame Job finds:
782	
783	- **People**, as a box around each person's head and shoulders.
784	- **Salient regions**, as boxes around the parts of the picture the eye goes to first. In a talking-head shot that's usually the speaker, and on a slide it's often the text.
785	
786	Each sample is judged on its own, so no person is followed from one moment to the next. See [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/) for how Frame Job uses them, and [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) to see faces, people and salient regions over the preview.
787	
788	### Person masks
789	
790	A person mask is an outline of a person, made for every frame of the video that a clip plays. [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) and [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/) draw with these masks, and they're made when a clip has one of those on.
791	
792	A frame counts as holding a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half strength. The masks are kept at the size Vision makes them, one for every frame, so a long clip's masks take up room in the package: about 62 MB for a minute of 1080p video.
793	
794	### Foreground masks on pictures
795	
796	On a still picture, Frame Job can mask the foreground subject, whether or not it's a person. Turn on Remove Background, then choose **Foreground** in the **Subject** row of the Clip tab's **Background** section. The row appears when every selected clip is a picture, and **Person** is the default.
797	
798	Either way a picture gets one mask, made from the picture as it's drawn, the right way up.
799	
800	### Sound events
801	
802	Frame Job can listen to a file's first sound track and score how likely six kinds of sound are: laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech. It uses Apple's Sound Analysis, in overlapping windows 1.5 seconds long that start every 0.75 seconds. Each score runs from 0 to 1, and there's no score where a window runs past the end of the sound.
803	
804	Only an agent can ask for these, and no menu or pane uses them. Treat the scores as hints, never as a finding on their own.
805	
806	The file needs sound, and an audio file works. Frame Job won't read sound events for a clip that plays in reverse, because its sound runs backwards.
807	
808	## What's built when a file arrives
809	
810	After you open a project, import a file or relink one, Frame Job builds these in the background, and the timeline fills in as they finish:
811	
812	- **Filmstrip thumbnails** for every file with a picture, which its clips show on the timeline. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
813	- **The waveform**, at 100 peaks a second.
814	- **The loudness record**, in 10 ms steps, which Normalize, Enhance Voice and the loudness read-outs use.
815	- **Sound-matching features**, which [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) uses.
816	- **[Voice detection](#voice-detection)**.
817	
818	At most two files' sound is read at a time, so a big import doesn't hold up playback or a speed ramp's sound. Anything already built for an unchanged file is never built again. A file with no sound has no waveform, loudness or voice detection, and a `.cube` LUT file gets none of these.
819	
820	Until one of these is ready, the controls that need it wait or read "measuring…". A command that needs it says the file is still being analysed and asks you to try again in a moment.
821	
822	If a waveform or loudness pass fails, Frame Job tries again after 2 seconds and again after 10. After that it tries the next time you open the project.
823	
824	### Voice detection
825	
826	Frame Job scores every 32 ms of a file's sound for speech, using the Silero voice model bundled with the app. That's how later commands tell a voice from noise. These use it:
827	
828	- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/voice-or-level/), in its **Voice** mode
829	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/)
830	- The [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
831	- [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/)
832	- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
833	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
834	- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)
835	- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/) and [Shorten a pause](/captions/shorten-pauses/)
836	- The [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/), to place where a word on this Mac's reading really starts and to find the pauses between paragraphs
837	
838	If the voice model can't be used, Remove Silences says so and judges quiet by level instead.
839	
840	## Results are kept per file
841	
842	Anything Frame Job finds is kept for the file, not for a clip, in the project's cache, a folder of things it can make again. Every clip of a file shares it, and a second request over the same part is ready at once. Picture analysis and sound events live in the `.framejob` package under `cache/analysis/`.
843	
844	A result counts only for the file it was made from, which Frame Job checks by the file's size, modification time and length. Relink to a different file, or change the file on disk, and it's analysed again. An unchanged file isn't.
845	
846	Picture analysis and sound events also record the macOS build they were made on. After a macOS update, or on a Mac running a different build, they're made again the next time something asks. The same goes when a Frame Job update changes what one of them stores.
847	
848	## Results travel with the project
849	
850	The caches live inside the `.framejob` package, so they go wherever it goes. Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps them. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/) for what's inside.
851	
852	A new project made from this one starts with them too, so nothing is analysed twice. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) and the **Make a copy** option of [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) carry these, for each file the new project keeps:
853	
854	- Filmstrips, waveforms and loudness
855	- Voice detection and sound-matching features
856	- On-device transcripts
857	- Everything on this page that's found in the picture or sound
858	- The reversed render of any clip that plays backwards
859	
860	Your media files are never copied. Neither is speed-ramp audio, or a voice-isolated or voice-effect render, and those are made again when they're needed. A cloud transcript stays behind unless its copy on AssemblyAI has already been deleted.
861	
862	## Good to know
863	
864	- **Show Subjects** never starts an analysis. Where nothing has been found it reads "Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it".
865	- A package with a missing or damaged cache still opens, and what's built when a file arrives is built again. Picture analysis is made again when something next asks, but a lost cloud transcript costs money to make again.
866	- Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches sit in a temporary folder. The first save copies them into the package.
867	
868	## With an agent
869	
870	An agent can read the results themselves with `get_media_analysis`, for a whole file or for the part one clip plays, and it's the only way to reach [sound events](#sound-events). It shows no sheet. It waits at most 60 seconds, then stops and says how much it covered. What it covered is kept, so asking again carries on. A long file is read in windows, because one reply has a size limit. Each reply says whether it came from the cache alone, and what the result was made with.
871	
872	`analyze_cutout` makes a clip's masks and says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
873

904	## What the tab shows
905	
906	A project points at your files where they are, and doesn't copy them in. That's why a row can be missing, and why the tab offers **Relink…** and **Consolidate…**.
907	
908	From top to bottom, the tab holds:
909	
910	- **The top bar:** **Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>) and [the item count](#the-item-count). See [Import media](/projects/import-media/). You can also drop files from the Finder onto the tab to add them.
911	- **The find band:** [a search field](#search-by-name), [a sort](#sort) and [Unused only](#unused-only). With no media yet, this band isn't there and the tab reads "Drop files here, or use Add Media…."
912	- **The list:** one row per file.
913	- **The footer:** **Consolidate…**, with the line "Copies sources into the package". See [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).
914	
915	Three more sections sit under the list and work on the [selected row](#select-a-row):
916	
917	| Section | Appears once the project has | See |
918	| --- | --- | --- |
919	| **Camera Log** | A video file | [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) |
920	| **HDR10** | An HDR10 (PQ) file | [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) |
921	| **Cursor** | A movie that has a picture, not only sound | [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/) |
922	
923	## Read a row
924	
925	Each row has a thumbnail, the file's name, and a line of facts that depends on the kind of file.
926	
927	| Kind | Thumbnail | The line reads |
928	| --- | --- | --- |
929	| Movie | A frame from the movie | Duration, size and frame rate, such as `00:01:12:04 · 1920×1080 · 29.97 fps` |
930	| Picture | The picture | Width × height and `30 fps`, such as `3024×4032 · 30 fps` |
931	| Sound | A waveform glyph | Duration |
932	| LUT | A cube glyph | `LUT` |
933	
934	A file with no duration or size shows its kind instead. Thumbnails arrive a moment after an import, and until then a glyph stands in. A line too long for the row ends in an ellipsis, so widen the inspector to read the rest.
935	
936	### Badges
937	
938	Badges sit at the right of a row:
939	
940	- **audio**, in green, marks a file with sound.
941	- **missing**, in coral, marks a file Frame Job can't find. It's always shown, however little room the row has, because the name and the line give way first. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
942	
943	### The tooltip
944	
945	Hover over a row to see how to place it: "Drag to a timeline track, or onto the canvas. Hold ⌥ to insert, ⇧⌥ to overwrite."
946	
947	A LUT's tooltip reads "A LUT: apply it to clips as a look."
948	
949	A file Frame Job made a movie copy of, such as a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) or a [conversion with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), has one more line above that. It gives the original's path and where the copy lives: Frame Job's Rewrapped folder, or this project's package once you've [consolidated](/projects/consolidate-media/#webm-mkv-and-converted-files).
950	
951	## Find a file
952	
953	### Search by name
954	
955	Type in **Search by name** and the list narrows as you type. It ignores case and accents, as the Finder does, so "resume" finds "Résumé.mov". Every character you type counts, including a space. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to clear the field.
956	
957	If nothing matches, or nothing is left once [Unused only](#unused-only) is on too, the tab reads "No media matches the search or the filter."
958	
959	### Sort
960	
961	The **Sort** popup puts the list in one of four orders. The default is **Import Order**.
962	
963	| Sort | Order |
964	| --- | --- |
965	| **Import Order** | The order the files were added. |
966	| **Name** | Alphabetical, the way the Finder sorts, so `clip2` comes before `clip10`. |
967	| **Duration** | Shortest first. Pictures and LUTs have no duration, so they come first. |
968	| **Kind** | Audio, Image, LUT, then Video. |
969	
970	Every order is ascending, and files that tie stay in import order.
971	
972	### Unused only
973	
974	Tick **Unused only** to show only the files no clip uses. It's a quick way to see what you could [remove](/projects/remove-media/) before you hand a project on.
975	
976	- A file used only inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) counts as used.
977	- A LUT counts as used when it's a clip's look or a file's Camera Log. A LUT used only as the look at the end of an action counts as unused.
978	
979	### The item count
980	
981	The top bar counts the files, and how many are showing while the list is narrowed:
982	
983	| Count | Means |
984	| --- | --- |
985	| No media | The project has no files. |
986	| 1 item, 12 items | Every file is showing. |
987	| 3 of 12 items | A search or Unused only is hiding the rest. |
988	
989	The search, the sort and Unused only belong to the window. They aren't saved with the project, and each open project has its own. They do survive an import, so a search stays on while you add more files.
990	
991	## Select a row
992	
993	Click a row to select it. The row gets an outline in the accent colour, and it becomes the file these work on:
994	
995	- **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** and **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**, which stay off until a row other than a LUT is selected. See [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/).
996	- The Camera Log, HDR10 and Cursor sections under the list.
997	
998	Selecting a row isn't an edit. It adds no undo step and doesn't mark the project as changed. If a search or Unused only hides the selected row, the row is deselected, so you can't place a file you can't see.
999	
1000	## The row's menu
1001	
1002	Right-click a row for its menu. It acts on the row you clicked, whatever the selected row is.
1003	
1004	| Item | What it does |
1005	| --- | --- |
1006	| **Insert at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead and makes room for it. Off for a LUT. |
1007	| **Overwrite at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead and takes the room it needs. Off for a LUT. |
1008	| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects the clips showing this file. See [below](#reveal-in-timeline). |
1009	| **Reveal in Finder** | Shows the file in the Finder. See [below](#reveal-in-finder). |
1010	| **Relink…** | Points this row at another file. See [Relink one file](/projects/relink-media/#relink-one-file). |
1011	| **Remove** | Takes the file out of the project. See [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/). |
1012	
1013	**Insert at Playhead** and **Overwrite at Playhead** also select the row. They use the same track as the **Edit** menu's items, the selected clip's track or else the front track, and [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/) has the rest. A LUT is never placed, because it's [applied as a look](/color/luts/). A LUT row doesn't drag either.
1014	
1015	### Reveal in Timeline
1016	
1017	**Reveal in Timeline** shows you where you used a file. It selects every clip showing the file and scrolls to the earliest one. If that changes the selection, the inspector switches to the Clip tab. For a LUT, it selects the clips whose look it is.
1018	
1019	The item is off when nothing in the timeline itself uses the file, and that includes a file whose only clips are inside a nest. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> first: the command looks at whatever's open, so it then finds the clips in there.
1020	
1021	Revealing clips changes the selection, not the project. It adds no undo step.
1022	
1023	### Reveal in Finder
1024	
1025	**Reveal in Finder** shows the file in the Finder. For a WebM, an MKV or another file Frame Job made a copy of, it shows the original, or the copy when the original has gone. With neither on disk, it beeps.

The project you made it from doesn't change. If you only want a file of that section, [export the range](/export/range/) instead.
1045	
1046	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ New Project from Range…" tools="new_project_from_range" />
1047	
1048	## Make a project from a range
1049	
1050	<Steps>
1051	
1052	1. Set the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) with **Mark ▸ Set In** (<kbd>I</kbd>) and **Mark ▸ Set Out** (<kbd>O</kbd>).
1053	
1054	2. Choose **File ▸ New Project from Range…**.
1055	
1056	</Steps>
1057	
1058	The new project opens in its own window straight away. There's no sheet to fill in, and the command has no key.
1059	
1060	The item is dimmed when no range is set, while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, and while a sheet is on the window.
1061	
1062	## What is kept
1063	
1064	- **Clips across an edge** are cut there, the same way [Split](/editing/splitting/) cuts them. This happens on every track, locked or not, and a linked pair stays linked.
1065	- **Clips wholly inside the range** are kept. Everything outside it goes.
1066	- **A transition across an edge** becomes a hard start or end. The piece beyond the edge is dropped, and at the In edge the incoming piece starts with no transition.
1067	- **Markers inside the range** are kept, on the same moments of the edit. A marker exactly on the Out frame isn't kept.
1068	- **Tracks and the canvas** stay as they are, including any track that ends up empty and any lock.
1069	- **Media no kept clip plays** is left out, unless a kept clip's look or a kept file's colour setting still uses it as a [LUT](/color/luts/), or a kept clip's **Hide While Silent** follows it. Nests no kept clip reaches are left out too.
1070	
1071	## What comes with it
1072	
1073	The new project brings what's already been measured, so nothing is measured again when it opens. For each media file it keeps:
1074	
1075	- filmstrips, waveforms, and loudness, speech and sync data
1076	- transcripts read on this Mac
1077	- [analyses](/projects/media-analysis/), such as shots, people's masks, faces, sound events and subjects
1078	- the backwards render of a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/)
1079	
1080	Media files themselves are never copied. The new project points at the same files as the original.
1081	
1082	[Speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), [isolated voice](/audio/voice-isolation/) and [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) renders don't come along. They're made again when needed.
1083	
1084	### Cloud transcripts
1085	
1086	A transcript from [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) goes to the new project only once AssemblyAI has been told to delete its copy. One still waiting for that delete stays in the original project.
1087	
1088	### Graphics
1089	
1090	The graphics the kept clips draw come along, and so does every font and picture of the project's graphics, whether a kept clip uses it or not. A graphic's kept earlier versions don't.
1091	
1092	## The new project's name and undo
1093	
1094	The new project opens untitled with unsaved changes, named after its parent with " (range)" added, such as "Interview (range)". Closing it asks whether to save.
1095	
1096	It starts at the range. There's no undo step back to the whole timeline, and the original project gets no undo step either, because nothing happened to it.
1097	
1098	## When Frame Job won't do it
1099	
1100	If the range can't be kept, the command beeps and shows why at the foot of the inspector, and no project opens.
1101	
1102	| The message says | What to do |
1103	| --- | --- |
1104	| "Clip *N* is a nest across the range's edge; a nest clip has no in point, so a cut there would replay it from its start. Move the edge, or open the nest and unnest it." | Do one of those. A nest clip can't be cut at an edge. |
1105	| "Nothing plays between … and … ticks." | The range holds no clips. Move it over something. |
1106	| "Keeping … to … ticks would leave clips *A* and *B* overlapping by … ticks, more than half of the shorter piece (… ticks); move an edge further from their transition." | An edge would cut a clip too short for a transition inside the range. Move the edge. |
1107	
1108	These messages give times in ticks, 600,000 to the second, so 1,200,000 ticks is 2 seconds into the timeline.
1109	
1110	The command also beeps when In and Out are on the same frame, because the range is empty.
1111	
1112	## With an agent
1113	
1114	`new_project_from_range` takes the range as times on the top-level timeline, so it doesn't need the In–Out range set, and it won't run while a nest is open. It can also save the new project at a path first, adding `.framejob` if the path lacks it, as long as nothing exists there and no other open project holds it. The assistant asks you before it does that. It returns the new project and how much came along with it. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

1130	
1131	A project is a `.framejob` package: one item in the Finder that holds your edit. This page is about opening one you've saved. To turn a movie, sound file or picture into a new project, see [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/).
1132	
1133	<AtAGlance
1134	  menu={['File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ Open Recent ▸', 'File ▸ Open Recent ▸ Clear Menu']}
1135	  keys="⌘O"
1136	  where={['Double-click in the Finder', 'Welcome window ▸ Open Video…', 'Welcome window ▸ Recent', 'A drop on the Dock icon or a window']}
1137	  tools={['open_project', 'relink_media']}
1138	/>
1139	
1140	## Open a saved project
1141	
1142	Choose **File ▸ Open…** (<kbd>⌘O</kbd>) and pick the package, or double-click it in the Finder. A double-click on a `.framejob` always opens it in Frame Job.
1143	
1144	The open panel lists projects along with QuickTime, MPEG-4 and M4V files, other movies, and M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Everything but a project opens as a [fresh untitled project](/projects/start-a-project/).
1145	
1146	A `.fjgraphic` isn't a project, and **File ▸ Open…** doesn't list one. See [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).
1147	
1148	## Open a recent project
1149	
1150	**File ▸ Open Recent ▸** lists what you've opened lately. Choose one to reopen it. macOS fills the list, and **Clear Menu** at the foot of it empties it.
1151	
1152	The [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/#reopen-a-recent-project) shows the five most recent from the same list.
1153	
1154	## Drop files to open them
1155	
1156	Drag from the Finder onto a project window, the Welcome window or the Dock icon. Each file opens as a document of its own:
1157	
1158	- A `.framejob` package opens that project.
1159	- A media file opens as a fresh untitled project built around it, so several files make several projects.
1160	
1161	Only projects and the types **File ▸ Open…** lists are taken: MOV, MP4, M4V and other movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC. Anything else is ignored, with one exception: a `.fjgraphic` dropped on the Dock icon [goes to the Import Graphic sheet](/graphics/share-a-graphic/#open-from-the-finder).
1162	
1163	:::caution
1164	A drop on a project window doesn't add to that project. To add a file to the project you have open, drop it on the [Media tab](/projects/import-media/). Anywhere else in the window, the timeline and preview included, the drop opens a new project.
1165	:::
1166	
1167	## Open a project that's already open
1168	
1169	Opening a saved project that's already open brings its window forward. It doesn't open a second copy.
1170	
1171	That's for saved projects. A movie opened as an untitled project has no file of its own yet, so opening the same movie again makes a second untitled project.
1172	
1173	## Open a project from another version
1174	
1175	A project saved by any earlier version of Frame Job opens. It's brought up to the current format as it opens, and the next save writes it in the current format.
1176	
1177	A project saved by a newer Frame Job won't open. The message gives both versions and asks you to update:
1178	
1179	> project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it
1180	
1181	## When a project won't open
1182	
1183	A damaged project, or one holding values out of range, fails to open with a message naming the problem. The package isn't rewritten, so a failed open costs you nothing.
1184	
1185	| The message says | What it means |
1186	| --- | --- |
1187	| "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." | The edit file inside the package can't be read as text. |
1188	| "project json is not valid json: …" | The edit file is damaged. |
1189	| "project json does not match the schema: …" | The edit file holds something Frame Job can't read as a project. |
1190	
1191	Filmstrips, waveforms and the like inside the package are never needed to open it. A missing or damaged one is made again. See [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).
1192	
1193	## Open a project with missing files
1194	
1195	A project always opens, even if its files have moved. The clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate until the files are found, and the **Missing media** sheet appears once, when the window first opens. You can close it and go on working, and use **Relink…** on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) later.
1196	
1197	A project with [consolidated media](/projects/consolidate-media/) finds the copies in its own package again after the package moves, with nothing for you to do.
1198	
1199	See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
1200	
1201	## With an agent
1202	
1203	`open_project` takes a path, absolute or starting with `~`, to a project, movie, sound file or picture. When that file is already open it brings the window forward and returns `already_open: true`. Unlike a person's open:
1204	
1205	- It recognises a movie already open as an untitled project, and brings that window forward instead of making a second one.
1206	- It never asks the [ffmpeg question](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
1207	
1208	See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

1221	---
1222	
1223	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
1224	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1225	
1226	A project points at your files where they are, so moving or deleting one leaves its clips with nothing to show. Relinking tells Frame Job where the file is now, or gives it another file to use instead.
1227	
1228	<AtAGlance
1229	  where={['The Missing media sheet, when a project opens', 'Right-click a row on the Media tab ▸ Relink…']}
1230	  tools={['relink_media', 'get_project']}
1231	/>
1232	
1233	## When a file goes missing
1234	
1235	A project always opens, even with files gone. For each missing file:
1236	
1237	- Its clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate, with no sound.
1238	- Its row on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wears a coral **missing** badge.
1239	- An export still runs, and writes the slate and silence for those clips.
1240	
1241	Frame Job remembers a file by more than its path, so one you've moved or renamed is often still found and never shows as missing.
1242	
1243	## Relink from the Missing media sheet
1244	
1245	When a project opens with files missing, the **Missing media** sheet comes up. It reads "The project opened without these files: their clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate until the files are found." Each file is listed with its old path, and the footnote counts them ("3 files").
1246	
1247	<Steps>
1248	
1249	1. Choose **Locate…** beside a file.
1250	
1251	2. Pick its new location in the panel, which reads "Choose the file for “name”." Its path appears in the row, and the button turns into **Change…**.
1252	
1253	3. Check the other rows. Frame Job has [looked in the same folder](#locate-one-file-find-the-rest) for them.
1254	
1255	4. Choose **Relink**.
1256	
1257	</Steps>
1258	
1259	**Relink** stays off until at least one file is located, then applies every choice as one undo step called **Relink Media**. You don't have to locate them all. The ones you skip stay missing, and you can [relink them later](#relink-one-file). **Cancel** changes nothing.
1260	
1261	The sheet is offered once, when the project's window opens, and doesn't appear over another sheet. After that, use the Media tab.
1262	
1263	### Locate one file, find the rest
1264	
1265	Choosing a file also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files, by name. So a shoot moved as one folder is usually found with one **Locate…**.
1266	
1267	Only the folder you pointed at is searched. A row is filled only if a file of that name is there, and a row that already has a file keeps it.
1268	
1269	## Relink one file
1270	
1271	To relink at any time, right-click the file's row on the Media tab, choose **Relink…**, and pick the file in the panel, which reads "Choose the file for “name”."
1272	
1273	This works for any file, missing or not, so you can use it to swap one file for another across every clip that shows it. It's one undo step, **Relink Media**. Thumbnails and waveforms are rebuilt if the new file is a different one, and a file that has only moved keeps them.
1274	
1275	## What Frame Job checks
1276	
1277	Frame Job reads the new file the way it reads an import:
1278	
1279	- **It must be the same kind of file.** You can't relink a movie to a sound file, for example. From the Media tab you get a beep and the reason at the foot of the inspector. In the sheet, the other relinks are applied first and then an alert gives the reason. The row stays as it was either way.
1280	- **It must be readable.** A file Frame Job can't open brings up an alert, and the sheet's other choices still go through.
1281	- **A WebM or MKV is copied as it is on import.** See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). Choosing **Cancel** during the copy leaves that file out of the relink. A file macOS can't open can go through the same [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) as an import.
1282	
1283	## What a relink changes
1284	
1285	The row takes on the new file's duration, size, frame rate, and whether it has audio, video and alpha.
1286	
1287	A clip that runs past the end of a shorter new file is shortened to end with it, on the timeline and inside [nests](/editing/nests/). A clip that starts past the new end is cut down to a single frame. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and everything else about the clip stays as it was.
1288	
1289	A different file is analysed again, so features that use the analysis, such as [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/), wait for the new answers.
1290	
1291	## What a relink keeps
1292	
1293	Some things don't come from the new file, so here's what happens to each:
1294	
1295	| What | After a relink |
1296	| --- | --- |
1297	| [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) | Kept. It's your reading of the footage, which a new path doesn't change. |
1298	| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) | Kept. The peak is read only at import, so set it by hand if the new file differs. |
1299	| [Cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) | The one beside the new movie is taken. If there's none, the existing one stays, as long as it's still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file. |
1300	| Saved speech, for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) | What still fits in the new file is kept. A new file with no sound forgets it. |
1301	
1302	## Good to know
1303	
1304	- A file in the Trash isn't missing yet. Frame Job follows it there and keeps playing it until you empty the Trash.
1305	- A project opened from a consolidated package that has moved finds its own copies, with no sheet. See [Move a consolidated package](/projects/consolidate-media/#move-a-consolidated-package).
1306	- If a WebM or MKV copy has gone but the original is still there, Frame Job makes the copy again when the project opens. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
1307	- A relink stores what Frame Job needs to follow the file, so the next move is followed too.
1308	- You can relink with a nest open. The change still applies to the whole project.
1309	
1310	## With an agent
1311	
1312	`get_project` lists the files that need relinking under `missing_media`, and `relink_media` points one at a new path, with the same checks. It makes the bookmark that follows the file for you, or takes one you pass. It works on one file at a time and doesn't search a folder. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

1326	
1327	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1328	
1329	Removing media takes a file off the project's list. It never touches the file on your disk, and one undo brings it back.

1332	  where="Right-click a row on the Media tab ▸ Remove"

1335	
1336	## Remove a file
1337	
1338	Right-click the file's row on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) and choose **Remove**.
1339	
1340	If no clip uses the file, it goes at once, with no question, as one undo step called **Remove Media**.
1341	
1342	To see what you can remove without losing a clip, tick [Unused only](/projects/media-tab/#unused-only) first.
1343	
1344	## Remove a file clips use
1345	
1346	If clips use the file, Frame Job asks first, because a clip can't stay in a project without its file. The alert reads "Remove “name”? It is used by 3 clips, which will be removed with it."
1347	
1348	- **Remove and Delete Clips** removes the file and those clips as one undo step.
1349	- **Cancel** changes nothing.
1350	
1351	The count covers the whole project, including clips inside [nests](/editing/nests/), even while a nest is open. The clips go from wherever they are:
1352	
1353	- Clips on the timeline leave their time empty. The clips around them don't move.
1354	- Clips inside a nest go from the nest. The nest itself stays, with everything else in it.
1355	
1356	If you'd rather keep the clips and use another file, [relink](/projects/relink-media/#relink-one-file) instead.
1357	
1358	## What stays on disk
1359	
1360	Remove never deletes a file:
1361	
1362	- Your original stays where it is.
1363	- A copy in the project's package, from [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/), stays in the package's `media` folder.
1364	- A movie copy Frame Job made of a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) stays in its Rewrapped folder.
1365	
1366	## Good to know
1367	
1368	- Removing a LUT works differently: its clips stay and lose their look, and the alert's button reads **Remove and Clear Looks**. See [Remove a LUT in use](/color/luts/#remove-a-lut-in-use).
1369	- If a clip's [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) follows the file you remove, Hide While Silent turns off on that clip. The clip stays.
1370	- You can remove a file with a nest open. It still comes out of the whole project.
1371	
1372	## With an agent
1373	
1374	`remove_media` doesn't ask. It won't remove a file that clips still use unless the call passes `with_clips: true`, which takes those clips too. Without it, the call stops and names the clips in the way. For a LUT, `with_clips` clears the looks and Camera Logs that name it and keeps the clips. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

1386	description: "Save a project as a .framejob package, let it autosave, make a copy, go back to an earlier version, and close it without losing work."
1387	---
1388	
1389	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1390	
1391	A project lives in a `.framejob` package. Save it once and Frame Job keeps the package up to date as you work, so most of these commands are about where the project lives and how to go back.
1392	
1393	<AtAGlance
1394	  menu={['File ▸ Save', 'File ▸ Duplicate', 'File ▸ Save As…', 'File ▸ Revert To ▸', 'File ▸ Rename…', 'File ▸ Move To…', 'File ▸ Share', 'File ▸ Close']}
1395	  keys={['⌘S', '⇧⌘S', '⌥⇧⌘S', '⌘W']}
1396	  tools={['save_project', 'close_project']}
1397	/>
1398	
1399	## Save a project
1400	
1401	Press <kbd>⌘S</kbd> or choose **File ▸ Save**. An untitled project asks for a name and a place first. After that, a save writes straight to the package.
1402	
1403	A project built around an opened movie, sound file or picture is untitled too. Its save panel opens in that file's folder with the file's name filled in, and the save writes a new package beside the file. It never writes over the file itself.
1404	
1405	The window's subtitle tells you where you stand. It reads, for example, `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · edited` while there are changes that haven't been written, and the word `edited` goes when they have. macOS also shows **Edited** beside the title, and the close button shows no dot.
1406	
1407	## Autosave
1408	
1409	Once a project has been saved, it autosaves in place, the macOS way: your changes are written to the package as you work, and you don't need to press <kbd>⌘S</kbd>. A project that has never been saved has no package to write to, so save it first.
1410	
1411	Because projects autosave, macOS adds its standard document commands to the **File** menu: **Duplicate**, **Rename…**, **Move To…**, **Revert To ▸** and **Share**.
1412	
1413	## Crash-safe writes
1414	
1415	Every save, autosaves included, writes the new package beside the old one and then swaps it in. A crash part-way through a save can't leave you with half a package.
1416	
1417	## Make a copy
1418	
1419	| Command | Key | What it does |
1420	| --- | --- | --- |
1421	| **File ▸ Duplicate** | <kbd>⇧⌘S</kbd> | Opens a copy of the project as a new untitled project. The original stays open as it was. |
1422	| **File ▸ Save As…** | <kbd>⌥⇧⌘S</kbd> | Writes the project to a new package, and the window carries on in it. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> with the **File** menu open and **Duplicate** becomes **Save As…**. |
1423	
1424	## Revert to an earlier version
1425	
1426	**File ▸ Revert To ▸** goes back to the last saved version, or lets you browse earlier versions of the package. It has no key.
1427	
1428	Going back throws away the changes made since that version. The playhead returns to the start, and the selection and the in/out range are cleared.
1429	
1430	## Rename or move a project
1431	
1432	| Command | What it does |
1433	| --- | --- |
1434	| **File ▸ Rename…** | Renames the project's package. |
1435	| **File ▸ Move To…** | Moves the project's package to another folder. |
1436	
1437	Click the window's title for the same two controls.
1438	
1439	Both act on the package alone. Footage the project points at stays where it is, unless you've copied it in with [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).
1440	
1441	## Share a project
1442	
1443	**File ▸ Share** opens the macOS Share menu for the project.
1444	
1445	:::note
1446	A package doesn't hold your footage until you've run [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/). Without that, whoever receives it sees a project with missing media.
1447	:::
1448	
1449	## Close a project
1450	
1451	Press <kbd>⌘W</kbd> or choose **File ▸ Close**. What happens depends on the project.
1452	
1453	| The project is | What Close does |
1454	| --- | --- |
1455	| Saved | Writes any changes and closes without asking. |
1456	| Untitled, with changes | Asks whether to save first. |
1457	| Built around an opened movie, sound file or picture | Asks whether to save first, even if you've changed nothing. It always counts as an untitled project with changes. |
1458	| Untitled, with no changes | Closes without asking. |
1459	
1460	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> with the **File** menu open and **Close** becomes **Close All** (<kbd>⌥⌘W</kbd>).
1461	
1462	## A project saves only as a package
1463	
1464	A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. **File ▸ Save** can't make a movie or a still. Those are separate steps: see [the export sheet](/export/export-sheet/). What a package holds is on [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
1465	
1466	## With an agent
1467	
1468	- `save_project` finishes only once the package is on disk. It needs a path the first time, and passing a path later writes there, as **Save As…** does. There's no tool for **Duplicate**.
1469	- `save_project` won't write to a path another open project holds, so close that project first. It won't write to a path a window is still opening either: call it again once the window has opened, or pass another path.
1470	- `get_project` reports `unsaved_changes`, so an agent can see whether anything is still unwritten.
1471	- `close_project` writes nothing. Where **Close** would save a project's changes, the tool leaves the project open unless you pass `discard`, which loses them. It also leaves a window open while a sheet is up. Once a project is closed, a call naming its path fails until the project is opened again.
1472	- The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) asks you before it saves, and it can't close a project, because that would close the window its conversation lives in.
1473	
1474	See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

If you'd rather start empty, **New Project** gives you a blank one. To open a project you've already saved, see [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).

1498	
1499	## Open a movie
1500	
1501	Any of these does the same thing:
1502	
1503	- Choose **File ▸ Open…** (<kbd>⌘O</kbd>), or **Open Video…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/), and pick the file.
1504	- In the Finder, choose **Open With ▸ Frame Job**.
1505	- Double-click the file, once you've made Frame Job the default app for that file type.
1506	- [Drop the file](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them) on the Dock icon or on a Frame Job window.
1507	
1508	Frame Job appears under **Open With** for movies and for M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files, but it doesn't take over their double-click unless you make it the default.
1509	
1510	You get an untitled project with the movie as its first media file and its first clip, at the very start of Track 1. The window is named after the file, so `Interview.mov` opens as "Interview".
1511	
1512	A WebM or MKV file is [copied into a movie](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) first. A file macOS can't open may still come in [through ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), if you have it installed.
1513	
1514	## Open a sound file
1515	
1516	Open a sound file the same way. A sound file has no picture to take a size from, so its project is 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, with the sound as the first clip on Track 1. A movie file that holds only sound gets the same project.
1517	
1518	## Open a picture
1519	
1520	Open a PNG, JPEG or HEIC the same way. The project takes the picture's pixel size, runs at 30 fps, and holds the picture as a 5-second clip on Track 1.
1521	
1522	## The size and rate you get
1523	
1524	| You open | Canvas size | Frame rate | First clip |
1525	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1526	| A movie | The size it displays at | The file's exact rate | The whole movie |
1527	| A sound file | 1920 × 1080 | 30 fps | The whole sound |
1528	| A picture | Its pixel size | 30 fps | 5 seconds of the picture |
1529	
1530	### Display size
1531	
1532	A project built from a movie uses the size the movie displays at, after the file's rotation. A portrait phone clip opens as 1080 × 1920, not sideways.
1533	
1534	An odd-sized movie keeps its size, even though a canvas size you type must be even. Once you change either canvas field, both sides have to be even. See [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/).
1535	
1536	### Exact frame rate
1537	
1538	The rate is read from the file and never rounded to a neighbour, so 29.97 stays 29.97 and 23.976 stays 23.976.
1539	
1540	A file's rate is matched to a standard rate if it's within 0.01 fps of one: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60. Any other rate is kept to three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48. A movie that reports no usable rate opens at 30 fps.
1541	
1542	Every file you [add to a project](/projects/import-media/) is read the same way. To change the project's rate later, see [Project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/).
1543	
1544	## Start a blank project
1545	
1546	Choose **File ▸ New Project** (<kbd>⌘N</kbd>), or **New Project** on the Welcome window. A blank project opens at once, with no dialog, in a window titled "Untitled Project". It's 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, with one empty track.
1547	
1548	**New Project** is always available, whether or not another project is open. Change the size and rate afterwards on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).
1549	
1550	## Save it for the first time
1551	
1552	A project made from a file exists only in its window until you save it. It opens already marked as changed, so closing it asks whether to save, even if you've done nothing to it yet.
1553	
1554	The first **File ▸ Save** (<kbd>⌘S</kbd>) offers to put the project next to the source file, under the source's name: the save panel opens in that file's folder, with the file's name and no extension. `Interview.mov` becomes `Interview.framejob` beside it, unless you choose otherwise.
1555	
1556	Saving never writes over the source file. A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. See [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/).
1557	
1558	## With an agent
1559	
1560	`open_project` does what opening a file does here, and `new_project` makes the same blank project.
1561	
1562	`new_project` can save the blank project at a path straight away, adding `.framejob` if the path lacks it. It won't use a path another open project holds, or one a window is still opening, and then nothing is created. Close the other project first. Without a path the project stays an untitled draft until `save_project`. Change the size and rate afterwards with `set_canvas`. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).
1563

1572	=================== projects/webm-and-matroska.mdx
1573	---
1574	title: "WebM and Matroska files"
1575	description: "How Frame Job brings in .webm and .mkv files by copying their streams into a movie, what the copy can carry, and where the copies live."
1576	---
1577	
1578	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1579	
1580	macOS won't open a WebM or MKV file directly, so Frame Job copies its video and sound into a QuickTime movie the first time you bring one in. Nothing is re-encoded, so no quality is lost, and your original stays where it is.
1581	
1582	<AtAGlance
1583	  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…']}
1584	  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
1585	  where="Drag to the Media tab"
1586	  tools={['import_media', 'open_project', 'relink_media']}
1587	/>
1588	
1589	## How a file is rewrapped
1590	
1591	Rewrapping means moving a file's video and sound streams into a different container without changing them. Add, open or relink the file as you would any other. There's no question to answer: the copy starts by itself, and the clip then plays from the copy.
1592	
1593	Frame Job recognises these files by what's inside them, not by their name, so a Matroska file with the wrong extension still imports when you drop it on the Media tab, unless that extension is a picture's or `.cube`.
1594	
1595	| Stream | What the copy carries |
1596	| --- | --- |
1597	| Video | VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC |
1598	| Sound | Opus, Vorbis or AAC |
1599	
1600	Only the first video track and the first audio track are copied. Any other track, such as a second language or subtitles, stays behind in the original.
1601	
1602	If the end of the file is damaged or cut short, the copy holds everything up to that point.
1603	
1604	Some video can't come in because this Mac can't decode it: VP8, AV1 on a Mac without a hardware decoder, and VP9 Profile 1 or 3. Nothing is copied, and the alert says why. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
1605	
1606	## The name in the Media tab
1607	
1608	The media keeps the original's name. Hover over its row in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) and the tooltip gives the original's path and says the file was copied into Frame Job's Rewrapped folder.
1609	
1610	## The Copying Movie window
1611	
1612	A copy that takes more than a second shows a small **Copying Movie** window, with a progress bar and how much has been copied, such as "412 MB of 1.2 GB". It reads "Reading the file…" until the copy starts.
1613	
1614	Choose **Cancel** to stop. The copy stops, nothing is added, no alert appears and no partial file is left behind. If you were opening the file with **File ▸ Open…**, no project opens. If you were adding several files, the others carry on.
1615	
1616	The window never takes the keyboard from a Frame Job window, so you can keep editing while it runs. Copies happen one at a time.
1617	
1618	## Free space
1619	
1620	Before copying, Frame Job checks that the disk has room. If it doesn't, nothing is copied and the alert says what's needed:
1621	
1622	> Not enough free space to open *file*: its video and sound need about *size* on “*volume*”, which has *size* free. Nothing was copied.
1623	
1624	If Frame Job can't read how much space the volume has, the copy goes ahead.
1625	
1626	## The Rewrapped folder
1627	
1628	Copies live in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, which all your projects share. Importing the same file again uses its copy instead of making another, even in a different project. If the original has changed, Frame Job makes a new copy.
1629	
1630	Frame Job doesn't clear this folder, so copies pile up. You can clear it yourself:
1631	
1632	- WebM and MKV copies are made again the next time a project that uses them opens, as long as the original is still there.
1633	- [ffmpeg conversions](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#a-lost-conversion-stays-missing) live here too, and they aren't made again. Their media stays missing until you relink it.
1634	
1635	[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies the movie, not the WebM, into the package. The row's tooltip then says it was copied into this project's package.
1636	
1637	## Streams the copy can't carry
1638	
1639	If a stream is in a codec the copy can't carry, the file isn't added, and an alert names the stream, for example:
1640	
1641	> *file* has FLAC audio, which Frame Job cannot copy out of a WebM or Matroska file.
1642	
1643	This applies to FLAC, MP3, MP2, AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, TrueHD and PCM sound, Vorbis whose headers can't be read, and MPEG-2, MPEG-4 Part 2, Theora and ProRes video. A codec without a familiar name appears under its Matroska codec ID. A compressed or encrypted track stops the import the same way: "*file* has a compressed or encrypted video track, which Frame Job cannot copy out of a WebM or Matroska file."
1644	
1645	If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job then offers to help. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/). Without it, the file isn't added.
1646	
1647	## Colour is kept
1648	
1649	The copy keeps the colour the file states: HLG, HDR10 (PQ), or a BT.709, BT.601 or BT.2020 SDR picture. Frame Job reads it from the file's colour information or, for VP9, from the video itself. HDR10 metadata carries over.
1650	
1651	A file that states no colour is shown as macOS reads it.
1652	
1653	## If a copy goes missing
1654	
1655	If a copy is deleted or moved to the Trash, the project makes it again from the original the next time it opens. The **Copying Movie** window shows as usual.
1656	
1657	This needs the original to be in place and still be a WebM or Matroska file. If that copy is cancelled or fails, a deleted copy shows as missing, with a slate, the **missing** badge and **Relink…**, and a copy in the Trash goes on playing from the Trash. The next open tries again.
1658	
1659	## With an agent
1660	
1661	An agent's import shows no window and waits for the copy to finish. `import_media` gives the copy as `path` and the file you asked for as `original`. If the copy can't carry a stream, an agent doesn't get the ffmpeg question: see [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#with-an-agent).
1662	
1663	## Related
1664	
1665	- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
1666	- [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/)
1667	- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)
1668	- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)

1671	---
1672	title: The Welcome window
1673	description: Use the window Frame Job shows when nothing is open to open a file, start a project or a recording, or reopen something recent.
1674	---
1675	
1676	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1677	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
1678	
1679	The Welcome window is where you start when no project is open. It offers the ways in and your recent projects, and it takes dropped files.
1680	
1681	<AtAGlance
1682	  where={['Shown when Frame Job starts with nothing to open', 'Shown when you click the Dock icon with no window open']}
1683	  tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'record_screen']}
1684	/>
1685	
1686	<Shot
1687	  name="01-welcome.window"
1688	  alt="The Welcome window: the Frame Job mark and name, the line Open a file. Start cutting., a note about what opening a movie does, the buttons Open Video…, New Project and New Recording…, and a line of file types at the foot."
1689	/>
1690	
1691	## Start something
1692	
1693	| Button | What it does |
1694	| --- | --- |
1695	| **Open Video…** | Shows the same open panel as **File ▸ Open…**. A movie becomes an untitled project at its own size and rate, with the file as the first clip on Track 1. Despite the name it also opens sound files, pictures and saved `.framejob` projects. |
1696	| **New Project** | Starts a blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project. |
1697	| **New Recording…** | Opens the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), with no project needed. |
1698	
1699	**New Recording…** never stops a recording, unlike the **File** menu item, which reads **Stop Recording** while one runs. During a screen recording, when the recorder panel is hidden, it only beeps. During a camera or microphone-only recording it shows the panel again.
1700	
1701	For what you get from each, see [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/).
1702	
1703	## Reopen a recent project
1704	
1705	Under the buttons, **Recent** lists up to five recent documents by name, most recent first. Click one to reopen it. Hover over a row to see its full path.
1706	
1707	The heading and the list disappear when there's nothing recent. [**File ▸ Open Recent**](/projects/open-a-project/#open-a-recent-project) keeps the same list, so **Clear Menu** empties this one too, the next time the window opens.
1708	
1709	## Drop files on it
1710	
1711	Drag a file or a project from the Finder and drop it anywhere on the window. Each file opens as its own document, so several files make several projects.
1712	
1713	The window takes `.framejob` projects and the movie, sound and picture types **File ▸ Open…** lists, and ignores anything else. The line at the foot of the window names the common ones: MOV · MP4 · M4V · M4A · MP3 · WAV · AIFF · PNG · JPEG · HEIC.
1714	
1715	## When it appears and goes away
1716	
1717	Frame Job shows the Welcome window when it starts with nothing to open, and when you click its Dock icon with no window open. It closes itself as soon as a project window comes up.
1718	
1719	Closing the last project doesn't bring it back on its own, and Frame Job keeps running. Click the Dock icon to see it again.
1720	
1721	The window is a fixed 720 × 600 and can't be resized.
1722	
1723	## Related
1724	
1725	- [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/)

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Assistant is a conversation with Claude, built into the inspector of every editor window. You ask in plain words, and it reads and edits that window's project.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌃⌘A"
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
  needs="Your own Anthropic API key. Without one, the tab says how to add it."

## The Assistant tab

You might ask:

- "trim the pauses out of the interview"
- "put a title over the first five seconds"
- "what is under the playhead?"

The Assistant uses the same tools an agent uses over MCP, less a few held back from it, so its edits are ordinary edits. You watch each change land, and each one is its own undo step. See [What the Assistant can do](/assistant/what-it-can-do/).

It's the fifth inspector tab, after **Clip**, **Media**, **Document** and **Transcript**. Before your first message, [save your key](/assistant/set-up/).

## Open the Assistant

Choose **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>). Frame Job shows the inspector if it was hidden, switches to the Assistant tab and puts the cursor in the message field.

It isn't a toggle. Pressed while the tab is already showing, it only puts the cursor back in the field.

The command stays enabled with no key, so the tab can [say what's needed](/assistant/set-up/#the-no-key-prompt). There's no message field to put the cursor in until then.

## The tab's layout

From top to bottom:

| Part | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Context** | How full the conversation is, with [**Clear**](#clear-the-conversation) (↺) at its right end. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/). |

---
title: Troubleshooting
description: Find out why a command is greyed, an edit is refused, a file won't open, a clip is silent or an export stops, and what to do next.
---

Frame Job says why it won't do something, in a sentence or a tooltip. This page starts from what you see and tells you what it means and what to do. For the numbers behind these answers, see [Limits](/reference/limits/).

## A command is greyed out

Every menu item has a rule for when it's on. [Menus](/reference/menus/) and [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/) give each item's rule. A ⌘ shortcut does nothing while its item is greyed.

If the item should be on, check these first:

| Check | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| The selection | Many commands need a clip selected, or a certain kind of clip. |
| A sheet | While a sheet is open, every editor command is off. Close the sheet first. |
| A nest | With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these are off: **New Project from Range…**, **Make Vertical Version…**, **Rename Graphic…**, **Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker**, **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** and **Text Behind Subject**. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. |
| A text field | **Open Nest**, **Close Nest**, **Delete** and **Ripple Delete** are off while you type, because their keys edit the text. |
| A key | A command that needs your own key stays in the menu, greyed, and its title ends "(needs your AssemblyAI key)". Rest the pointer on it to see which key and where to set it. Saving the key turns it on at once. See [A feature asks for a key](#a-feature-asks-for-a-key). |

## A key does nothing

Single-letter keys and the arrow keys belong to the editor window, and they stand down in two cases.

- **You're typing in a field.** Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click outside the field, to give the keys back to the editor.

65	</Steps>
66	
67	The field empties once the message is taken, and the reply arrives in the transcript. Everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply is called a turn.
68	
69	The field starts one line high, grows to five lines as you type, and scrolls past that. Spaces and blank lines at either end are dropped, and a message of nothing else does nothing.
70	
71	You can type your next message while the Assistant works, but you can't send it until the turn ends.
72	
73	## Message field keys
74	
75	| Key | In the message field |
76	| --- | --- |
77	| <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | Sends the message and gives the keys back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays while the Assistant works. While it's working or waiting for your answer, this beeps instead and the field keeps the keys. |
78	| <kbd>⇧↩</kbd>, <kbd>⌘↩</kbd>, <kbd>⌥↩</kbd> or <kbd>⌃↩</kbd> | Starts a new line |
79	| <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>⇧Tab</kbd> | Gives the keys back to the editor and never types a tab. With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, moves to the next or previous control. |
80	| <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> | Undo and redo your typing |
81	
82	Clicking **Send** gives the keys back the same way <kbd>↩</kbd> does, and so does clicking anywhere else in the window below its title bar. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/#start-and-finish-typing).
83	
84	Your typing never lands on the project's undo stack, and sending a message drops the field's own undo history. While the keys are in the field, <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> only undoes typing. Outside the field, it takes back the Assistant's last edit.
85	
86	<kbd>↩</kbd> never answers a question and never stops a turn. While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> belongs to it.
87	
88	## If a message cannot be sent
89	
90	If the conversation can't start, the reason appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the field. Your message isn't added to the transcript, so you can send it again once the cause is fixed.
91	
92	The usual causes are [a missing key](/assistant/set-up/#the-no-key-prompt) and [a helper that won't start](/assistant/set-up/#if-the-helper-is-missing).
93	
94	## Send becomes Stop
95	
96	The button reads **Send**, with the tooltip "Send the message". While a turn is running or waiting on you, it reads **Stop**, with the tooltip "Stop the turn".
97	
98	**Stop** is a click. It has no shortcut. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/).
99	
100	## What each message carries
101	
102	Each message starts with a short block describing your window at the moment you sent it, so "this clip" and "the selected titles" mean what you'd expect. The block holds:
103	
104	- the project's name, and its path, or a note that it's never been saved
105	- the nest open in the window, if there is one, or that the timeline is open
106	- the playhead's position
107	- the ids of the selected clips
108	
109	You don't see the block in the transcript, but it goes to Anthropic with your message. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).
110	
111	It isn't updated during the turn. The Assistant is told to read the project again after its own edits.
112	
113	## One conversation per window
114	
115	Each editor window has its own conversation, about that window's project. Closing the window ends the conversation and [declines](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining) any question waiting for your answer.
116	
117	Conversations aren't saved with the project, so reopening it starts with an empty transcript.
118	
119	The Assistant can't close its own window. You do that with **File ▸ Close** (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>).
120	
121	## Clear the conversation
122	
123	Click **Clear** (↺, "Clear the conversation") at the right end of **Context**. It ends the conversation and empties the transcript, and your next message starts a fresh one.
124	
125	- **Spend** goes back to "Nothing yet".
126	- The context meter keeps the model's window size, so after a conversation it reads "0 of … tokens · 0%", with that size in place of the dots, until the next response.
127	- Clear asks for no confirmation. It ends a running turn and declines a waiting question.
128	
129	The project is untouched. Edits already made stay, each still its own undo step.
130

139	---
140	title: "Long conversations"
141	description: Watch how much of the model's memory a conversation uses, and keep a long one going with compaction and tool result clearing.
142	---
143	
144	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
145	
146	A conversation with the Assistant grows with every message, tool result and rendered frame, and the model can only hold so much of it at once. That limit is its context window, measured in tokens, the small pieces of text a model counts in. The Context meter shows how full it is, and two settings keep a long conversation going.
147	
148	<AtAGlance
149	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
150	  keys="⌘,"
151	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Context"
152	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
153	/>
154	
155	## The context meter
156	
157	The **Context** row at the top of the Assistant tab shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response.
158	
159	| The row reads | When |
160	| --- | --- |
161	| "Nothing reported yet" | Before your first message in this window. |
162	| "12,000 of 200,000 tokens · 6%" | Once the model's window is known. The percentage shows at most one decimal. It can read "0 of …" for a moment after your first message, before the first response. |
163	| "12,000 tokens (window size unknown)" | Anthropic didn't report the window size. |
164	
165	When the inspector is narrow the figure shortens to "12,000 / 200,000 · 6%" or "6%", or to "12,000 tokens" with no known window. The tooltip always has the full figure.
166	
167	The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns coral past 80%.
168	
169	**Clear** (↺), at the end of the row, puts the count back to zero, and so does a change of key or model, because each ends the conversation.
170	
171	## The settings
172	
173	Both settings are in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**. A change applies without **Save** and keeps the conversation going. A new threshold counts from the end of the current turn, and a change to clearing applies from your next message.
174	
175	| Setting | What it does | Default | Range |
176	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
177	| **Compact when context reaches** … **tokens** | Replaces the conversation with a summary at the end of a turn. | On, 300,000 tokens | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens |
178	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop older tool results from what the model sees. | Off | |
179	
180	The token field is dimmed while **Compact when context reaches** is off. A number outside the range beeps, and the field goes back to the stored value.
181	
182	## Compaction
183	
184	With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is replaced by a summary at the end of the first turn that reaches the threshold. It never happens in the middle of a turn, and a [stopped](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) turn doesn't compact.
185	
186	The summary is asked to keep:
187	
188	- what you asked for and every preference you stated
189	- the project and any nest open
190	- the clips, tracks, markers and media involved
191	- the edits made, in order, and which were undone
192	- what's still open or was promised
193	
194	Rendered frames don't survive, so the summary describes in words what each one showed. The Assistant renders again when it needs to look.
195	
196	The transcript notes each step:
197	
198	| The transcript says | What it means |
199	| --- | --- |
200	| "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" | The summary has been asked for. |
201	| "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look." | It worked. The Context meter drops to about *M*. |
202	| "Compaction didn't finish (*reason*); it will try again after the next turn." | No summary came back. The conversation is unchanged. |
203	
204	The summary request is priced like any other response, and it's part of that turn's [`Cost:` line](/assistant/cost/#per-turn).
205	
206	:::tip
207	Compaction only starts once the conversation reaches the threshold, so the threshold has to be lower than the model's window. If the Context meter shows a window smaller than your threshold, lower it.
208	:::
209	
210	## With compaction off
211	
212	Nothing replaces the conversation, so it keeps growing until it fills the model's window. From then on each message fails, with an [error in the transcript](/assistant/conversation/#errors), until you click **Clear**. **Clear** ends the conversation, and nothing of it carries into the next message.
213	
214	## Clearing old tool results
215	
216	A tool result is what comes back from one of the Assistant's tool calls, and a project's details can run long. With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older ones from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It's a lighter step than compaction: the conversation stays, and only old tool results go.
217	
218	- It keeps the five most recent tool uses.
219	- It clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time.
220	- It can happen in the middle of a turn.
221	- It never clears tool search results, which are how the Assistant finds its tools.
222	
223	Each clearing adds a note to the transcript, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view." The model may have to fetch something again afterwards.
224	
225	Each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write: Anthropic can't reuse its stored copy of the conversation, so it stores a new one, and that goes on your bill. That's why it clears in large pieces.
226
