317	---
318	title: "Where Frame Job keeps its files"
319	description: "Find your API keys, spend ledger, export presets, converted movies, recordings and projects on your Mac, and see how Frame Job protects your keys."
320	---
321	
322	Frame Job keeps its own data in one folder in your Library and your recordings in your Movies folder. Projects live wherever you save them. Use this page when you want to back something up, clear something out, or check what's stored on your Mac.
323	
324	## What's where
325	
326	In this table, `…/Frame Job/` is short for `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`.
327	
328	| Path | What it is |
329	| --- | --- |
330	| `…/Frame Job/assemblyai-key` | Your [AssemblyAI key](#key-files) |
331	| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-key` | Your [Anthropic key](#key-files) |
332	| `…/Frame Job/spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](#the-spend-ledger) |
333	| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json` | The Assistant's [cached price table](#the-spend-ledger) |
334	| `…/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json` | Your [named export presets](#export-presets) |
335	| `…/Frame Job/Rewrapped/` | [Movies Frame Job copied or converted](#rewrapped-copies) from files macOS could not open |
336	| `…/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock` | The [local socket](#the-agent-socket) AI agents connect through |
337	| `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` | [Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs](#recordings) |
338	| Wherever you save them | [Projects](#projects), as `.framejob` packages |
339	| The `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` preferences domain | [View settings and other remembered choices](#preferences) |
340	| macOS's temporary folder | [Files Frame Job can make again](#temporary-files) |
341	
342	## The Application Support folder
343	
344	Frame Job's own folder is `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. The Finder hides your Library, so to open it choose **Go ▸ Go to Folder…** in the Finder and paste the path.
345	
346	Frame Job makes the folder when something first needs it, and each folder under it only when there's something to put there. You won't find empty folders for features you've never used.
347	
348	Each folder it makes has mode `0700`, so only your user account can open it. If you've already set a folder's permissions yourself, Frame Job leaves them alone.
349	
350	## Key files
351	
352	Your keys are two files in that folder:
353	
354	| File | What it holds |
355	| --- | --- |
356	| `assemblyai-key` | Your AssemblyAI key, for cloud transcription. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/). |
357	| `anthropic-key` | Your Anthropic key, for the Assistant. It goes to the Assistant's helper, the background program that talks to Anthropic, when a conversation starts, and nowhere else. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/). |
358	
359	Save, replace and remove keys in [Settings](/reference/settings/). A file that's empty, or holds only spaces, counts as no key.
360	
361	## How keys are stored
362	
363	Each key is a plain file that only your user account can read or write (mode `0600`). It's written to a temporary name and renamed into place, so it never exists with looser permissions and is never half-written.
364	
365	A key is never:
366	
367	- put in macOS preferences
368	- logged
369	- passed as a launch argument
370	- passed to an agent tool, or returned by one
371	- shown in the Settings window again
372	
373	:::caution
374	Frame Job doesn't use the Keychain. Anything running as your user account can read these files, so treat your Mac account as the protection.
375	:::
376	
377	## Keys from the environment
378	
379	If no key is stored, Frame Job falls back to an environment variable. This only helps when you start Frame Job from a shell that sets the variable, because an app opened from the Finder or the Dock doesn't see your shell's variables.
380	
381	| Key | Variable |
382	| --- | --- |
383	| Anthropic (Assistant) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
384	| AssemblyAI (Transcription) | `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` |
385	
386	- A stored key always wins over the variable.
387	- An empty variable counts as no key.
388	- **Verify** in Settings' Transcription section checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or stored. The Assistant section has no **Verify**.
389	- A key from a variable isn't stored, so **Remove** stays dimmed unless you've saved one too.
390	
391	## The spend ledger
392	
393	`spend.jsonl` records one line per Assistant response, with its time, model, token counts and estimated dollars. A response that was cut short is marked as one. The file never holds your key or the conversation, and only your user account can read it.
394	
395	The month's spend in Settings is added up from this file. If Frame Job can't write to it, the conversation carries on and the transcript shows a note saying why.
396	
397	`anthropic-prices.json` is the Assistant's cached copy of the price table it uses for that estimate. It's refreshed at most once a day. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
398	
399	## Export presets
400	
401	Your named export presets are in `ExportPresets.json`. If that file is missing or damaged, the presets list is empty and nothing else is affected. See [Export presets](/export/presets/).
402	
403	## Rewrapped copies
404	
405	The `Rewrapped/` folder holds movies Frame Job made from files macOS could not open: [WebM and MKV copies](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) and [ffmpeg conversions](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/). Your originals stay where they are.
406	
407	A project refers to the file in this folder, not to the original. If Frame Job can't find that file, the media is missing until you [relink](/projects/relink-media/) it.
408	
409	Every project shares this folder, and the only thing Frame Job deletes from it is a copy that turns out not to open, so copies pile up. You can clear it yourself:
410	
411	- WebM and MKV copies are made again from the original the next time a project using them opens, as long as the original is still there.
412	- ffmpeg conversions aren't. That media stays missing until you relink it.
413	
414	[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies a project's rewrapped files into its package, which frees that project from this folder.
415	
416	## The agent socket
417	
418	An AI agent outside Frame Job reaches it through an MCP client, and that client connects through `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`, a local socket Frame Job creates at every launch. See [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/).
419	
420	## Recordings
421	
422	Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs go to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time: `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`, `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33`, or `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. The folder is made when a recording first has something to put in it.
423	
424	See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/) for every file a recording writes.
425	
426	## Projects
427	
428	A project is a `.framejob` package, saved wherever you choose. Each package holds its own caches, so they move with it. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
429	
430	## Preferences
431	
432	View settings and other remembered choices are in the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` preferences domain. Keys are never stored there. See [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/).
433	
434	## Temporary files
435	
436	Files Frame Job can always make again go in macOS's temporary folder, outside any project: the caches of a project you haven't saved yet, and the [48 kHz copies](/reference/file-formats/#any-sample-rate) of sound at other sample rates. You don't need to keep them.
437

446	---
447	title: "The .framejob package"
448	description: "See what a saved project holds, which parts Frame Job can rebuild and which it can't, and what happens when you move or copy a package."
449	---
450	
451	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
452	
453	A Frame Job project is one `.framejob` package: a folder the Finder shows as one file. It holds your edit, its caches and, if you ask for them, copies of your footage.
454	
455	<AtAGlance
456	  menu={['File ▸ Save', 'File ▸ Consolidate Media…']}
457	  keys="⌘S"
458	  tools={['save_project', 'consolidate_media']}
459	/>
460	
461	## What a package is
462	
463	| Inside | What it is | Can Frame Job rebuild it? |
464	| --- | --- | --- |
465	| [`project.json`](#projectjson) | The edit itself | No. A package needs it to open. |
466	| [`cache/`](#cache) | Thumbnails, waveforms, analyses and renders | Yes, though [cloud transcripts](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) cost money. |
467	| [`media/`](#media) | Copies of your footage, only after **Consolidate Media…** | No. It may be the only copy. |
468	| [`graphics/`](#graphics) | Graphic modules, fonts, images and kept versions, only once you add a graphic, font or image | No. |
469	
470	To look inside, Control-click the package in the Finder and choose **Show Package Contents**.
471	
472	A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. A movie or a still is a separate step: see [Export](/export/formats/) and [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
473	
474	A save writes the new package beside the old one and swaps it in, so a crash part-way through can't leave half a package.
475	
476	:::caution
477	A save keeps only those four things. Any other file you put inside a package is dropped at the next save, autosaves included.
478	:::
479	
480	## `project.json`
481	
482	This is the edit itself: the canvas, media list, tracks, clips and markers. It's the only thing a package needs in order to open.
483	
484	A project from any earlier version of Frame Job opens, and the next save writes it in the current format. A project from a newer build won't open, and the message asks you to update Frame Job. See [Open a project from another version](/projects/open-a-project/#open-a-project-from-another-version).
485	
486	If `project.json` can't be read as text, the message says "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." See [When a project won't open](/projects/open-a-project/#when-a-project-wont-open).
487	
488	## `cache/`
489	
490	Everything here is something Frame Job can rebuild, so a package with a missing or damaged `cache/` still opens and redraws.
491	
492	| Folder | What it holds |
493	| --- | --- |
494	| `thumbs/` | Filmstrip thumbnails |
495	| `peaks/` | Waveforms |
496	| `loudness/` | Loudness measurements |
497	| `speech/` | Voice detection |
498	| `sync/` | The analysis for [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) |
499	| `transcripts/` | [Transcripts from AssemblyAI](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) |
500	| `device-transcripts/` | Words recognised on this Mac |
501	| `analysis/` | [On-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/): shot changes and sound events, faces and subjects found for an agent or drawn by **View ▸ Show Subjects**, and the masks made for an agent or for **Remove Background** |
502	| `reversed/` | [Reversed clips](/speed/reverse/) |
503	| `ramp-audio/` | Sound for [speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/) |
504	| `isolated/` | [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) renders |
505	| `voiced/` | [Voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) renders |
506	
507	The per-file caches build in the background after an open, an import or a relink, and the timeline fills in as they finish. At most two files' sound caches build at a time. A cache that already matches its file is never rebuilt. Analyses and renders are made when something asks for them.
508	
509	Masks can make a package much larger, because they're kept for every frame: a minute of 1080p video's masks take about 62 MB.
510	
511	### Transcripts are worth keeping
512	
513	A transcript from AssemblyAI costs money to make again, so treat `cache/transcripts/` as worth keeping. Everything else in `cache/` rebuilds for nothing but time.
514	
515	## `media/`
516	
517	This folder exists only after [Consolidate Media…](/projects/consolidate-media/), and it holds copies of your footage. Unlike `cache/`, it may be the only copy, so don't delete it.
518	
519	By default a project doesn't copy your footage. It remembers each file's path and a Finder bookmark, and reads the file from there. The package stays small but depends on the footage staying put. Consolidate Media is how a package comes to hold everything it needs.
520	
521	## `graphics/`
522	
523	This folder exists once you add a [graphic](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/), or a font or image for one. It holds the graphic modules, the small programs that draw each graphic, and these folders:
524	
525	| Folder | What it holds |
526	| --- | --- |
527	| `fonts/` | [Fonts](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
528	| `assets/` | [Images](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
529	| `history/` | The last 10 [kept versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/#kept-versions) of each module, one folder per module |
530	
531	## How a package travels
532	
533	Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps its caches. Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches live in a temporary folder, and the first save copies them in.
534	
535	When you open a package, any media missing from its stored path is looked for in the package's own `media/` folder under the same name. That's what lets you move a consolidated package. A working link is never replaced this way.
536	
537	A referenced file that has moved is often found again through its bookmark. If it isn't, see [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
538	
539	To take a project to another Mac, run Consolidate Media first, so the footage goes with it.

5	---
6	
7	Frame Job says why it won't do something, in a sentence or a tooltip. This page starts from what you see and tells you what it means and what to do. For the numbers behind these answers, see [Limits](/reference/limits/).
8	
9	## A command is greyed out
10	
11	Every menu item has a rule for when it's on. [Menus](/reference/menus/) and [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/) give each item's rule. A ⌘ shortcut does nothing while its item is greyed.
12	
13	If the item should be on, check these first:
14	
15	| Check | Why it matters |
16	| --- | --- |
17	| The selection | Many commands need a clip selected, or a certain kind of clip. |
18	| A sheet | While a sheet is open, every editor command is off. Close the sheet first. |
19	| A nest | With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these are off: **New Project from Range…**, **Make Vertical Version…**, **Rename Graphic…**, **Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker**, **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** and **Text Behind Subject**. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. |
20	| A text field | **Open Nest**, **Close Nest**, **Delete** and **Ripple Delete** are off while you type, because their keys edit the text. |
21	| A key | A command that needs your own key stays in the menu, greyed, and its title ends "(needs your AssemblyAI key)". Rest the pointer on it to see which key and where to set it. Saving the key turns it on at once. See [A feature asks for a key](#a-feature-asks-for-a-key). |
22	
23	## A key does nothing
24	
25	Single-letter keys and the arrow keys belong to the editor window, and they stand down in two cases.
26	
27	- **You're typing in a field.** Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click outside the field, to give the keys back to the editor.
28	- **A sheet is open.** Close it first. In a sheet, <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the default button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> cancels.
29	
30	One more thing can catch you out: with a point selected on a [curve](/color/curves/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point, not the clip.
31	
32	See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/) and [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/).
33	
34	## An edit is refused
35	
36	When the project's rules won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps, nothing changes, and the rule's own sentence appears at the foot of the inspector after "Refused: ":
37	
38	> Refused: clips 4 and 7 would overlap by 120000 ticks, more than half of the shorter clip (100000 ticks)
39	
40	The sentence stays until the project changes or you click it. It's exact rather than friendly. The clip numbers are Frame Job's own, not positions on the timeline, and a [tick](/reference/glossary/#projects-and-the-timeline) is 1/600,000 of a second. So this one says the overlap would be 0.2 s, and half of the shorter clip is 0.17 s.
41	
42	The rules you'll meet most:
43	
44	| Rule | What it means |
45	| --- | --- |
46	| The overlap rule | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip. |
47	| A locked track | Its clips can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled, and you can't insert onto it or close a gap on it. Unlock it with its [lock button](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
48	| The one-frame minimum | Trims and rolls leave a clip at least one frame long. |
49	| The ends of the file | A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. |
50	
51	Two other results look similar:
52	
53	- **A beep with no message** means the edit would have changed nothing, such as a slip already at the end of the footage. No rule was broken.
54	- **An error alert** means Frame Job couldn't use the request at all, such as a value outside its allowed range.
55	
56	During a drag, positions the rules won't allow are skipped, and the clip waits at the last allowed place. Only the drop counts.
57	
58	See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
59	
60	## A project won't open
61	
62	A project that can't be read fails with a message naming the problem, and Frame Job doesn't rewrite the package.
63	
64	| Message | What to do |
65	| --- | --- |
66	| "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." | The project file inside the package is damaged. Open a backup copy if you have one. |
67	| "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it" | A newer Frame Job saved it. [Update Frame Job](/getting-started/updates/). |
68	| "too many clips: 5000 (max 4096)", or the same for tracks, markers or media | The file is past one of the [project limits](/reference/limits/#project-size). |
69	
70	Files that have moved don't stop a project opening, and neither does a damaged `cache/` folder. For moved files, see [Clips show a slate](#clips-show-a-slate). Also see [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).
71	
72	## A file won't import
73	
74	Frame Job tells you which file it couldn't add and why.
75	
76	| Message | What it means |
77	| --- | --- |
78	| "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." | This Mac has no AV1 decoder. |
79	| "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." | Only those two VP9 profiles import. |
80	| "*file* is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode." | This Mac has no decoder for that codec. Other codecs it can't decode get the same sentence with their own name. |
81	| "Could not read *file*." | The file is damaged, or it isn't a format Frame Job reads. |
82	| "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." | The file holds neither. |
83	| "Timed out reading *file*." | The check took longer than 30 seconds, usually because of a stalled network volume. |
84	| "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." | The message names the line of the file and what's wrong with it. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/). |
85	| "Not enough free space to open *file*…" | A WebM or Matroska file needs room for its copy. The sentence says how much. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). |
86	
87	A file in a codec this Mac decodes still imports even when some of its data is damaged.
88	
89	If macOS can't open a file, you can repackage or convert it with your own ffmpeg. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
90	
91	If the **File ▸ Add Media…** panel won't let you choose a file, drop it on the Media tab instead. The panel lists only the common types. See [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).
92	
93	An agent's `import_media` reports these reasons too.
94	
95	## Clips show a slate
96	
97	A project always opens, even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place and show a slate, and their rows in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wear the **missing** badge.
98	
99	When a project opens with files missing, Frame Job offers the **Missing media** sheet once. Choose **Locate…** for a file, then **Relink**. Frame Job also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files by name, so a shoot moved as one folder is usually found in one go. To relink a file later, use **Relink…** on its row in the Media tab. An agent uses `relink_media`.
100	
101	Two other cases show a slate or leave media missing:
102	
103	- A reversed clip shows a slate until its backwards copy has been rendered. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/).
104	- A movie that was moved out of Frame Job's [Rewrapped folder](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#the-rewrapped-folder), where its WebM, MKV and ffmpeg copies live, stays missing until you relink it.
105	
106	See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
107	
108	## A clip is silent
109	
110	Check these in order. A muted clip, a muted track and a track silenced by a solo all draw the waveform faded.
111	
112	| Check | What to do |
113	| --- | --- |
114	| The clip's own sound | The clip may be muted in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/), or its [sound turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/). |
115	| The track's **Mute** | A muted track is silent. Mute wins over Solo, so a track that's muted and soloed stays silent. |
116	| **Solo** on another track | While any track is soloed, the others are silent, even if the soloed track has nothing on it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). |
117	| The clip's rate | Above ×12 a clip has no sound, and the Speed section says "Audio is silent above ×12". On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/). |
118	| Whether its sound has rendered | A ramp's sound, and a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, is silent in the preview until its render finishes. A failed render stays failed until the clip's timing changes or you reopen Frame Job. |
119	| **Detach Audio** | After a detach, the picture clip's own sound is off, and the sound is on its linked clip. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). |
120	
121	If the clip plays but [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) or a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) has gone, check its speed. Both play only at normal speed, so a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame plays without them.
122	
123	## An export won't start or stops
124	
125	An export that fails says why and leaves no finished file. An agent reads the same reason from `export_status`.
126	
127	While the timeline is empty, **File ▸ Export…** is greyed out. Add a clip first.
128	
129	"Preparing…" is a wait, not a stall. An export waits for what it has to draw and play first, such as speed-ramp audio, [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) masks, and sound measurements.
130	
131	| What you see | What to do |
132	| --- | --- |
133	| "Clip *N*'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops. Wait for the clip's Status rows to show its loudness, then export again. |
134	| "Clip *N*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | A failed render keeps failing exports until you change the clip's timing or reopen Frame Job. |
135	| "The export was not started: the graphic…" or "The export was stopped at frame *N* of the graphic…" | Frame Job won't export a graphic that can't draw itself. Fix its [module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) and export again. |
136	| "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose [another format](/export/formats/). |
137	| "An animated GIF is limited to 600 frames and this range is *N*." | Shorten the range, or lower the export frame rate. An APNG has the same limit. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/). |
138	| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) won't take a size of a different shape. Use a size from the popup, or one with the same proportions. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |
139	
140	A queued AV1 or VP9 job can sit waiting for memory, so it hasn't stalled. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
141	
142	:::caution
143	Quitting during an **Export…** progress sheet doesn't ask first, and it leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.
144	:::
145	
146	See [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/).
147	
148	## A feature asks for a key
149	
150	Anything that sends your words or your audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.
151	
152	| Message | What to do |
153	| --- | --- |
154	| "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." | Paste a key under **Transcription** in [Settings](/reference/settings/). |
155	| "No Anthropic API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant." | Paste a key under **Assistant** in Settings. |
156	| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The key failed. Check it, and press **Verify** to test it. |
157	
158	A transcript made in one AssemblyAI region can't be seen from the other, so check **Region** too.
159	
160	An agent can't set a key, so a person has to. See [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).
161	
162	## Recording won't start
163	
164	A recording needs macOS's permissions, and Frame Job asks for each one only when you press Record.
165	
166	- **Screen Recording** is at **System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording**. Once it's on, relaunch Frame Job if macOS asks, then press Record again. Later presses without it open that pane.
167	- **Microphone**, **Camera** and **Input Monitoring** are asked for only when the recording needs them.
168	- If you started Frame Job from a terminal or another app, macOS applies that app's permissions. The panel's note names the launching process and how to relaunch.
169	- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, nothing can be recorded until one wakes.
170	
171	An agent's `record_screen` never asks for a permission, so a person has to grant it first. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
172	
173	## An agent can't reach Frame Job
174	
175	Only programs running as you can connect, through the `framejob-mcp` helper inside the app.
176	
177	| What you see | What to do |
178	| --- | --- |
179	| The client can't start the helper after you moved Frame Job | In the **MCP** section of [Settings](/reference/settings/#mcp), press **Copy MCP Command** and register the new path. The path is the one you opened Settings from, and it doesn't follow the app. |
180	| "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job." | The helper isn't in this copy. Use a complete copy of the app. |
181	| "Frame Job did not answer at…" | Frame Job launched but wasn't ready within 60 seconds. Later calls in that client session don't launch another copy, so quit the stray copy and try again. |
182	
183	See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

194	title: Glossary

196	---
197	
198	The words Frame Job uses, in plain terms, each with a link to the page that explains it.
199	
200	## Projects and the timeline
201	
202	- **Action.** An animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).
203	- **Adjustment clip.** A clip with no picture of its own that grades every track behind it. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
204	- **Canvas.** The fixed frame every clip is drawn into. Every export starts from its size. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).
205	- **Clip.** One placed piece on a track: a stretch of a media file, or a text, shape, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
206	- **Current track.** The track of the first selected clip, or with nothing selected the front-most track. Track commands act on it. See [Menus](/reference/menus/).
207	- **Edit point.** A clip's start or end, where <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> stop. See [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
208	- **Frame grid.** The frames of the project's rate. Every time you set lands on one. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
209	- **In–Out range.** The span set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>, which many commands act on. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/).
210	- **Linked pair.** A picture clip and its detached sound, which move, split and ripple together. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
211	- **Media.** A file the project has imported, listed in the Media tab. Clips refer to it. See [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/).
212	- **Nest.** A clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
213	- **No-change edit, or identity.** An edit that was understood and had nothing to change. It beeps, makes no undo step and shows no message. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/#a-beep-with-no-message).
214	- **Package.** A `.framejob` project, a folder the Finder shows as one file. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
215	- **Playhead.** The current time on the timeline. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).
216	- **Refusal.** A rule stopping an edit. Frame Job beeps and shows the rule's sentence after "Refused: " at the foot of the inspector. Nothing changes and no undo step is made. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
217	- **Ripple.** An edit that closes the gap it leaves by moving later clips along. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).
218	- **Selected action.** The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing. While it's chosen, the fields show and write its end state. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
219	- **Tick.** Frame Job's unit of time, 600,000 to the second, which divides every common frame duration exactly. The "Refused: " line and agent tools give lengths in ticks. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
220	- **Track.** A lane of clips. The front track is the top lane, and it's drawn over those behind it. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).
221	
222	## Picture and sound
223	
224	- **Camera Log.** A file's setting saying which camera log curve it holds, so it's converted at the start of the picture. See [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
225	- **Cue.** One timed caption. See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/).
226	- **Cutout.** A clip with Remove Background on. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
227	- **Deep.** A picture with more than 8 bits for each colour component. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
228	- **Ducking.** Lowering a clip's sound under another's. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).
229	- **Dynamic range.** Whether the project works in SDR or HDR (HLG). See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).
230	- **J-cut and L-cut.** The sound of a linked pair starting before, or ending after, its picture. See [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
231	- **Look.** A built-in grade or a `.cube` LUT on a clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/).
232	- **LUFS.** The unit of loudness. See [Normalize](/audio/normalize/).
233	- **LUT.** A colour lookup table in a `.cube` file. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
234	- **Matte.** A track that cuts the track behind it by its alpha or brightness. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).
235	- **Plate.** A clip that fills the canvas behind everything, such as a solid colour or a picture from **Add Background**. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
236	- **Qualifier.** An adjustment clip's pick of the pixels it grades, by hue, saturation and brightness. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
237	- **Ramp.** A speed change over time, a Speed action on the action lane. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).
238	- **Scopes.** The waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram beside the preview. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/).
239	- **Slate.** What a clip draws in place of a picture it doesn't have, such as missing media. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
240	- **Stem.** One track's sound written as its own file beside the mix. See [Audio stems](/export/stems/).
241	- **Transition.** The change from one clip to the next across their overlap on one track. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
242	
243	## Graphics and agents
244	
245	- **Assistant.** The chat in the inspector that edits the open project on your own Anthropic key. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).
246	- **Category.** The list a module is filed under in the Graphic dialog. See [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/).
247	- **Error card.** What a graphic draws in its own box when it can't draw itself. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
248	- **Graphic.** A clip whose picture is drawn by code. It's the clip's content, not an effect. See [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/).
249	- **Graphic package.** A `.fjgraphic` file holding a module and the fonts and pictures it uses. See [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).
250	- **Kept revision.** An earlier text of a module the app kept, the last 10 for each module. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
251	- **MCP.** The protocol an agent uses to drive Frame Job, through the `framejob-mcp` helper. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).
252	- **Module.** A graphic's source, one JavaScript module returning SVG for each frame. See [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/).
253	- **Op.** Short for operation: one edit to a project, applied whole. Most agent tools each make one. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
254	- **Patch.** An object an agent sends holding only the properties it wants to change. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).
255	- **Props.** The values a graphic is drawn with, stored on its clip. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/).
256	- **Template.** A module the app ships, copied into the package when you insert it. See [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/).
257

265	title: "Tools: projects and history"

267	---
268	
269	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
270	
271	These tools work on whole projects: opening, making, saving and closing them, reading one back, and stepping through its undo history. None of them takes `scope`, because none of them edits inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/).
272	
273	<AtAGlance
274	  tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'new_project_from_range', 'save_project', 'close_project', 'get_project', 'undo', 'redo']}
275	/>
276	
277	Every tool takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. A path that names no open project is refused, and so is a call with no project open at all, which is told to call `open_project` or `new_project` first. Times are in ticks, 600,000 per second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/) for how they're written, and [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) for the short `project` summary most answers carry.
278	
279	## `open_project`
280	
281	Opens a project and shows its window, as [double-clicking a file](/projects/open-a-project/) does. It takes a `.framejob` package, or any movie, sound file or picture. A movie, sound file or picture [becomes a new untitled project](/projects/start-a-project/) with its size and frame rate, and the file as the first clip on track 1.
282	
283	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
284	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
285	| `path` | string | Yes | The file to open, as an absolute path or one starting with `~`. |
286	| `project` | string | No | Accepted, and makes no difference, because this call doesn't act on an open project. |
287	
288	It answers the opened project's `project` summary, with `missing_media` in that summary when a file has gone. If the file is already open, Frame Job brings that project forward and answers `already_open: true` with its summary. That includes a movie already open as an untitled project.
289	
290	It's refused when:
291	
292	- nothing exists at `path`
293	- the file can't be read, or doesn't open as a Frame Job project
294	- you're opening the same file in a window and that open hasn't finished after 30 seconds. Call it again once the window is up.
295	
296	A tool call never asks a question, so a file that would normally bring up the [ffmpeg offer](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) is treated as if you'd declined it.
297	
298	## `new_project`
299	
300	Makes a blank 1920×1080, 30 fps project and shows its window, as [**File ▸ New Project**](/projects/start-a-project/#start-a-blank-project) does. Change its size and rate afterwards with [`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
301	
302	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
303	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
304	| `path` | string | No | Where to save it straight away, such as `~/Movies/Cut.framejob`. `.framejob` is added when it's missing. Without a path the project stays an untitled draft until `save_project`. |
305	| `project` | string | No | Accepted, and makes no difference, because this call doesn't act on an open project. |
306	
307	It answers the new project's `project` summary, and `saved`, the full path, when you gave one.
308	
309	A path another open project holds is refused and nothing is created. `close_project` closes that project first. A path a window is still opening is refused the same way. A file on disk that no open project holds is replaced.
310	
311	## `new_project_from_range`
312	
313	Opens a stretch of the top-level timeline as a new project, moved to start at 0, as [**File ▸ New Project from Range…**](/projects/new-project-from-range/) does with the in/out range. The project you take it from doesn't change and gets no undo step.
314	
315	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
316	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
317	| `from` | integer | Yes | Where the range starts on the timeline, in ticks. It's rounded to a frame, and a negative time is taken as 0. |
318	| `to` | integer | Yes | Where the range ends on the timeline, in ticks. The frame at `to` isn't kept. It must be after `from`. |
319	| `path` | string | No | Where to save the new project first. `.framejob` is added when it's missing, and nothing may exist there yet. Without it the project opens untitled, with unsaved changes, named "*name* (range)". |
320	| `project` | string | No | The project to take the range from. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
321	
322	What's kept follows the sheet:
323	
324	- A clip across an edge is cut there, on every track, as [`split`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/) would cut it. Locked tracks are cut too.
325	- A transition across an edge becomes a hard start or end.
326	- Markers inside the range are kept and moved with it.
327	- Media nothing kept plays is left out.
328	- Each kept file's caches come along, so nothing is analysed again, and so do the graphics the kept clips draw, with every font and picture. [What comes with it](/projects/new-project-from-range/#what-comes-with-it) has the list.
329	- Media files are never copied. The new project points at the same files.
330	
331	It answers `project`, the new project's summary, `carried` with the `files`, `bytes` and `seconds` that came along, and `saved`, the path, when you gave one. The new project opens in front, so later calls with no `project` reach it. Name it by its path once it has one.
332	
333	It's refused:
334	
335	- while a nest is open. Call `set_scope` with no arguments first.
336	- when `to` isn't after `from`, once both are on the frame grid
337	- for a path another open project holds, or where anything already exists
338	- for a nest clip across either edge, because a nest clip has no in point and would replay from its start
339	- when nothing plays in the range
340	- when an edge would leave a transition inside the range too long for what's left of its clip. Move that edge further from the transition.
341	
342	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first when the call names a `path`.
343	
344	## `save_project`
345	
346	Saves the project, as [**File ▸ Save**](/projects/save-and-revert/#save-a-project) does, and answers only once the package is on disk.
347	
348	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
349	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
350	| `path` | string | The first time | Where to write the `.framejob` package. `.framejob` is added when it's missing. Giving a path always writes there, as Save As does, unless it's the project's own file, which is a plain save. |
351	| `project` | string | No | The project to save. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
352	
353	A project needs a `path` the first time, whether it came from `new_project` with no path or from a movie opened as a project. After that, leave it out and the project is written back to its own file.
354	
355	It answers `saved`, the full path, and the `project` summary.
356	
357	It's refused when a project that has never been saved has no `path`, and for a path another open project holds. `close_project` closes that one first. A path a window is still opening is refused the same way. A file on disk that no open project holds is replaced. A save that takes more than 120 seconds answers that it timed out.
358	
359	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first.
360	
361	## `close_project`
362	
363	Closes a project and its window, as [**File ▸ Close**](/projects/save-and-revert/#close-a-project) (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>) does. It never writes the package, so call `save_project` first to keep your changes.
364	
365	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
366	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
367	| `discard` | boolean | No | Close even with unsaved changes, losing them. Default `false`. |
368	| `project` | string | No | The project to close. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
369	
370	It answers `ok: true`, `closed` (the project's name), `path` (null for a blank project never saved) and `discarded_changes`, which says whether unsaved changes went with it. A later call naming that path is refused, because it's no longer open.
371	
372	It's refused when the window has a sheet open, whatever `discard` says, and when `get_project` reports `unsaved_changes` and `discard` isn't `true`.
373	
374	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call this tool, because closing the project would close its own conversation.
375	
376	## `get_project`
377	
378	Answers the whole project as JSON, plus what the app holds outside it: the playhead, the selection and the in/out range. Read it first, because every other tool names things by the ids it reports. [Read the project: get_project](/mcp/get-project/) goes through it in full.
379	
380	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
381	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
382	| `project` | string | No | The project to read. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
383	
384	The answer's `project` key is the project itself: `canvas`, `media`, `tracks`, `clips`, `markers`, `nests` and `next_id`. Beside it are `path`, `name`, `unsaved_changes`, `duration`, `playhead`, `selection` and `scope`, then `in_out_range` and `missing_media` when there's something to report, `graphics`, and a `note`. [What it answers](/mcp/get-project/#what-it-answers) explains each one.
385	
386	While a nest is open, `project` is that nest seen as a project. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
387	
388	## `undo`
389	
390	Undoes one step, as [**Edit ▸ Undo**](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/#undo-and-redo) (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) does. Every tool that edits makes exactly one step, so one `undo` walks back exactly one call. The history is the project's, so a step you made by hand counts as well.
391	
392	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
393	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
394	| `project` | string | No | The project to undo in. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
395	
396	It answers `ok: true`, `undone` (the name of the step), `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the `project` summary.
397	
398	It's refused when there's nothing to undo. The tools on [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/) make no step, so they can't be undone.
399	
400	## `redo`
401	
402	Redoes one undone step, as [**Edit ▸ Redo**](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/#undo-and-redo) (<kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>) does. Any new edit clears what there was to redo, as it does in the app.
403	
404	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
405	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
406	| `project` | string | No | The project to redo in. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
407	
408	It answers `ok: true`, `redone` (the name of the step), `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the `project` summary.
409	
410	It's refused when there's nothing to redo.
411

420	=================== mcp/tools-media.mdx
421	---
422	title: "Tools: media"
423	description: The agent tools that bring files into a project, relink and remove them, copy them into the package, and set a file's Camera Log, peak and speech.
424	---
425	
426	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
427	
428	These tools work on the project's media list, the files a project points at. A file on the list isn't on the timeline until a clip uses it. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).
429	
430	<AtAGlance
431	  tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'consolidate_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech']}
432	/>
433	
434	The media list belongs to the whole project, not to a nest, so:
435	
436	- Pass `scope` to `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color` or `set_media_speech`, and the call is refused with "*tool* has no meaning inside nest *id*".
437	- With a nest open and no `scope` passed, those same edits apply to the whole project. All but `add_media` list themselves under `document_ops` in the answer, so you can see they skipped the nest. See [Document edits while a nest is open](/mcp/nests/#document-edits-while-a-nest-is-open).
438	- Media ids mean the same thing everywhere.
439	
440	Every tool here also takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. Each edit is one undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) for the `project` summary and the two ways an edit can fail to happen.
441	
442	The cursor file beside a recording has its own tool, [`set_media_cursor`](/mcp/tools-recording/#set_media_cursor).
443	
444	## `import_media`
445	
446	Reads a movie, sound file, picture or `.cube` LUT and adds it to the media list, as [**File ▸ Add Media…**](/projects/import-media/#add-media) does. It isn't on the timeline yet. Place it with [`add_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).
447	
448	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
449	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
450	| `path` | string | Yes | The file, as an absolute path or one starting with `~`. |
451	| `project` | string | No | The project to add it to. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
452	
453	It answers:
454	
455	| Key | What it is |
456	| --- | --- |
457	| `media` | The new media id. |
458	| `path` | Where the entry points. For a converted file, that's the copy. |
459	| `original` | The file you named, when the entry points at a copy. |
460	| `kind` | `video`, `audio`, `image` or `lut`. |
461	| `duration` | The file's length, in ticks. |
462	| `width`, `height` | Its display size. |
463	| `fps` | Its frame rate, as `[numerator, denominator]`. |
464	| `has_video`, `has_audio`, `has_alpha` | What it holds. |
465	| `note` | What to do next: `add_clip`, or for a LUT, [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/) with a look. |
466	| `project` | The `project` summary. |
467	
468	A [WebM or Matroska file](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) is copied into a `.mov` first and named after the original. A file the [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) converts is recorded the same way.
469	
470	A tool call never asks, so where the app would offer to convert a file with ffmpeg, this answers with the reason instead. Convert it from the app's window, or [set Frame Job to always convert](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#with-an-agent).
471	
472	It's refused when nothing exists at `path`, or when the file can't be read. A file whose path is already on the list changes nothing, and the answer says so. The undo step is called "Add Media".
473	
474	## `add_media`
475	
476	Adds a media entry from a description you supply, with no reading of the file. Use `import_media` unless you're replaying a project's own JSON. Frame Job has no menu item for this tool, because reading the file is the app's job.
477	
478	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
479	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
480	| `descriptor` | object | Yes | The entry to add, as below. |
481	| `scope` | integer | No | Leave it out. Passing it is refused, because this edit has no meaning inside a nest. |
482	| `project` | string | No | The project to add it to. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
483	
484	The descriptor is an element of `media` from `get_project`, without its `id`. Only `path` is required by name.
485	
486	| Key | What it is | Default |
487	| --- | --- | --- |
488	| `path` | The file. A leading `~` is expanded. | |
489	| `bookmark` | A base64 file bookmark. | None |
490	| `kind` | `video`, `audio`, `image` or `lut`. | `video` |
491	| `duration` | The length, in ticks. | 0 |
492	| `width`, `height` | The size in pixels. A file with pixels needs both. | 0 |
493	| `fps` | The frame rate, as `[numerator, denominator]`. | `[30, 1]` |
494	| `has_video` | Whether it has a picture. | On for `video` and `image` |
495	| `has_audio` | Whether it has sound. | On for `audio` |
496	| `has_alpha` | Whether it has an alpha channel. | Off |
497	| `original` | `{path, bookmark?}`: the file a `.mov` copy or conversion was made from. | None |
498	| `color` | A video file's Camera Log, as `set_media_color` takes it, plus `detected`, and `pq`, a PQ file's `{file?, from?, peak?}` as `get_project` shows it. | None |
499	| `cursor` | `{path, bookmark?, in_picture}`: the cursor file recorded beside a video, with `in_picture` true when the movie's own picture already shows the pointer. Both `path` and `in_picture` are required, and it's for a video with a picture only. | None |
500	
501	It answers `ok: true`, `media` (the new id), `path` and the `project` summary.
502	
503	An unknown key is refused by name, and so is a value of the wrong shape. A picture with no width or height, a video with a frame-rate term of 0, an empty path and a negative duration are all refused. A `color` that `set_media_color` wouldn't take is refused too. A path already on the list changes nothing.
504	
505	## `relink_media`
506	
507	Points a media entry at a file that moved, as [the Relink… sheet](/projects/relink-media/) and the Media tab's row menu do. `get_project`'s `missing_media` names the entries that need this.
508	
509	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
510	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
511	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
512	| `path` | string | Yes | Where the file is now. |
513	| `bookmark` | string | No | A base64 file bookmark. Leave it out and one is made for you, so the next move is followed automatically. |
514	| `scope` | integer | No | Leave it out. Passing it is refused, because this edit has no meaning inside a nest. |
515	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
516	
517	The new file is read as `import_media` reads one, and the entry takes its duration, size, frame rate and audio, video and alpha flags. What happens to the rest is on [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/#what-a-relink-keeps):
518	
519	- A clip running past the end of a shorter file is shortened to end with it. One that starts past the new end keeps a single frame.
520	- Camera Log and an HDR10 peak are kept.
521	- Saved speech is held to the new file, and forgotten when the new file has no sound.
522	- The cursor file beside the new movie is taken. If there's none, the old one stays as long as it's still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the entry's cursor file is cleared.
523	- A WebM or Matroska file is copied into a `.mov` first, and a file the ffmpeg step converts is recorded the same way. Either becomes the entry's new `original`, and any other file clears it.
524	
525	It answers `ok: true`, `media`, `path`, `kind`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `has_video`, `has_audio`, `has_alpha`, `original` when there is one, and the `project` summary.
526	
527	It's refused when no media has that id, when nothing exists at `path`, when the file can't be read, and for a file of another kind, such as a sound file for a video entry. The undo step is called "Relink Media".
528	
529	## `remove_media`
530	
531	Removes a media entry from the project, as [**Remove** in the Media tab's row menu](/projects/remove-media/) does. The file on disk isn't touched.
532	
533	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
534	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
535	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
536	| `with_clips` | boolean | No | Remove the clips using it as well, including those inside nests. For a LUT, clear the looks and Camera Log conversions that name it instead. Default `false`. |
537	| `scope` | integer | No | Leave it out. Passing it is refused, because this edit has no meaning inside a nest. |
538	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
539	
540	A nest clip isn't a user of the file, so it stays even when clips inside it go. Any [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) setting that listens to the file is cleared.
541	
542	It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary.
543	
544	It's refused while clips use the file and `with_clips` isn't `true`, naming the clips. A LUT in use as a look or a Camera Log is refused the same way, naming what uses it. The undo step is called "Remove Media".
545	
546	## `consolidate_media`
547	
548	Copies every file the project references into `media/` inside the `.framejob` package and relinks the project at the copies, as [**File ▸ Consolidate Media…**](/projects/consolidate-media/) does. Afterwards the package is the whole edit. It can be moved or archived and still open with the original footage deleted.
549	
550	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
551	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
552	| `project` | string | No | The project to consolidate. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
553	
554	It copies as many bytes as the footage weighs, so it can take a while, and it has no **Cancel**. Frame Job's window doesn't respond until it's done. A recording's cursor file is copied beside its movie.
555	
556	Files already inside are left alone, and missing files are reported rather than guessed at. A file that can't be copied keeps pointing at the original, so the project always still opens.
557	
558	It answers `ok: true`, `copied`, `bytes`, `directory`, `summary`, `failures` and `missing` when there are any, and the `project` summary. When every file it can find is already inside, it answers `copied: 0`, `directory`, `missing`, a `note`, and the summary, and makes no step.
559	
560	It's refused when the project has never been saved, so call `save_project` with a path first, when the project references no media files, and when nothing could be copied. The undo step is called "Consolidate Media".
561	
562	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first.
563	
564	## `set_media_color`
565	
566	Sets how a video file's camera log footage is converted to Rec. 709, as the Media tab's [Camera Log popup](/hdr/camera-log/) does, and where a PQ file's highlights roll off to white, as its [HDR10 Peak field](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) does.
567	
568	Every clip of the file follows the setting, reversed clips included. It's converted before the chroma key and every grade, and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) keeps it.
569	
570	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
571	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
572	| `media` | integer | Yes | The video's media id, or a PQ still's for `peak` alone. |
573	| `color` | object or null | Yes | What to set, as below. `null` clears it, but the key must be there. |
574	| `scope` | integer | No | Leave it out. Passing it is refused, because this edit has no meaning inside a nest. |
575	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
576	
577	`color` is one of these:
578	
579	| `color` | What it does |
580	| --- | --- |
581	| `{log, gamut?}` | Converts with a built-in curve. |
582	| `{lut}` | Converts with an imported `.cube`, named by its media id. [`import_media`](#import_media) it first. See [Camera log from your own LUT](/hdr/log-luts/). |
583	| `{peak}` | A PQ file's peak, a whole number of cd/m² from 1 to 10,000. |
584	| `log` or `lut` beside `peak` | Both at once. |
585	| `null` | No conversion, which shows the log picture, and no peak override. |
586	
587	The curves, and the gamuts each takes. An absent `gamut` means the first one listed:
588	
589	| `log` | The curve | `gamut` |
590	| --- | --- | --- |
591	| `apple_log` | Apple Log | `bt2020` |
592	| `apple_log2` | Apple Log 2 | `apple_wide_gamut` |
593	| `slog3` | S-Log3 | `s_gamut3_cine`, `s_gamut3` |
594	| `vlog` | V-Log | `v_gamut` |
595	| `canon_log2` | Canon Log 2 | `cinema_gamut`, `bt2020` |
596	| `canon_log3` | Canon Log 3 | `cinema_gamut`, `bt2020` |
597	
598	An Apple Log or Apple Log 2 file is set at import, and `get_project` shows `detected: true` in the file's `media[].color`.
599	
600	Import reads a PQ file's own peak into `media[].color.pq`, as `{file, from}`: MaxCLL, or else the mastering display's maximum. When the file names neither, `pq` is `{}`, which means 1,000. `peak` overrides that reading.
601	
602	:::caution
603	`color` replaces the Camera Log and the peak together, so send both to keep both. `null` clears both, and the peak goes back to the file's own reading.
604	:::
605	
606	It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary. The undo step is called "PQ Peak" when `color` holds only `peak`, and "Camera Log" otherwise.
607	
608	It's refused:
609	
610	- on an audio file or a LUT
611	- on a picture, unless it's a PQ still and `color` is `peak` alone
612	- for a `peak` on a file that isn't PQ, or outside 1 to 10,000
613	- for a `color` with none of `log`, `lut` and `peak`
614	- for `log` and `lut` together
615	- for a `gamut` without a `log`, or one its curve doesn't take
616	- for a `lut` that doesn't name a LUT in the project
617	- for `detected` or `pq`, which only import writes
618	
619	## `set_media_speech`
620	
621	Saves where a file's speech is. [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#where-the-speech-comes-from) ducks the mix by these spans, and [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) reads them too.
622	
623	Setting **Duck by** to **Speech** in the Sound sub-tab's **Ducking** section writes them from the file's detected speech, and so does [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) with `duck.mode` set to speech. Call this only to give spans of your own.
624	
625	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
626	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
627	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
628	| `spans` | array of `[start, end]` pairs | Yes | Where the speech is, in ticks of the file played forward, sorted, with each end excluded. An empty list means the file has no speech. |
629	| `scope` | integer | No | Leave it out. Passing it is refused, because this edit has no meaning inside a nest. |
630	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
631	
632	It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary, and `get_project` shows the spans as `media[].speech`. Spans equal to what the file already has change nothing. The undo step is called "Speech Spans".
633	
634	It's refused:
635	
636	- on a file with no sound
637	- for a span that starts before 0, ends at or before its start, or ends past the file's duration
638	- for spans out of order or overlapping. Touching is fine.
639	- past 100,000 spans
640

2	---
3	title: Chat with the Assistant
4	description: Open the Assistant tab, ask for what you want in plain words, and manage the conversation that goes with each window.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	The Assistant is a conversation with Claude, built into the inspector of every editor window. You ask in plain words, and it reads and edits that window's project.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
14	  keys="⌃⌘A"
15	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
16	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key. Without one, the tab says how to add it."
17	/>
18	
19	## The Assistant tab
20	
21	You might ask:
22	
23	- "trim the pauses out of the interview"
24	- "put a title over the first five seconds"
25	- "what is under the playhead?"
26	
27	The Assistant uses the same tools an agent uses over MCP, less a few held back from it, so its edits are ordinary edits. You watch each change land, and each one is its own undo step. See [What the Assistant can do](/assistant/what-it-can-do/).
28	
29	It's the fifth inspector tab, after **Clip**, **Media**, **Document** and **Transcript**. Before your first message, [save your key](/assistant/set-up/).
30	
31	## Open the Assistant
32	
33	Choose **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>). Frame Job shows the inspector if it was hidden, switches to the Assistant tab and puts the cursor in the message field.
34	
35	It isn't a toggle. Pressed while the tab is already showing, it only puts the cursor back in the field.
36	
37	The command stays enabled with no key, so the tab can [say what's needed](/assistant/set-up/#the-no-key-prompt). There's no message field to put the cursor in until then.
38	
39	## The tab's layout
40	
41	From top to bottom:
42	
43	| Part | What it shows |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| **Context** | How full the conversation is, with [**Clear**](#clear-the-conversation) (↺) at its right end. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/). |
46	| **Spend** | What this conversation has cost so far, as Frame Job estimates it. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). |
47	| The transcript | Your messages, the replies and each tool call. See [Read the conversation](/assistant/conversation/). |
48	| The ask-first row | Shows only while the Assistant is waiting for your permission. See [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). |
49	| The message field and **Send** | Where you type. |
50	
51	## The tab stays put
52	
53	The Assistant's own edits change the selection without moving you off the tab, so you can read along as it works.
54	
55	Clicking a clip in the timeline or on the canvas still switches to the **Clip** tab.
56	
57	## Send a message
58	
59	<Steps>
60	
61	1. Click in the message field, which reads "Ask about or edit this project…", and type what you want.
62	
63	2. Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or click **Send**.
64	
65	</Steps>
66	
67	The field empties once the message is taken, and the reply arrives in the transcript. Everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply is called a turn.
68	
69	The field starts one line high, grows to five lines as you type, and scrolls past that. Spaces and blank lines at either end are dropped, and a message of nothing else does nothing.
70	
71	You can type your next message while the Assistant works, but you can't send it until the turn ends.
72	
73	## Message field keys
74	
75	| Key | In the message field |
76	| --- | --- |
77	| <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | Sends the message and gives the keys back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays while the Assistant works. While it's working or waiting for your answer, this beeps instead and the field keeps the keys. |
78	| <kbd>⇧↩</kbd>, <kbd>⌘↩</kbd>, <kbd>⌥↩</kbd> or <kbd>⌃↩</kbd> | Starts a new line |
79	| <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>⇧Tab</kbd> | Gives the keys back to the editor and never types a tab. With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, moves to the next or previous control. |
80	| <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> | Undo and redo your typing |
81	
82	Clicking **Send** gives the keys back the same way <kbd>↩</kbd> does, and so does clicking anywhere else in the window below its title bar. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/#start-and-finish-typing).
83	
84	Your typing never lands on the project's undo stack, and sending a message drops the field's own undo history. While the keys are in the field, <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> only undoes typing. Outside the field, it takes back the Assistant's last edit.
85	
86	<kbd>↩</kbd> never answers a question and never stops a turn. While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> belongs to it.
87	
88	## If a message cannot be sent
89	
90	If the conversation can't start, the reason appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the field. Your message isn't added to the transcript, so you can send it again once the cause is fixed.
91	
92	The usual causes are [a missing key](/assistant/set-up/#the-no-key-prompt) and [a helper that won't start](/assistant/set-up/#if-the-helper-is-missing).
93	
94	## Send becomes Stop
95	
96	The button reads **Send**, with the tooltip "Send the message". While a turn is running or waiting on you, it reads **Stop**, with the tooltip "Stop the turn".
97	
98	**Stop** is a click. It has no shortcut. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/).
99	
100	## What each message carries
101	
102	Each message starts with a short block describing your window at the moment you sent it, so "this clip" and "the selected titles" mean what you'd expect. The block holds:
103	
104	- the project's name, and its path, or a note that it's never been saved
105	- the nest open in the window, if there is one, or that the timeline is open
106	- the playhead's position
107	- the ids of the selected clips
108	
109	You don't see the block in the transcript, but it goes to Anthropic with your message. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).
110	
111	It isn't updated during the turn. The Assistant is told to read the project again after its own edits.
112	
113	## One conversation per window
114	
115	Each editor window has its own conversation, about that window's project. Closing the window ends the conversation and [declines](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining) any question waiting for your answer.
116	
117	Conversations aren't saved with the project, so reopening it starts with an empty transcript.
118	
119	The Assistant can't close its own window. You do that with **File ▸ Close** (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>).
120	
121	## Clear the conversation
122	
123	Click **Clear** (↺, "Clear the conversation") at the right end of **Context**. It ends the conversation and empties the transcript, and your next message starts a fresh one.
124	
125	- **Spend** goes back to "Nothing yet".
126	- The context meter keeps the model's window size, so after a conversation it reads "0 of … tokens · 0%", with that size in place of the dots, until the next response.
127	- Clear asks for no confirmation. It ends a running turn and declines a waiting question.
128	
129	The project is untouched. Edits already made stay, each still its own undo step.
130

139	---
140	title: "Long conversations"
141	description: Watch how much of the model's memory a conversation uses, and keep a long one going with compaction and tool result clearing.
142	---
143	
144	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
145	
146	A conversation with the Assistant grows with every message, tool result and rendered frame, and the model can only hold so much of it at once. That limit is its context window, measured in tokens, the small pieces of text a model counts in. The Context meter shows how full it is, and two settings keep a long conversation going.
147	
148	<AtAGlance
149	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
150	  keys="⌘,"
151	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Context"
152	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
153	/>
154	
155	## The context meter
156	
157	The **Context** row at the top of the Assistant tab shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response.
158	
159	| The row reads | When |
160	| --- | --- |
161	| "Nothing reported yet" | Before your first message in this window. |
162	| "12,000 of 200,000 tokens · 6%" | Once the model's window is known. The percentage shows at most one decimal. It can read "0 of …" for a moment after your first message, before the first response. |
163	| "12,000 tokens (window size unknown)" | Anthropic didn't report the window size. |
164	
165	When the inspector is narrow the figure shortens to "12,000 / 200,000 · 6%" or "6%", or to "12,000 tokens" with no known window. The tooltip always has the full figure.
166	
167	The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns coral past 80%.
168	
169	**Clear** (↺), at the end of the row, puts the count back to zero, and so does a change of key or model, because each ends the conversation.
170	
171	## The settings
172	
173	Both settings are in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**. A change applies without **Save** and keeps the conversation going. A new threshold counts from the end of the current turn, and a change to clearing applies from your next message.
174	
175	| Setting | What it does | Default | Range |
176	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
177	| **Compact when context reaches** … **tokens** | Replaces the conversation with a summary at the end of a turn. | On, 300,000 tokens | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens |
178	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop older tool results from what the model sees. | Off | |
179	
180	The token field is dimmed while **Compact when context reaches** is off. A number outside the range beeps, and the field goes back to the stored value.
181	
182	## Compaction
183	
184	With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is replaced by a summary at the end of the first turn that reaches the threshold. It never happens in the middle of a turn, and a [stopped](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) turn doesn't compact.
185	
186	The summary is asked to keep:
187	
188	- what you asked for and every preference you stated
189	- the project and any nest open
190	- the clips, tracks, markers and media involved
191	- the edits made, in order, and which were undone
192	- what's still open or was promised
193	
194	Rendered frames don't survive, so the summary describes in words what each one showed. The Assistant renders again when it needs to look.
195	
196	The transcript notes each step:
197	
198	| The transcript says | What it means |
199	| --- | --- |
200	| "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" | The summary has been asked for. |
201	| "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look." | It worked. The Context meter drops to about *M*. |
202	| "Compaction didn't finish (*reason*); it will try again after the next turn." | No summary came back. The conversation is unchanged. |
203	
204	The summary request is priced like any other response, and it's part of that turn's [`Cost:` line](/assistant/cost/#per-turn).
205	
206	:::tip
207	Compaction only starts once the conversation reaches the threshold, so the threshold has to be lower than the model's window. If the Context meter shows a window smaller than your threshold, lower it.
208	:::
209	
210	## With compaction off
211	
212	Nothing replaces the conversation, so it keeps growing until it fills the model's window. From then on each message fails, with an [error in the transcript](/assistant/conversation/#errors), until you click **Clear**. **Clear** ends the conversation, and nothing of it carries into the next message.
213	
214	## Clearing old tool results
215	
216	A tool result is what comes back from one of the Assistant's tool calls, and a project's details can run long. With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older ones from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It's a lighter step than compaction: the conversation stays, and only old tool results go.
217	
218	- It keeps the five most recent tool uses.
219	- It clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time.
220	- It can happen in the middle of a turn.
221	- It never clears tool search results, which are how the Assistant finds its tools.
222	
223	Each clearing adds a note to the transcript, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view." The model may have to fetch something again afterwards.
224	
225	Each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write: Anthropic can't reuse its stored copy of the conversation, so it stores a new one, and that goes on your bill. That's why it clears in large pieces.
226
