233	---
234	title: "Read the conversation"
235	description: "Follow what the Assistant is doing as it works: its replies, its tool calls, the questions it asked, and why it stopped."
236	---
237	
238	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
239	
240	The transcript in the Assistant tab shows everything that happens in a conversation: your messages, the replies, each tool call, each question, and what went wrong. Reading it tells you what the Assistant did and why it stopped.
241	
242	<AtAGlance
243	  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
244	  keys="⌃⌘A"
245	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
246	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key"
247	/>
248	
249	## What's in the transcript
250	
251	| You see | It looks like |
252	| --- | --- |
253	| Your message | Semibold |
254	| The Assistant's [replies](#replies) | Regular |
255	| Its [working notes](#working-notes) | Small and faint |
256	| [Tool call lines](#tool-call-lines), [`failed:` lines](#failed-lines), [permission lines](#permission-lines) and [notes](#notes) | Small monospace |
257	| [Errors](#errors) | Red |
258	
259	## Replies
260	
261	A reply streams in as it's written, under your message. The transcript scrolls to the newest line each time anything arrives, even if you've scrolled up to read something earlier.
262	
263	Replies are short on purpose. See [How it behaves](/assistant/what-it-can-do/#how-it-behaves).
264	
265	## Working notes
266	
267	Between tool calls the Assistant writes small, faint notes on what it's working through. They're its thinking updates, and they stream in as replies do. They aren't addressed to you, and there's nothing to answer.
268	
269	## Tool call lines
270	
271	A tool is one action the Assistant can take in Frame Job, such as splitting a clip. Each tool call is one line, with the tool's name and its arguments, the details it was given:
272	
273	```
274	split (at: 1200000, clips: [12])
275	```
276	
277	That line splits clip 12 at the timeline's two-second mark. A time shows as a large number, 600,000 to the second.
278	
279	Arguments are in alphabetical order, and the line shows only their first 70 characters. A call with no arguments shows the tool's name alone.
280	
281	The line appears when the call starts. Apart from a [permission line](#permission-lines) if it asked you first, a call that works adds nothing more to the transcript, and you see its result in the project. A call that doesn't work adds a [`failed:` line](#failed-lines). [All tools](/mcp/tools/) describes every tool.
282	
283	## `failed:` lines
284	
285	A tool call that didn't work is followed by `failed:` and the reason. The line shows the first 200 characters of what the tool said.
286	
287	The Assistant reads the same message in full, so it can correct itself. A `failed:` line followed by another tool call is normal, and often the next try works.
288	
289	| The line reads | What happened |
290	| --- | --- |
291	| `failed: … was refused at …: …` | Frame Job wouldn't make the edit. The line names the edit, then gives the same sentence you'd see yourself. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/). |
292	| `failed: … made no change: the project is already in that state.` | The edit wouldn't have changed anything. |
293	| `failed: The person declined: …` | You chose **Deny**, or the question was declined for you. The Assistant won't try that call again this turn unless you ask. |
294	| `failed: Cancelled by the user.` | **Stop** cancelled the call before it started. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/). |
295	| `failed: … is not available to the assistant: …` | The Assistant isn't allowed that tool. The reason names the menu item to use instead. See [What it won't do](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). |
296	
297	## Permission lines
298	
299	The Assistant [asks before it writes a file](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). Once a question is answered, the transcript records the outcome with the question's sentence, for example `Allowed: export writes /Volumes/Work/cut.mp4`.
300	
301	| The line starts | What happened |
302	| --- | --- |
303	| `Allowed:` | You chose **Allow**. |
304	| `Declined:` | You chose **Deny**. |
305	| `Declined (stop):` | You chose **Stop** while the question was waiting. |
306	| `Declined (close):` | The conversation ended while the question was waiting, for example because the key or the model changed. |
307	| `Declined (helper):` | [The helper stopped](#if-the-helper-stops) while the question was waiting. |
308	
309	## Notes
310	
311	Frame Job writes its own small monospace notes into the transcript.
312	
313	| The note reads | What it means |
314	| --- | --- |
315	| `Cost: …` | What the turn came to, at the end of each turn. For example, `Cost: $0.0312 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-11-02)`. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). |
316	| `Compacting the conversation (… tokens)…` | The conversation has reached your compaction threshold, and Frame Job is replacing it with a summary. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/). |
317	| `Compacted: … → about … tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look.` | The summary is in place. |
318	| `Compaction didn't finish (…); it will try again after the next turn.` | No summary came back, so the conversation is unchanged. |
319	| `Cleared … old tool results (… tokens) from the model's view.` | Old results were dropped from what the model sees. This only happens with clearing turned on in Settings. |
320	| `The model is now …; the next message starts a new conversation.` | The model changed in Settings. |
321	| `The API key changed; the next message starts a new conversation.` | The key was saved or removed in Settings. |
322	| `The spend ledger … could not be written: ….` | A response's cost couldn't be recorded. The note appears once per conversation, and an unrecorded response is missing from the month's total in Settings. |
323	
324	## Errors
325	
326	An error is a red line, and it says what went wrong.
327	
328	| The error reads | What it means |
329	| --- | --- |
330	| `API error status: message` | Anthropic turned the request down or it failed, for example a bad key, a rate limit or an outage. The status is Anthropic's, and it's blank when the request never reached Anthropic. |
331	| "The reply was cut off at the output limit." | The response reached 32,000 [tokens](/assistant/context-and-compaction/), the small pieces of text a model counts in. Thinking counts toward that as well as the reply. |
332	| "The model declined this request." | The model wouldn't do what you asked. |
333	| "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one." | See [If the helper stops](#if-the-helper-stops). |
334	
335	If a conversation can't start, for example because the helper won't run, the reason shows as an error and your message stays in the field.
336	
337	A request you end with **Stop** shows no error.
338	
339	## Automatic retries
340	
341	Rate limits, outages and connection failures are retried up to three times before an error appears. Nothing shows in the transcript during a retry, so a turn can seem to pause. A bad key fails at once.
342	
343	## Select and copy
344	
345	The transcript is one block of text, so you can drag a selection across entries. <kbd>⌘C</kbd> copies it as plain text, with a line break between entries.
346	
347	A conversation isn't saved with the project. Copy anything you want to keep before you close the window.
348	
349	## If the helper stops
350	
351	The helper is the background program that talks to Anthropic for the Assistant. If it stops:
352	
353	- The transcript says "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one."
354	- A question that was waiting is declined, with a `Declined (helper):` line.
355	- The edits the Assistant already made stay in the project.
356	
357	Your next message starts a new conversation under the old transcript. The Assistant doesn't remember anything from before, and the Spend row carries on from where it was. To start clean, choose **Clear** (↺) at the top of the tab.
358	
359	## Good to know
360	
361	- A [turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/), everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply, takes at most 30 rounds of tool calls. At that point it ends with no error line, and your next message carries on from there.
362	- Each window has its own transcript. **Clear** empties it, and closing the window ends it. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).

374	---
375	title: "What it costs"
376	description: See what the Assistant costs per turn, per conversation and per month, and how far to trust the figures.
377	---
378	
379	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
380	
381	The Assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key, so Anthropic bills you directly for what it uses. Frame Job shows you an estimate of that cost for each turn, each conversation and each month.
382	
383	<AtAGlance
384	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
385	  keys="⌘,"
386	  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Spend', 'The Cost line at the end of each turn']}
387	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
388	/>
389	
390	## Your own billing
391	
392	Every response is priced by Frame Job from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices, a public price table on GitHub. Every figure on this page is **Frame Job's own estimate**. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was actually billed.
393	
394	| Where | What it covers |
395	| --- | --- |
396	| The [`Cost:` line](#per-turn) in the transcript | One turn |
397	| The [**Spend** row](#per-conversation) in the tab | The conversation so far |
398	| The [month's line](#per-month) in Settings | The current calendar month, across every window |
399	
400	## Per turn
401	
402	Each turn ends with a line in the transcript. For example:
403	
404	`Cost: $0.0182 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-10-25)`
405	
406	The amount sums every response in the turn, the [compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) summary included. It shows to four decimal places, and a tiny positive amount reads "under $0.0001". A turn with no response has no `Cost:` line.
407	
408	The brackets name the price table and its date:
409	
410	| The brackets say | The prices came from |
411	| --- | --- |
412	| "bundled table of …" | The copy built into the app |
413	| "cached …" | The copy Frame Job keeps, from an earlier refresh |
414	| "fetched …" | A copy downloaded for this conversation |
415	
416	If a refresh failed, the brackets add "; not refreshed:" and the reason. A table that downloaded but couldn't be saved adds "; the price cache could not be written:" and the reason.
417	
418	## Unpriced responses
419	
420	A response that couldn't be priced shows as unknown with its reason, never as $0. In the `Cost:` line it reads "unknown (*reason*)", followed by "· at least $…" for the part that could be priced.
421	
422	A response goes unpriced when:
423	
424	- its model isn't in the price table, for example "*model* is not in the price table"
425	- the table lists the model but has no rate for what was used
426	- it used fast mode, for example `speed "fast" is not priced`
427	- it used a batch or priority tier
428	- it was a US-only request
429	
430	When a request sends more than 200,000 tokens, the model's higher rates apply if the table lists them.
431	
432	## Responses cut short
433	
434	A response cut short by [Stop](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) or an error is priced from what had arrived. It shows as "at least $… (a response was cut short)".
435	
436	## Per conversation
437	
438	The **Spend** row, under **Context** in the Assistant tab, adds up the conversation's turns since the last **Clear**, or since a key or model change ended the conversation.
439	
440	| The row reads | When |
441	| --- | --- |
442	| "Nothing yet" | Before the first response. |
443	| "$0.0532 · Frame Job's estimate" | Every response was priced. |
444	| "at least $… · Frame Job's estimate" | A response was cut short or couldn't be priced. Shortened to "≥$… · Frame Job's estimate" when the inspector is narrow. |
445	| "under $0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate" | A tiny positive amount. Shortened to `<$0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate` when narrow. |
446	| "unknown · Frame Job's estimate" | Nothing could be priced, or a response has no price and the priced part is under $0.00005. |
447	
448	Hovering the figure shows "What this conversation's responses cost at LiteLLM prices, as Frame Job estimates it. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
449	
450	The figure is held in memory. If the helper, the small program that talks to Anthropic, stops, the row carries on from where it was.
451	
452	## Per month
453	
454	In **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**, a line under **Save** and **Remove** totals what the Assistant has cost in the current calendar month. The month runs in UTC, so it can turn over before or after midnight where you are.
455	
456	A response here is one reply from Anthropic, so one turn can count as several, and a compaction summary counts as one.
457	
458	| The line reads | When |
459	| --- | --- |
460	| "October 2026 (UTC): $1.24 over 87 responses." | Every response was priced. |
461	| "Nothing recorded in October 2026 (UTC)." | No responses this month. |
462	| "October 2026 (UTC): 5 responses; none could be priced." | No response had a price. |
463	| "October 2026 (UTC): 87 responses; 3 could not be priced, the rest came to $0.80." | Some had no price. They're counted, never added as $0. |
464	| "Reading the spend ledger…" | The [ledger](#the-spend-ledger) is being read. |
465	| "The spend ledger could not be read: *reason*." | It couldn't be read. |
466	| "This launch keeps no spend ledger." | Frame Job has no folder to keep one in. |
467	
468	Totals are rounded to the cent, and a positive amount that would round to $0.00 reads "under $0.01". When some lines of the ledger are damaged, the line adds a sentence such as "2 ledger lines could not be read." That count covers the whole ledger, because a line with no readable time can't be placed in a month.
469	
470	The line refreshes when Settings opens, and after each response while Settings is visible. During a refresh after a response, the last sentence stays until the new one is ready.
471	
472	Under it, a faint note says: "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
473	
474	## Prices refreshed daily
475	
476	Frame Job prices from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. It has a table built into the app, and keeps a copy refreshed at most once a day at `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json`.
477	
478	A refresh is checked when a conversation starts, with a 30-second limit, and a turn keeps the prices it started with. The download is a plain request to `raw.githubusercontent.com`, made by the helper. It carries no key and no project data.
479	
480	If it fails, Frame Job prices from the cached copy or the built-in table, and the `Cost:` line says which it used.
481	
482	## The spend ledger
483	
484	The figures in Settings come from a ledger, `spend.jsonl` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. It's on your Mac, and only your account can read it.
485	
486	Each response is one line, with its time, the service, the model, the token counts, its speed and service tier, the prices used, and the dollars or why they're unknown. It never records your key or the conversation's content.
487	
488	If a response's cost can't be written, the transcript notes it once per conversation: "The spend ledger *path* could not be written: *reason*." That response is then missing from the month's total in Settings.

498	---
499	title: "Assistant privacy"
500	description: What goes to Anthropic when you use the Assistant, what stays on your Mac, and how long a conversation lasts.
501	---
502	
503	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
504	
505	The Assistant works by sending your conversation to Anthropic, so it's worth knowing what that includes. Frame Job has no account or relay of its own: what you send goes to Anthropic under your own key, and nowhere else.
506	
507	<AtAGlance
508	  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant tab', 'Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant ▸ ⓘ']}
509	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
510	/>
511	
512	## What goes to Anthropic
513	
514	When you use the Assistant, these go to Anthropic under your key:
515	
516	- **Your messages**, and a short block in front of each one: the project's name and path, the open nest, the playhead and the selection.
517	- **What the tools send back**: the project's details as JSON, including media file paths, any clip transcripts it reads, the reason when something couldn't be done, and other results.
518	- **The frames it renders** to look at the picture.
519	
520	What it costs is billed to your key. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
521	
522	Your key is handed straight to the helper, the small program Frame Job runs to talk to Anthropic. It isn't placed on a command line or in the helper's environment.
523	
524	When a conversation starts, the helper also asks Anthropic for the model's context window, under your key. That request names only the model.
525	
526	The Assistant [asks before](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-asks-about-first) it exports a movie or captions, saves the project or consolidates media. Other tools can still [write files without asking](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#file-writes-that-do-not-ask).
527	
528	## No audio to the cloud transcriber
529	
530	Audio never goes to the cloud transcriber from the Assistant. [Cloud transcription is withheld](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-will-not-call), so uploading audio stays your choice, in **File ▸ Generate Captions…** or **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**.
531	
532	## The price table download
533	
534	Once a day at most, the helper downloads LiteLLM's public price table from GitHub. That request carries no key and no project data. See [Prices refreshed daily](/assistant/cost/#prices-refreshed-daily).
535	
536	## What stays on your Mac
537	
538	Everything else stays on your Mac. The Assistant keeps these files in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`:
539	
540	| File | What it is |
541	| --- | --- |
542	| `anthropic-key` | Your key, in a file only you can read. |
543	| `spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](/assistant/cost/#the-spend-ledger). It holds token counts and dollars, never your key or the conversation's content. |
544	| `anthropic-prices.json` | The cached price table. |
545	
546	## The conversation lives in memory
547	
548	The conversation is kept in memory only, and goes when you clear it or close the window. Nothing of it is saved in the project or in the spend ledger.
549	
550	## Related
551	
552	- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
553	- [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/)
554	- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)
555	- [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/)

557	=================== assistant/set-up.mdx
558	---
559	title: Set up the Assistant
560	description: Save your Anthropic API key, choose the model, and set how long conversations are kept in bounds.
561	---
562	
563	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
564	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
565	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
566	
567	The Assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key. Save the key once in Settings and the Assistant tab is ready in every editor window.
568	
569	<AtAGlance
570	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
571	  keys="⌘,"
572	  where="Settings ▸ Assistant"
573	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key."
574	/>
575	
576	## Your own Anthropic key
577	
578	There's no Frame Job account and no relay in between. The Assistant talks to Anthropic with your key, and Anthropic bills what it uses to your account.
579	
580	Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each turn and each month costs. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). The Anthropic Console shows what you were actually billed.
581	
582	## Open Settings
583	
584	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). **Assistant** is the second of the window's four sections, under **MCP** and above **Transcription**.
585	
586	<Shot
587	  name="02-settings.window"
588	  alt="The Settings window. The Assistant section has an Anthropic API key field reading Paste your key, a Model field showing claude-opus-5-5, Compact when context reaches ticked at 300,000 tokens, Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens unticked, the line No API key is set, Save and Remove buttons, and this month's spend. Transcription and Playback sit below it."
589	/>
590	
591	From top to bottom, the section holds:
592	
593	- the heading, with its [ⓘ](#what-the-info-button-says)
594	- **Anthropic API key:**
595	- [**Model:**](#choose-a-model)
596	- [**Compact when context reaches**](#compact-when-context-reaches)
597	- [**Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens**](#clear-old-tool-results)
598	- the [status line](#the-status-line), then **Save** and **Remove**
599	- this month's spend and a note on where the figure comes from. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
600	
601	## Save your key
602	
603	Create an API key in the Anthropic Console first. Settings has no link to your Anthropic account, so you'll need to go there yourself.
604	
605	<Steps>
606	
607	1. Paste your key into **Anthropic API key:**. With no key saved, the field reads "Paste your key".
608	
609	2. Click **Save**, or press <kbd>↩</kbd> in the field.
610	
611	</Steps>
612	
613	Spaces and line breaks around the key are dropped. The field empties, the status line reads "Key saved.", and the message field appears in every Assistant tab.
614	
615	A saved key is never shown again. The field shows a row of dots instead, and the row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key. To change the key, paste the new one and save. It replaces the old one.
616	
617	**Save** with an empty field beeps and changes nothing.
618	
619	## No Verify
620	
621	AssemblyAI's key has a **Verify** button, but this one doesn't. Frame Job doesn't contact Anthropic until you send a message from the Assistant tab, so that's the test.
622	
623	A key Anthropic won't accept shows in the transcript straight away as `API error <status>: <message>`, with no retries.
624	
625	## Remove your key
626	
627	Click **Remove**. It's only enabled while a key is saved. The saved key is deleted and the status line reads "Key removed."
628	
629	Every window's message field gives way to the [no-key prompt](#the-no-key-prompt) straight away, unless [the environment](#a-key-from-the-environment) still supplies a key.
630	
631	## The status line
632	
633	A line above **Save** and **Remove** tells you the key's state and what your last press did.
634	
635	| The line says | What it means |
636	| --- | --- |
637	| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, saved or in the environment. This is a state, not an error, so it's in the ordinary muted colour. It goes as soon as you type in the field. |
638	| "Key saved." | **Save** worked. |
639	| "Key removed." | **Remove** worked. |
640	| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written or removed, and the line gives the reason in stronger text. |
641	
642	The last line appears for a failed **Remove** too, with the same opening words. A failed **Save** still empties the field, so paste the key again once you've fixed the cause. After a failed **Remove**, the saved key stays. Neither ends a conversation.
643	
644	## Choose a model
645	
646	Type a model id into **Model:**, or leave it blank for the default, `claude-opus-5-5`, which the field shows as its placeholder.
647	
648	There's no list to pick from, and Frame Job doesn't check what you type. An id Anthropic doesn't know shows up as an error in the transcript when you next send a message.
649	
650	The change counts when you press <kbd>↩</kbd> or leave the field. Changing to a different model [ends open conversations](#what-a-change-does).
651	
652	## Compact when context reaches
653	
654	Tokens are the units Anthropic counts text in, and a turn is everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply. When a turn ends with the conversation at or past this many tokens, the conversation is replaced by a summary. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/) for what that keeps and what it loses.
655	
656	| Setting | Default | Range |
657	| --- | --- | --- |
658	| The checkbox | On | Untick it to never compact |
659	| The token field | 300,000 | 20,000 to 900,000 |
660	
661	The field is enabled only while the box is ticked. A new number counts when you press <kbd>↩</kbd> or leave the field. Anything outside the range beeps, the field goes back to the stored number, and nothing is written.
662	
663	## Clear old tool results
664	
665	**Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** is off by default. Tick it and Anthropic drops old tool results from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens, even partway through a turn. Only the checkbox is yours to set. The 150,000 is fixed.
666	
667	The five most recent tool results always stay, tool search results are never cleared, and each clearing takes out at least 50,000 tokens. Each clearing also costs a fresh prompt-cache write: Anthropic stores the shortened conversation again and charges for that.
668	
669	## What a change does
670	
671	A conversation keeps the key and model it started with, so changing either has to end it.
672	
673	| You change | Open conversations | The note in the transcript |
674	| --- | --- | --- |
675	| The key, by saving or removing | End, in every window | "The API key changed; the next message starts a new conversation." |
676	| The model, to a different one | End, in every window | "The model is now …; the next message starts a new conversation." |
677	| Compaction or clearing | Carry on | None |
678	
679	When a conversation ends this way:
680	
681	- The transcript stays, and your next message starts a new conversation.
682	- The Spend row and the context meter start over.
683	- A running turn ends, and a question waiting for your answer is [declined](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining).
684	
685	A window with no conversation open has nothing to end, so it gets no note.
686	
687	**Save** always counts as a change, even if you paste the same key again. **Model:** doesn't: retyping the current model, or blanking the field while the default is in use, ends nothing.
688	
689	### Chat settings apply at once
690	
691	There's no Save button for the compaction and clearing settings. A change reaches every open conversation and keeps each one going. A new compaction threshold applies at the end of the current turn, and a change to clearing applies from the next message.
692	
693	## What the info button says
694	
695	The ⓘ beside the **Assistant** heading sums up the section:
696	
697	- The Assistant sends your messages, the project's details and the frames it renders to Anthropic, using your own key, and what it costs is billed to that key.
698	- It asks before writing a file. See [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/).
699	- The key is kept in a file only you can read, and it's never shown again once saved.
700	- Leave the model blank for `claude-opus-5-5`. Changing the key or the model starts a new conversation.
701	- Compaction replaces the conversation with a summary at the end of a turn past the threshold, which is 20,000 to 900,000 tokens and 300,000 by default. Earlier renders don't survive it.
702	- Clearing lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn, but never tool search results. Each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write.
703	- Changing either setting keeps the conversation.
704	
705	## Where the key is kept
706	
707	A saved key lives in a file named `anthropic-key` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`, beside AssemblyAI's key file. Only your user account can read it: the file's mode is `0600`, and Frame Job creates the folder at `0700` if it isn't there yet.
708	
709	The key goes to the Assistant's [helper](#if-the-helper-is-missing) when a conversation starts, on the helper's standard input, and nowhere else. It's never a tool argument, a launch argument or an answer to a tool. See [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) for the rest of that folder.
710	
711	## Out of reach of tools
712	
713	No tool reads or writes the key, the model or the chat settings. An agent connected over MCP can't see or change them, and neither can the Assistant.
714	
715	## A key from the environment
716	
717	With no saved key, Frame Job uses the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable, read from the environment Frame Job was started in. In practice this only applies when you launch Frame Job from a shell that sets the variable.
718	
719	- A saved key always comes first.
720	- An empty variable counts as no key.
721	- A key from the variable isn't saved, so **Remove** stays dimmed unless you've saved one too.
722	- With the variable set, removing a saved key leaves the message field in place, and the next conversation uses the variable's key.
723	
724	The same rule gives [AssemblyAI's key](/captions/assemblyai-key/) the variable `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY`.
725	
726	## The no-key prompt
727	
728	Without a key, the Assistant tab still opens. In place of the message field it says "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and offers **Open Settings…**, which opens the Settings window. **View ▸ Assistant** stays enabled so the tab can tell you this.
729	
730	<Shot
731	  name="11b-assistant-tab.inspector"
732	  alt="The Assistant tab with no key set. Context reads Nothing reported yet, Spend reads Nothing yet, the transcript is empty, and at the foot is the line Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant, with an Open Settings button."
733	/>
734	
735	Saving the key brings the message field back at once.
736	
737	If the key goes some other way, say you delete the file by hand while Frame Job runs, the message field stays. An open conversation carries on with the key it started with. The next conversation fails to start, with "No Anthropic API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant."
738	
739	## If the helper is missing
740	
741	The Assistant runs in a small helper program inside the app, at `Contents/Helpers/framejob-agent`. Frame Job looks for it when a conversation starts. If it can't start one, a line appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the message field. A helper that stops later says so in red too.
742	
743	| The transcript says | What it means |
744	| --- | --- |
745	| "The assistant helper is not in this build." | This copy of Frame Job has no helper it can run. [Install Frame Job again](/getting-started/requirements-and-install/). |
746	| "Could not start the assistant helper: …" | The helper is there but won't run, and the line gives the reason. |
747	| "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one." | The helper stopped during a conversation. See [Clear the conversation](/assistant/chat/#clear-the-conversation). |
748

757	=================== assistant/stop-a-turn.mdx
758	---
759	title: "Stop a turn"
760	description: End what the Assistant is doing, see what stopping leaves in place, and how its tool calls wait for your drags and for each other.
761	---
762	
763	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
764	
765	A turn is everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply, including its tool calls, the actions it takes in Frame Job. You can end one at any moment with **Stop**. Nothing you or it has done is undone.
766	
767	<AtAGlance
768	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Stop, the Send button while a turn runs"
769	  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'cancel_export']}
770	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
771	/>
772	
773	## Stop a turn
774	
775	Click **Stop**. It's the **Send** button, which reads **Stop** while a turn runs or a question waits.
776	
777	Stop is a click only. Pressing Return in the message box while a turn runs beeps, and it never stops the turn.
778	
779	When you click **Stop**, Frame Job:
780	
781	- ends the request to Anthropic
782	- [declines a question](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining) that's waiting, recorded as `Declined (stop):`
783	- cancels every tool call that hasn't started, and tells the Assistant "Cancelled by the user."
784	- ends a long-running job that has started, if it's one of those below
785	
786	Any other tool call that has already started is allowed to finish.
787	
788	| Running when you stop | What happens |
789	| --- | --- |
790	| Transcribing on this Mac | The transcription is cancelled. |
791	| Reading a clip's or the timeline's transcript | The read is cancelled, and nothing is saved from it. |
792	| Measuring loudness for Normalize, Enhance Voice or Match Audio | The measurement ends, and nothing changes. |
793	| Waiting for on-device analysis, to read it, split at shots, reframe a clip, make a vertical version, switch by speaker or analyse a cut-out | The wait ends, and nothing is made from it. |
794	
795	A timeline transcript that the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) also wants carries on. Stop withdraws only the Assistant's own request for it.
796	
797	## What stopping leaves in place
798	
799	Stop undoes nothing and ends only the turn.
800	
801	- Edits already made stay, and each one is still its own undo step.
802	- The conversation keeps the results of the tool calls that finished before you stopped, and your next message carries on from there.
803	- A stopped request shows no error.
804	- A response cut short is priced from what had arrived, as "at least $…". See [Responses cut short](/assistant/cost/#responses-cut-short).
805	- A stopped turn doesn't [compact](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) the conversation, even if it has passed the threshold.
806	
807	## Stop and exports
808	
809	An export is handed to the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) as soon as it starts, so Stop doesn't reach it. Cancel it in the Export Queue, or ask the Assistant to cancel it.
810	
811	## The 30-round limit
812	
813	One turn stops after 30 requests to Anthropic, which usually means 30 rounds of tool calls. No error appears at the limit. The turn ends with its `Cost:` line, whatever work was left. Send another message to carry on.
814	
815	## While you are dragging
816	
817	If one of the Assistant's tool calls arrives during a drag on the timeline, the canvas or an inspector slider, it waits until you release the mouse. It then runs as its own undo step, after yours, so your drag never undoes the Assistant's change or mixes with it.
818	
819	The call waits for as long as the mouse is held down, and a drag in any open project holds it. The same applies to agents over [MCP](/mcp/overview/).
820	
821	## Tool calls take turns
822	
823	The Assistant's tool calls and MCP agents' calls take turns, one at a time, and each window's calls run in order, so two of them never work on a project at the same moment. While a window waits for your **Allow** or **Deny**, MCP agents and other windows keep working.
824

832	=================== assistant/what-it-can-do.mdx
833	---
834	title: "What the Assistant can do"
835	description: "What you can ask the Assistant for, job by job, how it checks its work, and where its limits are."
836	---
837	
838	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
839	
840	The Assistant edits the project in its own window. You ask in plain words, it makes the edits one at a time, and each one lands where you can see it. Almost all of them [can be undone](#each-edit-is-an-undo-step). This page goes through what you can ask for, job by job, and where the limits are.
841	
842	<AtAGlance
843	  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
844	  keys="⌃⌘A"
845	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
846	  tools={['get_project', 'render_frame', 'undo', 'redo']}
847	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key"
848	/>
849	
850	## The same tools as MCP
851	
852	The Assistant works by calling tools, one for each job. They're the same tools an outside AI agent uses when it connects to Frame Job [over MCP](/mcp/overview/), so anything here is something an agent can do too. There are a few exceptions, listed in [What it won't do](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/), and some tools that write files [ask you first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-asks-about-first).
853	
854	Four tools are always at hand: reading the project, rendering a frame, undo and redo. It finds every other tool by searching for what it wants to do, so you never need to name one. A tool kept from it outright doesn't turn up in that search at all.
855	
856	Each job below lists its tools, because those are the names you'll see in the [tool call lines](/assistant/conversation/#tool-call-lines). [All tools](/mcp/tools/) describes each one.
857	
858	## What you can ask for
859	
860	Ask in your own words, for example "put a title over the first five seconds". You don't need to know which job a request falls under. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/) for how to send one.
861	
862	### Projects and navigation
863	
864	It can open, create and save projects, move the playhead, set the in and out range, change the selection, and enter or leave a nest. It can also make a [new project from a range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) or a [vertical version](/framing/make-vertical-version/).
865	
866	Saving asks first. Making a new project from a range or a vertical version asks first when it names where to save. Moving the playhead, setting the range and changing the selection aren't edits, so they make no undo step.
867	
868	A project it opens or creates gets a window of its own, and the Assistant stays with the project it started in.
869	
870	<AtAGlance tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version', 'save_project', 'set_playhead', 'set_range', 'set_selection', 'set_scope']} />
871	
872	### Tracks, markers and the canvas
873	
874	It can add, remove and reorder tracks, remove the empty ones, rename a track, hide, mute, solo or lock one, and set its [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) and [mix](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). It can add, move, rename and remove [markers](/timeline/markers/), make one a chapter, and set its colour, which you can't do yourself. It can change the canvas's [size](/projects/canvas-size/), [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) and [background](/projects/background-and-timecode/).
875	
876	<AtAGlance tools={['add_track', 'remove_track', 'move_track', 'set_track', 'remove_empty_tracks', 'add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker', 'set_canvas']} />
877	
878	### Media
879	
880	It can [import](/projects/import-media/), [relink](/projects/relink-media/) and [remove](/projects/remove-media/) media, [copy it into the project](/projects/consolidate-media/) and set a file's [camera log](/hdr/camera-log/). Copying into the project asks first.
881	
882	It can also save where a file's speech is, read the [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of a file, and attach or read a recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/).
883	
884	<AtAGlance tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech', 'consolidate_media', 'get_media_analysis', 'set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events']} />
885	
886	### Placing clips
887	
888	It can place media, [text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/), [backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/), [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) and [graphics](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/). It can [insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/), paste and duplicate, and put [text behind a subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).
889	
890	<AtAGlance tools={['add_clip', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip', 'add_adjustment_clip', 'add_background', 'add_blurred_background', 'text_behind_subject', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'paste', 'duplicate', 'insert_graphic']} />
891	
892	### Editing clips
893	
894	It can [move](/editing/move-clips/), [trim](/editing/trimming/), [split](/editing/splitting/), [slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/), [rate-stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/), [ripple-delete and lift](/editing/delete-clips/), [insert time and close gaps](/editing/close-gaps/). It can [detach audio and attach it again](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and make [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
895	
896	For several cameras or long recordings it can [split at shot changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/), [copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/), [switch a shot's angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [switch by speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).
897	
898	<AtAGlance tools={['move_clip', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'rate_stretch', 'slip', 'roll', 'split', 'delete', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'lift_range', 'insert_time', 'close_gap', 'detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'split_at_shots', 'copy_pieces', 'switch_angle', 'switch_by_speaker']} />
899	
900	### Nests
901	
902	It can [nest clips](/editing/nests/) or take a nest apart. An edit lands in whichever timeline the window is showing, unless the Assistant names a nest, and it can [open a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/#open-a-nest) as you do. Markers belong to the timeline, never to a nest.
903	
904	<AtAGlance tools={['nest', 'unnest']} />
905	
906	### Speed
907	
908	It can [set a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), [reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/), [freeze a frame](/speed/freeze-frame/), add [speed ramps](/speed/make-a-ramp/), [retime a range](/speed/retime-range/) and [speed up the typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) in a screen recording.
909	
910	<AtAGlance tools={['set_speed', 'set_reversed', 'freeze_frame', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range', 'speed_up_typing']} />
911	
912	### Look and sound
913	
914	It can change how a clip looks and sounds: position, scale, crop, colour, filters, volume, fades, text and its style, and shapes. It can rename or label a clip, turn its picture or sound off, and [paste attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
915	
916	It can also work with [transitions](/motion/transitions/), [actions](/motion/actions/) and [zooms](/motion/zoom-to-region/), including [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), and with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/), [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) and [reframing](/framing/reframe-clip/).
917	
918	<AtAGlance tools={['set_video', 'set_audio', 'set_text', 'set_shape', 'set_clip', 'set_enabled', 'paste_attributes', 'analyze_cutout', 'add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_duration', 'set_transition_style', 'add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'auto_zoom', 'switch_layout', 'reframe_clip', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']} />
919	
920	### Captions and words
921	
922	It can [import captions](/captions/import-captions/), [transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/), read a clip's or the whole timeline's timed words, [re-lay word captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) for the canvas, and [export captions](/captions/export-captions/).
923	
924	Transcribing runs on this Mac only, because the Assistant can't send audio to the cloud. Exporting captions asks first.
925	
926	<AtAGlance tools={['import_captions', 'transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'relay_captions', 'export_captions']} />
927	
928	### Audio clean-up
929	
930	It can find [silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [filler words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) and [cut them](#cut-words-by-asking), [normalise](/audio/normalize/) loudness, [enhance a voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [match one clip's sound to another](/audio/match-audio/) and [synchronise audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
931	
932	<AtAGlance tools={['detect_silence', 'detect_fillers', 'normalize_clip', 'enhance_voice', 'match_audio', 'sync_audio']} />
933	
934	### Graphics
935	
936	It can write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics, import their fonts and pictures, and add [shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/). Exporting a graphic asks first. See [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#the-assistant).
937	
938	<AtAGlance tools={['add_graphic_clip', 'set_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'get_graphic', 'graphic_reference', 'render_graphic', 'import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'delete_graphic', 'rename_graphic', 'restore_graphic', 'list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'export_graphic', 'import_graphic', 'add_shortcut_overlays']} />
939	
940	### Export
941	
942	It can [export](/export/export-sheet/), check how an export is going, or cancel it. Exporting asks first, because it writes a movie and replaces any file already there.
943	
944	<AtAGlance tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']} />
945	
946	## Cut words by asking
947	
948	You can ask the Assistant to take out filler words, silences or a false start, for example "cut the false start at the beginning of this clip." It cuts each request as one undo step, labelled **Undo Ripple Delete** rather than with the sheet's name.
949	
950	Its filler search reads only media that already has a cloud transcript made with filler words, and it can't upload audio to make one. In other media the search finds nothing, and it reports which media has no such transcript. To start the paid transcription, press **Transcribe** in the [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) sheet yourself.
951	
952	It removes a false start only when you ask, because deciding what counts as one is a judgement of meaning. It reads the words and their times, says which it will cut, then cuts them. The words come from a transcript the file already has or from this Mac's own speech recogniser, so no audio is uploaded. There's no menu command for this.
953	
954	See [Cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/).
955	
956	## It looks at rendered frames
957	
958	The Assistant checks its work by rendering a frame of the finished timeline, drawn the way an export draws it. It's told to look before and after a visual edit. It renders at the playhead unless it picks a time, and it's told to keep the image small.
959	
960	Rendering writes a picture file without asking. By default that's a temporary file.
961	
962	:::note
963	The frames it renders go to Anthropic, along with your messages and the project's details. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).
964	:::
965	
966	Earlier renders don't survive compaction, so it renders again when it needs to look. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).
967	
968	## Each edit is an undo step
969	
970	Every edit the Assistant makes is its own undo step on the project, the same as your own, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names it after the edit. A turn isn't grouped, so a turn that made ten edits takes ten undos.
971	
972	Graphics files are the exception. Writing, restoring, deleting or importing a graphic, and importing a font or picture for one, change files in the project and make no undo step. See [Undo rules](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#undo-rules).
973	
974	To take back its last change, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> outside the message field. You can also ask the Assistant to undo or redo.
975	
976	## How it behaves
977	
978	- **Short replies.** A reply is a sentence or two, and it doesn't repeat what the tool lines already show.
979	- **Captions only on request.** It writes or restyles a caption only when you ask.
980	- **Medium effort, thinking on.** The model always runs with these two Anthropic settings, and Frame Job's Settings has no control for them. The faint [working notes](/assistant/conversation/#working-notes) are its thinking updates.
981	
982	## Only its own window's project
983	
984	The Assistant acts only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation. A tool call that names another project doesn't run, and the transcript shows a `failed:` line: `The assistant edits its own window's project, …; … is a different project.`
985	
986	If its project has closed, a tool call fails with "The assistant's project is no longer open."
987	
988	## Limits
989	
990	- It works only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation.
991	- It needs your own Anthropic API key. There's no Frame Job account. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).
992	- It can't record the screen, close its window's project, or send audio to the cloud transcriber.
993	- A tool call that arrives during a drag waits until you release the mouse. See [While you are dragging](/assistant/stop-a-turn/#while-you-are-dragging).
994	- **Stop** doesn't cancel an export that's already been queued. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/).
995	- With [compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/) off, a long conversation eventually fails until you **Clear** it.
996	- Changing the key or the model ends every window's conversation.
997

1007	---
1008	title: "What it won't do and what it asks first"
1009	description: The jobs the Assistant leaves to you, the file writes it asks about first, and how to answer or decline a question.
1010	---
1011	
1012	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
1013	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1014	
1015	The Assistant can do most of what you can do in Frame Job, but a few jobs stay with you. It won't record, close its own project or send audio to the cloud, and it stops to ask before it exports, saves or copies media.
1016	
1017	<AtAGlance
1018	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab, the row headed “The assistant asks first:”"
1019	  tools={['record_screen', 'close_project', 'transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'export', 'export_captions', 'save_project', 'consolidate_media', 'export_graphic', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version']}
1020	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
1021	/>
1022	
1023	## Tools it will not call
1024	
1025	The Assistant works by calling tools, one for each job. Four jobs are yours to do yourself.
1026	
1027	| The job | Tool | Why | Do it with |
1028	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1029	| Record the screen or a camera | `record_screen` | Recording needs a person at the Record button. | **File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) |
1030	| Close the project | `close_project` | Closing the project would close the window the conversation lives in. | **File ▸ Close** (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>) |
1031	| Transcribe in the cloud | `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine | Audio leaves your Mac only when you choose it, with the price in front of you. | **File ▸ Generate Captions…** |
1032	| Transcribe for filler words | `transcribe_for_fillers` | The same: it uploads audio to the cloud. | **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** |
1033	
1034	`record_screen`, `close_project` and `transcribe_for_fillers` are taken out of what the Assistant can see, so it can't call them. `transcribe` stays, because transcribing on this Mac is allowed, and only a call that names the cloud engine is stopped.
1035	
1036	If one of the four is called anyway, it doesn't run. The transcript shows a [`failed:` line](/assistant/conversation/#failed-lines), "*tool* is not available to the assistant:" and the reason, which names the menu item to use instead. For the cloud engine the line starts `transcribe with engine "assemblyai"`.
1037	
1038	## Tools it asks about first
1039	
1040	Before it writes a movie, a caption file, a graphic package or the project, the Assistant waits for you.
1041	
1042	<Steps>
1043	
1044	1. The row headed "The assistant asks first:" appears in the Assistant tab, with a sentence saying what will happen, and **Allow** and **Deny** buttons. See [what each question reads](#what-each-question-reads).
1045	
1046	2. Read the sentence. A capitalised **REPLACES** means a file is already there.
1047	
1048	3. Click **Allow** to run the tool, or **Deny** to [decline](#declining).
1049	
1050	</Steps>
1051	
1052	Nothing runs until you click **Allow**. A question has no time limit, and it waits until you answer. You answer with a click only: no key answers it, and Return in the message box beeps. While a question waits, the **Send** button reads **Stop**.
1053	
1054	The transcript keeps a record of each answer, as `Allowed:` or `Declined:` and the sentence.
1055	
1056	## What each question reads
1057	
1058	Five tools always ask. The last two in this table ask only when the Assistant gives them a path to save to, because without one they don't write a project package.
1059	
1060	| Tool | The question reads |
1061	| --- | --- |
1062	| `export` | "export writes *path*", or "export REPLACES *path*" when a file is already there |
1063	| `export_captions` | "export_captions writes *path*", or "export_captions REPLACES *path*" |
1064	| `save_project` | "save_project writes *path*", or "save_project REPLACES *path*". With no path known, "save_project writes a file" |
1065	| `consolidate_media` | "consolidate_media copies every referenced file into *package*/media", or "… into the project's package" when the project has never been saved |
1066	| `export_graphic` | "export_graphic writes *path*", or "export_graphic REPLACES *path*", with `.fjgraphic` added when it's missing |
1067	| `new_project_from_range` | "new_project_from_range writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |
1068	| `make_vertical_version` | "make_vertical_version writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |
1069	
1070	A `~` in the path is expanded before the question is asked, so the sentence shows the full path.
1071	
1072	A few answers depend on what's on disk:
1073	
1074	- Saving a project that's already on disk reads "save_project REPLACES *path*", because the package is there. That's the normal question for an ordinary save.
1075	- `new_project_from_range` and `make_vertical_version` never replace anything. With something already at the path the question reads REPLACES, but after **Allow** nothing is written, and the Assistant is told to choose a new path.
1076	- A project that has never been saved needs a path. If `save_project` has none, the question reads "save_project writes a file" and nothing is written after **Allow**. `consolidate_media` also stops there, and the Assistant has to save the project first.
1077	- For `export`, `export_captions` and `save_project`, the sentence shows the path as the Assistant wrote it. Frame Job adds or corrects the file extension as it writes, and REPLACES looks only at the path in the sentence, so a question that reads "writes" can still replace a file at the corrected name.
1078	
1079	## File writes that do not ask
1080	
1081	Some tools write files without a question.
1082	
1083	| What it does | Tools |
1084	| --- | --- |
1085	| Writes a rendered frame, a PNG unless another format is asked for, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_frame` |
1086	| Writes a graphic's contact sheet as a PNG, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_graphic` |
1087	| Writes modules, fonts and assets into the project's graphics folder | `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `import_graphic` |
1088	| Saves a new, blank project at a path the Assistant names | `new_project` |
1089	
1090	`import_graphic` replaces nothing: a name that's already taken gets a suffix, and a picture whose name clashes stops the import.
1091	
1092	## The dot on the tab
1093	
1094	While a question waits, a small dot in the accent colour shows on the **Assistant** tab title, whichever inspector tab you're on. It sits to the right of the title, or raised at the title's top-right corner when the tab is narrow.
1095	
1096	The dot takes no clicks, so a click on it reaches the tab underneath. Frame Job doesn't switch tabs for you. If the inspector is hidden, **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) shows it and picks the tab.
1097	
1098	## Declining
1099	
1100	**Deny** tells the Assistant you declined. The tool doesn't run, and the Assistant is told not to try it again in the same [turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) unless you ask. The transcript shows a `failed:` line, "The person declined:" and the sentence, beside the `Declined:` record.
1101	
1102	A question also counts as declined when the turn or the conversation ends under it, and the transcript says what ended it:
1103	
1104	| What happened | The transcript reads |
1105	| --- | --- |
1106	| You clicked **Deny** | `Declined:` |
1107	| You clicked [**Stop**](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) | `Declined (stop):` |
1108	| A change of key or model in Settings ended the conversation | `Declined (close):` |
1109	| The helper, the small program that talks to Anthropic, stopped | `Declined (helper):` |
1110	
1111	**Clear** and closing the window decline it too, and those take the transcript with them.
1112	
1113	## A waiting question holds only its window
1114	
1115	An unanswered question holds that window's Assistant and no other's. Other windows' Assistants and agents over MCP keep working while it waits, and you can go on editing.
1116	
1117	## MCP agents are not bound
1118	
1119	These rules belong to the Assistant. An agent connected over [MCP](/mcp/overview/) drives the same tools directly, so it's never asked first, and none of these tools is withheld from it.

22	
23	## Opening Settings
24	
25	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). It works with or without a project open, so you can set your keys from the Welcome window before you make anything. It's a window, not a sheet, and it shows the same settings whichever project is open.
26	
27	The window has four sections, one under the other: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. There are no tabs. On a short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls.
28	
29	There's no OK or Cancel. Every control saves as you use it, and a key saves when you press its **Save** button. While it's open it's listed in the **Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.
30	
31	Other places send you here:
32	
33	- With no Anthropic key, the Assistant tab shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an **Open Settings…** button that opens this window.
34	- With AssemblyAI chosen and no key, the note above the buttons in the Generate Captions sheet, and the **Generate** button's tooltip, read "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." The sheet doesn't open Settings for you. If every file already has a transcript it can use, you don't need a key and there's no note.
35	- With no AssemblyAI key and no filler transcript to use, **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** is greyed, its title ends "(needs your AssemblyAI key)", and its tooltip is that same sentence.
36	
37	[AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/) says what each key turns on.
38	
39	## The info buttons
40	
41	The **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback** headings each carry an ⓘ button that explains the section. The MCP section has none, because its text is shown in full.
42	
43	- Rest the pointer on it for about a third of a second to see the explanation. Moving away closes it.
44	- Click it to keep the explanation open. Click it again, click anywhere else, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or close the window to end it.
45	
46	VoiceOver reads it as "About Assistant", and so on for each section. With keyboard navigation on, <kbd>Space</kbd> presses it.
47	
48	## MCP
49	
50	This section shows how an MCP client, such as Claude Code, reaches Frame Job. Clients use `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app, which connects over a local socket that only programs you run can open. If Frame Job isn't running, the first tool call opens it in the background.
51	
52	Under that text is the full path of the helper inside the copy you're running. You can select and copy it.
53	
54	**Copy MCP Command** puts the line that registers the helper with Claude Code on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell:
55	
56	```sh
57	claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
58	```
59	
60	The section then says "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."
61	
62	The path is always the one for the app you opened Settings from, so copy the command again if you move Frame Job. If the helper is missing from this copy, the button is dimmed and the section says "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."
63	
64	The command is for Claude Code. Other clients use the same helper path in their own configuration. See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).
65	
66	## Assistant
67	
68	This section holds what the Assistant tab needs: your Anthropic key, the model, and two settings for long conversations. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).
69	
70	| Control | What it does | Default |
71	| --- | --- | --- |
72	| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
73	| **Model:** | The Anthropic model the assistant uses, typed as text. Saved when you press <kbd>Return</kbd> or leave the field. Leave it blank for the default. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
74	| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When a turn ends with the conversation past this size, the conversation is replaced by a summary. Untick it to never compact. The number can be 20,000 to 900,000, and the field works only while the box is ticked. | On, 300,000 |
75	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn. It never drops tool search results. | Off |
76	| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
77	| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
78	
79	There's no **Verify** button here. Your key is first used when you send a message from the Assistant tab.
80	
81	**A change to the key or the model starts over.** Saving or removing the key, or changing the model, ends the conversation in every open window's Assistant tab, and the next message starts a new one. Pressing <kbd>Return</kbd> in **Model:** without changing the model that's used ends nothing.
82	
83	**A change to the other two keeps going.** The compaction and clearing settings apply to every open conversation at once and end none of them. They have no **Save** button. A compaction number outside 20,000 to 900,000 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.
84	
85	Compaction loses the frames the assistant rendered earlier, so it renders again when it needs to look. Each clearing also adds to your bill. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).
86	
87	Under the buttons is what the assistant has cost this month, with a note that the figure is Frame Job's own estimate. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
88	
89	The ⓘ sums up what's sent to Anthropic, that it's billed to your key, that the assistant asks before writing a file, where the key is kept, the blank **Model:** default and the two chat settings.
90	
91	## Transcription
92	
93	This section holds your AssemblyAI key and region. **File ▸ Generate Captions…** uses them with AssemblyAI chosen, and so does **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. Captions made on your Mac need no key. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).
94	
95	| Control | What it does | Default |
96	| --- | --- | --- |
97	| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
98	| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**. Saved as soon as you pick it. | United States |
99	| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
100	| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
101	| **Verify** | Makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with the key and region, to check they work. | |
102	| **Account Page** | Opens AssemblyAI's dashboard in your browser, where you get a key and see what you've spent. | |
103	
104	A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your AssemblyAI account uses. A stored region Frame Job doesn't recognise counts as United States.
105	
106	**Verify** checks a key you've typed and not saved, otherwise the stored key, otherwise a key from the environment. It's dimmed with no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running. The line under the controls gives the answer:
107	
108	| The line says | What it means |
109	| --- | --- |
110	| "Checking…" | The check is running. |
111	| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI took the key in this region. |
112	| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
113	| Any other sentence, such as "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" or "No network connection" | The check failed, and the sentence says why. |
114	
115	Saving or removing the key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so you don't need to reopen it.
116	
117	The ⓘ explains what's uploaded, when it's deleted and what AssemblyAI charges. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).
118	
119	## Playback
120	
121	This section controls whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time while you're idle, so they play smoothly from the start.
122	
123	| Control | What it does | Default |
124	| --- | --- | --- |
125	| **Background render** | While you leave Frame Job alone, it draws the graphics after the playhead in the window you used last. | On |
126	| **Start after … seconds** | How long you must be idle first, as a whole number from 1 to 60. Type it or use the stepper. Dimmed while **Background render** is off. | 5 |
127	
128	The box and the stepper save the moment you use them, and a typed number saves when you press <kbd>Return</kbd> or leave the field. A number outside 1 to 60 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.
129	
130	Anything you do in Frame Job stops the drawing at once and starts the wait again from zero: a key, a click, a scroll, an edit, play or a seek. An agent's calls count when they edit a project or move a playhead, and a call that only reads doesn't. Moving the pointer alone doesn't count, and neither does what you do in other apps.
131	
132	Background render never runs while a window is playing, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs. Its frames are held in memory, at most a quarter of your Mac's and less when memory is short, until the window closes or newer frames replace them. It draws pictures only and changes nothing about the sound. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).
133	
134	## How the key fields behave
135	
136	The Anthropic and AssemblyAI fields work the same way. A saved key is never shown again.
137	
138	- With a key stored, the field shows a row of dots as its placeholder. The row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key, and the key itself is never put in the field.
139	- With no key stored, the field reads "Paste your key".
140	
141	The line under the controls reports what happened:
142	
143	| The line says | What it means |
144	| --- | --- |
145	| "Key saved." or "Key removed." | The press worked. |
146	| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, in storage or in the environment. It's in ordinary grey, because this isn't an error. |
147	| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written, and the end of the line gives the reason. The field is still emptied. A **Remove** that fails shows the same sentence with its own reason, and the stored key stays. |
148	
149	[Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) says where the keys are stored, and how a key can come from the environment.
150	
151	## Agents and Settings
152	
153	No agent tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Your keys, the model, the region and **Background render** are set only by you, in this window.
154	
155	An agent's cloud tools, `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers`, do use the key and region saved here, so you have to set the key first. Without one they stop at the point they would send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use needs no key. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).

167	---
168	title: "What Frame Job remembers"
169	description: "Which view choices, pane sizes, sheets and panels reopen the way you left them, what starts fresh in each window, and where those choices are kept."
170	---
171	
172	Frame Job remembers some of your choices between launches, so the next window or sheet opens the way you left it. These are your choices on this Mac, not part of a project, so none of them travels with a `.framejob` package. The [Settings](/reference/settings/) window has its own page.
173	
174	## View choices
175	
176	The last choice you made, in any window, is what the next window opens with. These apply to every project.
177	
178	| Choice | Where | Options | Default |
179	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
180	| Snapping | **View ▸ Snapping**, <kbd>N</kbd>, or **Snap** in the timeline bar | On, off | On |
181	| Safe area guides | **View ▸ Safe Areas**, or **Safe** in the toolbar | On, off | Off |
182	| Inspector | **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (<kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd>), which reads **Show Inspector** while hidden | Shown, hidden | Shown |
183	| Timeline track height | **View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸**, or **S**, **M** and **L** in the timeline bar | Small, Medium, Large | Medium |
184	| Preview quality | **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸** | Full, Half, Quarter | Full |
185	
186	Preview quality changes only how sharply the preview is drawn while you work. Export and saved frames always render at full size. See [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/).
187	
188	Holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> while you drag turns snapping off for that drag only, and changes nothing that's remembered.
189	
190	## Pane sizes
191	
192	Drag the divider above the timeline, or the one left of the inspector, and new windows open at that size.
193	
194	| Pane | Range | Default |
195	| --- | --- | --- |
196	| Inspector width | 280 to 440 pt | 304 pt |
197	| Timeline height | 140 pt to 60% of the window | 300 pt |
198	
199	The canvas stays at least 380 pt wide, and the area above the timeline at least 220 pt tall.
200	
201	Only dragging a divider saves a size. Resizing the window, or hiding and showing the inspector, changes neither saved size, and the inspector's width isn't saved while it's hidden.
202	
203	## Preview Window frame
204	
205	**View ▸ Preview Window** (<kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd>) opens where the last one was left, on a second display for example. There's one saved frame for every project.
206	
207	With two projects' previews open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved. Whether the window is open isn't remembered. See [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).
208	
209	## Sheets
210	
211	These reopen on what you chose last time. Any sheet not listed here opens on its defaults every time.
212	
213	| Where | What's remembered | When it's saved |
214	| --- | --- | --- |
215	| **File ▸ Generate Captions…** | **Engine:** (On this Mac or AssemblyAI), **Style:**, and the **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken** and **Dim in pauses** boxes | As you change each one |
216	| **File ▸ Export…** | The last settings you exported with, except **Dynamic Range** | When you press **Export…** or **Add to Queue** |
217	| **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** | **Zoom:**, **Arrive:**, **Stay:**, **Follow the cursor while zoomed**, **Replace existing zooms** and **Motion blur** | When you press **Zoom** |
218	| **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:** | When you press **Follow** |
219	| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | **Follow:** and **Where Empty:**, shared with Follow Subject | When you press **Make** |
220	| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | **Rate:**, **Shortest stretch:** and **Keep pitch** | When you press **Apply** |
221	| **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** | **Minimum shot:**, **Cut:**, **Crosstalk:** and **Ignore bleed:** | When you press **Switch** |
222	| The **Normalize** row of the [Volume section](/audio/normalize/) | Its mode, **Peak** or **Loudness**, and its target in LUFS | As you change each one |
223	| The Document tab's **Canvas** section | **Resize clips proportionally**, used with your next [canvas-size](/projects/canvas-size/) change | As you tick it |
224	
225	Where a choice is saved on a press, cancelling the sheet saves nothing.
226	
227	The first time you export, the sheet opens on H.264 at document size. Named export presets are kept in a file, so they're on [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/).
228	
229	**Follow:** can read differently in the two sheets that share it. If Make Vertical Version last used **Speaker**, it opens on **Speaker** again, and Follow Subject, which has no such choice, opens on **Subject**.
230	
231	**Resize clips proportionally** is a preference, not an edit, so undo doesn't reach it.
232	
233	No agent tool reads any of these. An agent's call uses the values it passes, or the tool's own defaults.
234	
235	## Recorder panel
236	
237	**File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) reopens on your last choices, each saved as you change it.
238	
239	| Group | What's remembered |
240	| --- | --- |
241	| Source | The display in **Source:**, **Include Frame Job windows** |
242	| Camera | **Camera:** and **Format:**, **Record the camera too**, **Layout:**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands** |
243	| Sound | **Microphone:**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **System Audio:** |
244	| Pointer and keys | **Cursor:**, **Show Clicks:**, **Record shortcuts** |
245	| When it lands | **Zoom in on clicks**, **Show shortcuts**, **Speed up typing** |
246	| Picture | **Rate:**, **Size:** |
247	
248	Until you change them, **Record the camera too**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **Record shortcuts** and **Speed up typing** are off, **Zoom in on clicks** and **Show shortcuts** are on, **Layout:** is **Corner**, and **Cursor:** follows the default for the source.
249	
250	A few things don't last between launches:
251	
252	- **Record Into:** is never remembered.
253	- A picked window, **Microphone Only** and **Camera** as the **Source:** row last for the session only. The camera you chose is remembered, even though the row isn't.
254	
255	See [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
256	
257	## Inspector sections
258	
259	Whether each inspector section is collapsed or expanded is remembered, section by section, in every window. Only a click on a section's header is remembered.
260	
261	A section you've never clicked opens in its default state. Transform, a text or shape's main section, a graphic's Properties, and the sections of the Media and Document tabs start open, and most others start closed. If that would leave a Clip tab with every section shut, the first one you've never clicked opens. See [The inspector](/getting-started/inspector/).
262	
263	## Permission questions
264	
265	macOS shows its Screen Recording prompt only once, so Frame Job remembers that it has already asked. A later press of **Record** without the permission opens the Screen Recording pane of System Settings instead of the prompt. Input Monitoring, which **Record shortcuts** needs, is remembered the same way. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
266	
267	## Convert on import
268	
269	When macOS can't open a file and Frame Job offers to repackage or convert it, ticking **Do this automatically from now on** in that alert remembers your answer:
270	
271	- Ticked with **Convert** or **Repackage**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
272	- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails.
273	
274	There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:
275	
276	```sh
277	defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
278	```
279	
280	See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).
281	
282	## Update checks
283	
284	The downloaded copy of Frame Job remembers your answer to whether it should check for updates automatically, and when it last checked. See [Updates](/getting-started/updates/).
285	
286	## What is not remembered
287	
288	**View ▸ Preview Window**, **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection**, **Show SDR Version**, **Show Subjects**, **Scopes** and **Loudness Meter** all start off in each new window. None of them changes an export.
289	
290	Nothing about the scopes is kept: a new window starts with Waveform over Vectorscope. The Loudness Meter starts off and empty.
291	
292	Timeline zoom, Loop, the playhead, the selection and the in/out range aren't remembered between launches.
293	
294	Some rows in the sheets above are never remembered, even though the rows around them are:
295	
296	- **Zoom:** in Follow Subject and Make Vertical Version
297	- **Make a copy** in Make Vertical Version
298	- **Zoom on typing** in Auto Zoom
299	- **Record Into:** in the recorder panel
300	- **Dynamic Range** in Export
301	- **Minimum shot:** in Switch by Speaker when the cameras share one microphone
302	
303	**Clip ▸ Match Audio…** remembers none of its choices.
304	
305	## Where these are kept
306	
307	All of these live in macOS's preferences for Frame Job, the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` domain. So do the model, the region, the compaction and clearing settings, and **Background render** from the Settings window. Your API keys are never stored there.
308
